Add beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half. Strain the jus through a fine-mesh sieve. Return to clean saucepan. Add half of the tarragon sprigs. Simmer for 5 minutes. Remove tarragon. Keep warm.

Prepare the Celeriac Purée: Peel celeriac. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place celeriac in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain celeriac thoroughly. Return to hot pan to dry excess moisture. Pass celeriac through a food mill or mash well. Add 50 grams butter and heavy cream. Blend with an immersion blender until silky smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare the King Oyster Mushrooms: Wipe mushrooms clean. Slice mushrooms into 1 cm thick rounds or batons. Heat 10 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms. Sear until golden brown and tender, about 3-4 minutes per side. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Prepare the Beef Tenderloin: Pat beef dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 10 ml olive oil and 50 grams butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until butter foams. Carefully place beef tenderloin in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, turning to brown all surfaces. Baste with butter during cooking. Remove beef from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 10 minutes.

Plate the Dish: Slice beef tenderloin into 4 equal thick chunks. Place a quenelle or elegant swoosh of celeriac purée slightly off-center on each plate. Arrange one beef tenderloin chunk beside the purée. Place 2-3 pieces of roasted king oyster mushroom near the beef. Spoon a generous pool of tarragon jus around the beef and purée. Garnish with a small, fresh tarragon sprig on the beef or purée.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Rôti aux Pommes de Terre et Champignons
recipes.visual_description: Crispy skin on roasted chicken thigh, cooked to a golden-brown, rests centrally on a clean white round porcelain plate. Beside it, golden-brown roasted potato wedges are artfully arranged, their edges slightly crisped. A generous portion of pan-seared cremini mushrooms, retaining their earthy color and plump texture, is nestled alongside. A light, glossy pan jus is drizzled sparingly around the chicken and potatoes. The dish is garnished with vibrant green, freshly torn basil leaves, adding a pop of color and aromatic freshness. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting, with appropriate negative space. The setting features a rustic wooden table, a folded white linen napkin, and standard silver flatware, all under soft, natural lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges. Toss with 30ml olive oil, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 20 minutes.
While potatoes roast, heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden and crispy, about 8 minutes. Flip and sear for 2 minutes.
Transfer skillet with chicken to oven alongside potatoes. Continue roasting both for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Mince garlic. Slice mushrooms 0.5cm thick.

When chicken and potatoes are nearly done, heat remaining 15ml olive oil and butter in a separate skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and minced garlic. Sauté until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove chicken from skillet. Deglaze skillet with chicken broth, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Plate each serving with one roasted chicken thigh, a portion of crispy potato wedges, and sautéed mushrooms. Drizzle with pan jus. Garnish with fresh torn basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Rosemary-Thyme Roasted Potatoes and Garlic Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared beef medallion, showcasing a rich, dark brown crust, is the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a generous portion of golden-brown roasted potato chunks, each approximately 2 cm, display a crispy exterior and tender interior, flecked with green rosemary and thyme. Nestled alongside the beef and potatoes are earthy sautéed mushrooms, some whole, others sliced to 1 cm, glistening with garlic and butter. A fresh sprig of thyme rests delicately on the beef as a garnish. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, allowing each component to stand out. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic European-style flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and vibrant, natural colors of the dish, creating an inviting, casual dining presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Place in a large bowl.
Add 30 ml olive oil, 2 sprigs fresh rosemary, 2 sprigs fresh thyme, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper to potatoes. Toss to coat.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and golden.
While potatoes roast, clean mushrooms. Slice thick mushrooms into 1 cm slices. Keep smaller mushrooms whole.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves and leaves from 1 sprig fresh thyme to mushrooms. Sauté for 1 minute more. Season with 2g salt and 1g black pepper. Set aside.
Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with 5g salt and 2g black pepper on all sides.
Heat a heavy-bottomed frying pan or cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Add 15 ml olive oil.
Carefully place beef medallions in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness.
During the last 2 minutes of cooking, add 30g unsalted butter and 1 sprig fresh thyme to the pan. Tilt the pan and spoon melted butter over the beef repeatedly.
Remove beef from pan. Place on a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 5-7 minutes.
To serve, divide roasted potatoes and sautéed mushrooms among 4 plates. Place one beef medallion on each plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Braciole with Rustic Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef Braciole is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Two to three thick cross-sections of the rolled, braised beef are nestled in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce. The braciole pieces reveal the savory breadcrumb and herb filling. The beef is dark golden-brown from searing, contrasting with the vibrant red sauce. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the top as a garnish. A light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese adds a touch of white. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, capturing natural, even lighting. A single silver fork and knife are placed beside the plate, and a crisp white cotton napkin is folded nearby, completing a modern bistro setting with an authentic Italian feel. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, keeping the focus entirely on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of al dente pasta, such as rigatoni or paccheri, to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Pecorino Romano cheese at the table.

ingredients.name: Beef Top Round or Sirloin, thinly sliced

instructions: Pound beef slices to 5 mm thickness. Use a meat mallet.
Prepare filling: Combine breadcrumbs, minced garlic, grated Parmesan, chopped parsley, chopped basil, egg, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Mix well.
Spread filling evenly over each beef slice. Leave a small border.
Roll each beef slice tightly. Secure with kitchen twine or toothpicks.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear braciole until golden brown on all sides. Remove braciole from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add remaining minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared braciole to the pot. Ensure braciole is mostly submerged in sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot. Simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours. Beef should be fork-tender.
Remove braciole from sauce. Carefully remove twine or toothpicks.
Slice braciole into thick cross-sections before serving.
Serve braciole with rustic tomato sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Acorn Squash, Gruyere Cream, Ketchup Spheres, Compressed Cucumber
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a sophisticated, minimalist composition on a pristine white bone china plate. A golden-brown roasted acorn squash wedge, caramelized and tender, anchors the plate. Adjacent, a silken, pale ivory Gruyere cream forms an organic pool. Artfully arranged are translucent, emerald-green compressed cucumber rounds, providing crisp contrast. Scattered are 3-5 glistening, ruby-red ketchup spheres, each a perfect orb, hinting at concentrated flavor. A delicate sprig of micro cilantro adds vibrant green. Abundant negative space emphasizes precise placement. The setting is a luxurious, matte grey marble surface, with a folded white linen napkin and minimalist silver flatware. Dramatic, soft lighting enhances textures and depth.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve squash, scoop out seeds. Cut each half into two wedges. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Place cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast 30-40 minutes until tender and caramelized.

Combine milk and cream in a saucepan. Heat gently. Add grated Gruyere. Stir until melted and smooth. Bring to a simmer. Whisk in cornstarch slurry. Cook, stirring, until thickened to a light cream consistency. Season with nutmeg and salt. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.
For Ketchup Spheres: In a tall container, whisk sodium alginate into 500ml distilled water using an immersion blender. Let stand at least 2 hours to remove air bubbles. This is the alginate bath.
In a separate bowl, whisk calcium lactate gluconate into ketchup until fully dissolved.

Using a syringe or squeeze bottle, carefully drop small amounts of ketchup mixture into the alginate bath. Let spheres form 1-2 minutes. Gently remove with a slotted spoon. Rinse spheres immediately in clean water. Store in a small amount of fresh water.

Peel cucumber. Slice into very thin rounds (1-2mm) using a mandoline. In a bowl, combine rice vinegar, water, sugar, and salt. Add cucumber slices. Vacuum seal the bag. If no vacuum sealer, press firmly to remove air and let marinate 30 minutes, pressing occasionally.

On each plate, place a roasted acorn squash wedge. Spoon a generous pool of Gruyere cream next to the squash. Arrange a few compressed cucumber slices artfully. Carefully place 3-5 ketchup spheres around the squash and cream. Garnish with a small sprig of micro cilantro or dill. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the alginate bath is completely free of air bubbles for perfect spheres.
The Gruyere cream should be light and smooth, not heavy.
Adjust seasoning for all components to balance flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions, Whipped Bone Marrow Cream, Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an exquisite, matte white bone china plate, centered on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. Ample negative space surrounds the components. A single, thick-cut, seared beef medallion, approximately 4cm high with a deeply caramelized crust and a vibrant pink medium-rare interior, anchors the composition. Adjacent to the beef, an organically shaped, generous dollop of pale ivory whipped bone marrow cream sits delicately. The cream's smooth, airy texture contrasts with the beef's robust surface. A precise scattering of finely chopped, bright green gremolata—a mixture of fresh parsley, vibrant lemon zest, and micro-minced garlic—is artfully placed over the cream and subtly touches the beef, providing a pop of color and freshness. The composition is asymmetrical, natural, and elegant, emphasizing the quality of ingredients and precise execution. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting textures. A perfectly folded white linen napkin sits discreetly nearby.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast marrow bones on a baking sheet for 15-20 minutes, until marrow is soft. Scoop marrow into a small heatproof bowl. Discard bones.

Heat heavy cream in a small saucepan until just simmering. Add hot cream to the bowl with roasted marrow. Blend immediately with an immersion blender until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill cream mixture in a metal bowl over an ice bath. Once cold, whip with a whisk or electric mixer until light and aerated. Season with salt and pepper.
Finely chop parsley. Finely grate lemon zest. Mince garlic very finely. Combine parsley, lemon zest, and garlic in a small bowl.

Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat until shimmering. Sear beef medallions for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, creating a deep brown crust. Adjust time for desired doneness. Remove beef from skillet. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Place one seared beef medallion slightly off-center on each plate. Place a generous dollop of whipped bone marrow cream next to the beef. Sprinkle a pinch of gremolata over the cream and beef. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, matte-finished ceramic bowl on a dark wood table. The base is a vibrant, reddish-orange long-grain rice, cooked to a moist, free-flowing consistency. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs with crispy skin rest atop the rice. The chicken is not sliced. Accompanying the chicken are charred tomato wedges and small cubes of sautéed onion mixed within the grains. Garnishes include fresh, bright green cilantro leaves and thin wedges of lime placed on the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textural contrast between the crispy chicken skin and the soft rice. A linen napkin and a heavy silver fork sit beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with pickled red onions
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from guajillo and arbol chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chilies in 200ml hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend soaked chilies, tomatoes, half the onion, and garlic until smooth.
Pat chicken dry and season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes then remove from pot.
Add rice and remaining onion to the pot.
Toast rice for 3 minutes until opaque and slightly golden.
Pour blended chili-tomato mixture into the rice.
Cook for 5 minutes while stirring until sauce thickens.
Add chicken stock and return chicken to the pot.
Reduce heat to low and cover with a tight lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs to ensure the meat remains juicy during simmering
Do not over-toast the dried chilies as they can turn bitter
The rice should be moist and flavorful, absorbing all the chili-tomato broth

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Strawberry-Balsamic Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared duck breast is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish. The golden-skinned duck breast, sliced into thick pieces, is compactly arranged; its crisp skin contrasts with the succulent pink interior. Beside it, a rectangle of creamy, golden-brown potato dauphinoise, lightly gratinéed. A small pile of roasted carrot batons, caramelized and vibrant orange, adds color. A glossy, deep ruby-red strawberry-balsamic glaze, with softened red onion and strawberry pieces, is artfully spooned over the duck and around the plate. Fresh chopped parsley garnishes the dish. Metal flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are beside the plate, suggesting a refined restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with standard European flatware.
Pair with a light-bodied red wine, such as Pinot Noir.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium, peeled, cut into 5cm thick batons

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.quantity: 4 cloves, minced (2 for dauphinoise, 2 for glaze)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Prepare Potato Dauphinoise: In a medium bowl, combine thinly sliced potatoes, 2 minced garlic cloves, heavy cream, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Butter a small oven-safe gratin dish (approx. 20x15cm). Layer potato mixture evenly. Sprinkle with grated Gruyère cheese.
Bake dauphinoise for 45-50 minutes, or until golden brown and potatoes are tender.
Prepare Roasted Carrots: Toss carrot batons with olive oil, salt, pepper, and 2 sprigs of thyme on a baking sheet.
Roast carrots for 25-30 minutes, or until tender-crisp and lightly caramelized.
Prepare Strawberry-Balsamic Glaze: In a small saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add thinly sliced red onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add quartered strawberries, balsamic vinegar, chicken stock, and 2 sprigs of thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens to a glaze consistency. Remove thyme sprigs. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare Duck Breast: Pat duck breasts dry. Season skin and flesh generously with salt and pepper.
Place duck breasts, skin-side down, in a cold oven-safe skillet. Turn heat to medium-low.
Cook duck skin-side down for 8-12 minutes, rendering fat slowly, until skin is golden brown and crispy. Pour off excess fat periodically.
Flip duck breasts. Cook flesh-side down for 3-4 minutes.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 6-8 minutes for medium-rare (internal temperature 57-60°C). Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove duck from oven. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes before slicing into thick pieces.
To Serve: Place a portion of potato dauphinoise on a plate. Arrange roasted carrots beside it.
Place sliced duck breast pieces beside the vegetables.
Spoon strawberry-balsamic glaze generously over the duck and around the plate.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork with Grapefruit and Dill
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of succulent braised pork chunks, approximately 4-5 cm, rests in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The pork is bathed in a rich, earthy red-brown sauce, thick and clinging. Fresh, bright green dill sprigs are generously scattered over the pork and sauce, providing a vibrant contrast. Alongside, a few plump, pink grapefruit segments are casually arranged, adding a pop of color and fresh acidity. The overall plating is natural and inviting, fitting for a comforting home-cooked meal. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, illuminated by warm, natural light. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard metal fork complete the homely setting, emphasizing a relaxed, family dining atmosphere. The scene is uncluttered, focusing on the hearty, comforting dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad

ingredients.name: Grapefruit
ingredients.quantity: 1 large (zest and juice of half, segments of other half)

instructions: Pat pork chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks until well browned on all sides. Remove pork from the pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with dark rum, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Cook until rum mostly evaporates.
Stir in unsweetened cocoa powder until dissolved.
Return pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and broth.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot tightly.
Braise for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until pork is very tender.
Remove the lid. Simmer for 15-20 minutes to allow the sauce to thicken slightly.
Stir in the grapefruit zest and half of the chopped fresh dill.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh grapefruit segments and remaining fresh dill. Sprinkle with a tiny amount of toasted coconut flakes, if desired.
notes: The cocoa powder adds depth and richness to the sauce, not a chocolate flavor.
The rum cooks off, leaving only a subtle aromatic note.
Toasted coconut flakes are an optional garnish for texture; use sparingly to maintain Mediterranean focus.

recipes.recipe_name: Stir-fried Pork with Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Stir-fried Pork with Bell Peppers is presented on a round, white ceramic plate, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Thin strips of savory pork are mixed with vibrant red, yellow, and green bell pepper strips, creating a colorful and appealing mound in the center. The ingredients are casually arranged, some touching, some slightly overlapping, reflecting a homely plating style. The pork pieces are tender and coated in a glossy, savory brown sauce. Bell peppers retain a slight crispness, their natural colors prominent. A sprinkle of fresh green onion slices garnishes the top. A simple white rice bowl filled with steamed white rice and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks are placed beside the plate, completing the authentic Chinese home meal setting. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting, comfort-food appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served immediately with steamed white rice
Eaten family style, sharing from a main dish onto individual rice bowls
Use chopsticks
instructions: Cut pork into thin strips. Marinate pork with 15 ml light soy sauce, 15 ml Shaoxing rice wine, 10 g cornstarch, and 5 ml sesame oil for 15 minutes.
Cut bell peppers into strips. Mince garlic and ginger. Slice green onions.
Combine 30 ml light soy sauce, 5 ml dark soy sauce, 15 ml Shaoxing rice wine, sugar, white pepper, 60 ml water or chicken stock, and 5 g cornstarch in a small bowl. Whisk well.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat until smoking.
Add marinated pork. Stir-fry quickly until pork is just cooked through and lightly browned. Remove pork from wok.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to wok. Add minced garlic and ginger. Stir-fry for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add bell pepper strips to wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Return cooked pork to wok. Pour in prepared stir-fry sauce.
Stir constantly until sauce thickens and coats pork and vegetables.
Transfer to a serving plate. Garnish with sliced green onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Bavette with Fermented Tomato Paste and Onion Confit
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a creamy beige handcrafted ceramic plate, featuring a minimalist, unforced composition. A bed of glossy, golden-brown onion confit forms an organic base. Adjacent are two thick, irregularly cut chunks of seared beef bavette, showing a caramelized crust and reddish-pink interior. A vibrant crimson dollop of fermented tomato paste, with natural texture, provides a contrasting pop of color. Crumbled fresh goat cheese, stark white and irregular, is scattered over the beef and confit. A small sprig of fresh thyme or oregano provides a subtle green accent. Ample white space highlights the ingredients' natural beauty. The setting includes a light bamboo surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft natural lighting. A clean background with subtle greenery enhances the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Paste (start 5-7 days in advance):
Wash tomatoes. Quarter them.
Blend tomatoes into a coarse puree.
Strain puree through a fine-mesh sieve, collecting pulp. Discard excess liquid and seeds.
Combine tomato pulp with 15g sea salt and starter culture in a clean jar. Mix well.
Ensure pulp is fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Cover jar with an airlock lid or burp daily.
Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 5-7 days, or until tangy. Store in refrigerator.
Prepare Onion Confit:
Peel and thinly slice onions. Save onion skins for stock.
Peel and smash garlic cloves.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, combine sliced onions, garlic, thyme, rosemary, and 150ml olive oil.
Cook over very low heat for 1.5-2 hours, stirring occasionally. Onions should be very soft and translucent. Do not brown.
Remove herbs and garlic. Store confit in an airtight container with oil.
Prepare Beef:
Pat beef bavette dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef bavette for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness.
Remove beef from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes.
Plate Dish:
Place a spoonful of onion confit in the center of each plate.
Slice beef against the grain into thick chunks. Place 1-2 chunks next to the confit.
Spoon a dollop of fermented tomato paste onto the plate.
Crumble fresh goat cheese over the beef and confit.
Garnish with a small fresh herb sprig.
notes: For a zero-waste approach, use beef trimmings for stock or rendered fat for cooking.
Onion skins and root ends can be saved for vegetable stock.
The fermentation process can be adjusted based on desired tanginess.
This dish champions local, seasonal ingredients and minimises waste through preservation techniques.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken Thighs with Roasted Potatoes, Tomatoes, and Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of baked chicken is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A whole, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh rests prominently. Surrounding the chicken are roasted potato chunks and vibrant orange carrot rounds, tender and slightly caramelized. Halved, burst cherry tomatoes add pops of bright red and juiciness among the vegetables. Thinly sliced, roasted garlic cloves are visible throughout. A generous sprinkle of melted, lightly golden Parmesan cheese covers the chicken and vegetables. The dish is garnished with fresh, finely chopped green parsley, adding a vibrant contrast. The arrangement is natural and rustic, with elements distributed evenly without overcrowding. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food. The background suggests a modern bistro setting, minimal and unobtrusive.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 3 medium, peeled, cut into 2 cm thick rounds

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine potato chunks, carrot rounds, halved cherry tomatoes, and sliced garlic.
Drizzle with olive oil. Add oregano, salt, and black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 20 minutes.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Remove tray from oven. Push vegetables to one side. Place seasoned chicken thighs on the empty side of the tray.
Return to oven. Roast for another 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and vegetables are tender.
Remove tray. Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over chicken and vegetables.
Return to oven for 5 minutes, until cheese is melted and lightly golden.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Pork Shoulder with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of beer-braised pork shoulder rests on a sturdy, cream-colored ceramic plate. The pork, cut into large, irregular chunks, boasts a deep, rich mahogany-brown crust from searing and a tender, falling-apart texture from braising. It's enveloped in a glossy, thick, dark amber sauce, studded with soft, browned quartered potatoes. A few vibrant green fresh thyme sprigs are scattered casually over the top. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife are placed beside the dish, emphasizing its homely, unpretentious comfort.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Cut pork shoulder into 5-7 cm large chunks. Pat dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks until deeply browned on all sides. Do this in batches to avoid overcrowding. Remove pork and set aside.
Add diced onion, chopped carrots, and chopped celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon.
Return the seared pork chunks to the pot. Add chicken or beef broth and fresh thyme sprigs. Ensure liquid mostly covers the pork.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Cover the pot tightly with a lid.
Transfer the Dutch oven to the preheated oven. Braise for 2 hours.
Add the quartered potatoes to the pot. Stir gently. Continue braising for another 1 hour, or until the pork is fork-tender and easily pulls apart.
Remove the pot from the oven. Carefully remove the pork chunks and set aside to rest for 10 minutes. Discard thyme sprigs.
If the sauce is too thin, place the pot on the stovetop over medium-high heat. Simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens to your desired consistency.
Serve the tender pork chunks and potatoes generously coated with the rich braising sauce.
notes: This dish tastes even better the next day, making it excellent for meal preparation.
Any dark or amber ale will work well for this recipe; avoid overly hoppy or bitter beers.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage and Eggplant Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Sausage and Eggplant Pasta is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The rigatoni pasta is coated in a rich, rustic deep red tomato sauce. Visible within the sauce are irregular chunks of browned Italian sausage and tender, slightly caramelized 2cm eggplant cubes. Fresh, vibrant green torn basil leaves are scattered throughout, providing a striking color contrast. A generous dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese crowns the dish. The composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth.
instructions: Cut eggplant into 2cm cubes. Place in colander. Sprinkle with salt. Let sit 30 minutes. Pat dry with paper towels.
Heat 30ml olive oil in large pot over medium-high heat. Add sausage. Break apart with spoon. Cook until browned and no pink remains. Remove sausage from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to pot. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add eggplant cubes to pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Return cooked sausage to pot. Add crushed tomatoes and red pepper flakes. Stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring sauce to simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 20 minutes. Stir occasionally.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta to sauce. Add half of the fresh basil leaves, torn. Add 125ml reserved pasta water. Toss well to combine.
Continue to cook 2 minutes. Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency. Sauce should coat pasta.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Open-Faced Ham and Cheese Toasts
recipes.visual_description: The open-faced ham and cheese toasts are presented on a rustic, well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen light. Two toasts are arranged side-by-side on a simple, everyday ceramic plate with natural imperfections. Each toast features a base of golden-brown, lightly buttered bread. Generous, warm pieces of cooked ham are layered over the bread, not fanned, with a melted, bubbling layer of golden-yellow cheddar cheese blanketing them. The cheese shows slight browning at the edges, indicating its comforting warmth. On top of the melted cheese and ham, fresh, vibrant red tomato slices are casually placed, or small, bright red diced tomato pieces are scattered. A generous dollop of creamy white sour cream sits atop the tomatoes, adding a cool, soft contrast. A light sprinkle of finely chopped green chives provides a touch of fresh color. The overall presentation is unpretentious and hearty, reflecting a comforting, homestyle snack. The focus is on the natural textures and inviting colors of the ingredients, with ample negative space around the plate.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet.
Brush each bread slice lightly with melted butter.
Cut ham into rustic, bite-sized pieces. Distribute ham evenly over each bread slice.
Sprinkle shredded cheese generously over the ham.
Bake for 8-12 minutes. Cheese should be melted and bubbling, and bread edges lightly golden.
While toasts bake, slice tomatoes into thin rounds or dice them into small cubes.
Remove toasts from oven. Arrange on serving plates or a shared board.
Top each toast with fresh tomato slices or diced tomato.
Dollop sour cream generously over the tomato.
Garnish with chopped chives and a grind of black pepper, if desired.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef and Onion Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty Spicy Beef and Onion Stew fills a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a matte finish. The stew is rich mahogany brown, featuring tender, dark brown beef chunks. Roughly chopped, translucent onion pieces and specks of red chili flakes are visible. The beef, cut into substantial cubes, appears fork-tender. A scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the top. The bowl rests on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table, revealing its grain. A simple, silver fork and spoon are casually placed. A folded, cream-colored linen napkin rests beside the bowl. Warm kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere. The background suggests a lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread for dipping
Serve over mashed potatoes or egg noodles
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown beef cubes in batches until seared on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add chopped onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and red chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes and beef broth.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef Chili with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Spicy Beef Chili with Roasted Potatoes is presented in a clean, wide white ceramic bowl. The chili, a rich, deep red-brown, is mounded generously on one side, showcasing visible chunks of ground beef, diced onions, and quartered mushrooms. Its surface has a slight sheen from the sauce. Beside the chili, golden-brown roasted potato wedges are arranged organically, some displaying slightly crispy, caramelized edges. Bright green peas are scattered lightly over the chili and around the potatoes, adding a vibrant pop of color and freshness. A small cluster of fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves garnishes the chili, providing a final touch of color and aroma. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, focusing attention entirely on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with shredded cheddar cheese
Offer a dollop of sour cream or plain Greek yogurt
Accompany with warm cornbread or tortilla chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges or chunks. Toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, and 0.5 teaspoon black pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and golden brown, flipping halfway.

While potatoes roast, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add ground beef. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat. Remove beef from pot and set aside.

Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Return cooked beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, to allow flavors to meld.
Stir in chopped dark chocolate until melted and fully incorporated. Season chili with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in green peas. Cook for 2-3 minutes, until peas are heated through.
Serve hot chili alongside roasted potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality ground beef and high-cacao dark chocolate. The chocolate enhances depth, not sweetness.
Adjust chili powder and add fresh chopped jalapeño or serrano peppers for increased heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Prosciutto and Fontina Stuffed Chicken with Sage Butter Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, pan-seared and baked chicken breast, generously stuffed, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken showcases a rich, even crust. A glistening, amber sage butter sauce is artfully drizzled over and around the chicken. Fresh, vibrant green sage leaves are thoughtfully placed atop the chicken as an aromatic garnish. Alongside, roasted asparagus spears, retaining their bright green color and slight char, provide complementary texture and visual balance. The plating is clean, with moderate negative space. The scene is set on a simple light wooden table, illuminated by soft, natural lighting. A folded white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware complete the modern bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a light green salad or crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Butterfly each chicken breast. Place between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 0.5 cm thickness.
Season chicken lightly with salt and pepper.
Place two slices of prosciutto on each pounded chicken breast. Top with sliced Fontina cheese.
Carefully roll each chicken breast tightly. Secure with toothpicks if needed.
Dredge each rolled chicken breast lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken rolls 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to preheated oven.
Bake chicken 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
While chicken bakes, prepare asparagus. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast alongside chicken for the last 10-12 minutes.
For the sauce, melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add fresh sage leaves. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Simmer 1 minute. Add chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Remove toothpicks from chicken. Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick chunks. Do not fan.
Serve chicken chunks with roasted asparagus. Spoon sage butter sauce generously over chicken and asparagus.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Resting the chicken before slicing helps retain juices.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Ham and Cheese Toasties with Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A generous platter of golden-brown ham and cheese toastie halves, each diagonally sliced, is presented on a well-used wooden cutting board. The bread, perfectly toasted, boasts a crisp, buttery exterior with a rich, inviting hue. Inside, layers of melted, gooey cheddar cheese embrace tender, thinly sliced ham and vibrant red tomato rounds. A slight ooze of cheese from the edges highlights the comforting warmth. The toasties are arranged casually, slightly overlapping, inviting guests to grab a piece. Natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the authentic textures and inviting colors. The setting is a homely family kitchen table, complete with simple ceramic plates and a casually placed, folded cloth napkin, evoking a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere perfect for a comforting snack.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of ketchup or mustard for dipping.
Accompany with pickle spears.

ingredients.name: Slices of white or sourdough bread
Cheddar or Gruyere cheese, sliced or grated

instructions: Lightly butter one side of each of the 8 bread slices.
Heat a large frying pan or griddle over medium heat.
Place 4 bread slices, butter-side down, in the hot pan.
On each slice, layer approximately 50g of cheese.
Add 50g of ham over the cheese.
Arrange a few thin tomato slices over the ham. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Top with another 50g of cheese.
Place the remaining 4 bread slices, butter-side up, on top of the cheese.
Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until bread is golden brown and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Press down gently with a spatula during cooking to ensure even browning and melting.
Remove from pan.
Slice each toastie diagonally into two triangles.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Paella Mixta with Chicken and Beef
recipes.visual_description: The Paella Mixta is presented in a wide, shallow white bowl, showcasing a vibrant composition. Golden saffron-infused Bomba rice forms the base, with visible, distinct grains. Scattered throughout are browned, rustic 2-3 cm cubes of seared chicken and beef, their edges slightly caramelized. Bright green peas and finely diced orange carrots add pops of color and texture. A rich, reddish hue from the tomato and smoked paprika base coats the ingredients. The surface shows a light crispness, hinting at the desired 'socarrat' at the bottom. The dish is garnished simply with fresh, finely chopped parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge positioned to the side. The overall appearance is abundant and inviting, reflecting traditional Spanish hospitality, with moderate negative space on the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the paella pan for a communal experience.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the pan juices.
Serve with aioli (garlic mayonnaise) on the side.
Accompany with a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Red chili, mild (e.g., Fresno or small bell pepper)

instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm cubes. Dice beef into similar 2-3 cm cubes.
Finely dice the carrot. Mince the onion. Mince the garlic. Thinly slice the mild red chili.
Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown on all sides. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add beef cubes to the same pan. Sear until browned. Remove beef from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced onion and finely diced carrot to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and smoked paprika. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and darkens, about 5 minutes.
Return seared chicken and beef to the pan. Stir in the rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the rice grains with the pan mixture.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Distribute all ingredients evenly across the pan. Do not stir from this point onward.

Bring the liquid to a simmer. Cook uncovered over medium heat for 15-18 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is al dente. Listen for a crackling sound, indicating the 'socarrat' is forming at the bottom.
Scatter green peas evenly over the rice. Cover the pan loosely with foil. Remove from heat. Let the paella rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh, finely chopped parsley and lemon wedges. Serve directly from the pan or portion into individual bowls.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the broth is added; this allows the 'socarrat' (crispy rice crust) to form at the bottom.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Ham and Cheese Toasties
recipes.visual_description: Four hearty ham and cheese toasties, cut diagonally, reveal warm, melted cheddar cheese stretching from golden-brown, pan-fried bread. The bread is crisped and buttered, showing slight char marks. Thinly sliced cooked ham is nestled beneath the cheese. The toasties are arranged casually on a large, well-used wooden cutting board, halves slightly overlapping. Alongside, thick-cut tomato rounds and cucumber half-moons are scattered naturally, their vibrant red and green colors contrasting with the warm tones. Fresh parsley leaves are roughly chopped and sprinkled over the vegetables. The scene is set on a simple, worn wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, soft overhead lighting. Everyday ceramic plates are stacked nearby. A casually draped striped tea towel adds a homely touch. Portions are substantial, reflecting comfort food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a simple side salad.
Often accompanied by ketchup or a mild mustard.

ingredients.name: Cheddar cheese, grated or thinly sliced

instructions: Butter one side of each bread slice.
Spread a thin layer of Dijon mustard on the unbuttered side of 4 bread slices, if using.
Place a generous layer of thinly sliced cooked ham on the mustard-spread side (or plain side if no mustard) of the 4 bread slices.
Top the ham with a generous layer of grated or thinly sliced cheddar cheese.
Place the remaining 4 bread slices on top, buttered side facing out.
Heat a large frying pan or griddle over medium heat.
Place the toasties in the hot pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cheese is melted.
While toasties cook, slice tomatoes and cucumber into thick rounds or half-moons. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove toasties from pan. Cut each toastie in half diagonally.
Serve hot with fresh thick-cut tomato and cucumber slices on the side.
notes: Use good quality bread for best results.
Adjust cheese and ham quantities to preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper Salad with Crispy Garlic-Parmesan Breadcrumbs
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, homely salad served on a rustic ceramic plate. Roasted bell pepper strips, in warm shades of red, yellow, and orange, are casually arranged amidst vibrant green mixed salad leaves. Thin slices of red onion are scattered throughout. Small, golden-brown crispy chicken cubes are nestled among the vegetables. The dish is topped generously with golden, textured garlic-Parmesan breadcrumbs and a scattering of fresh green chopped parsley. The dressing lightly coats the ingredients, adding a subtle sheen. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen light. A simple cloth napkin and everyday flatware are casually placed beside the plate. Portions are modest and approachable, filling the plate without overcrowding.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve bell peppers. Remove seeds. Slice into 2cm strips. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, pepper. Spread on baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly charred.

Dice chicken breast into 1cm cubes. Season with salt, pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring, until golden and cooked through (75°C internal temp). Remove chicken. Set aside.

In same skillet, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Mince garlic cloves. Add garlic and breadcrumbs to skillet. Toast over medium heat 3-5 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden brown. Remove from heat. Stir in Parmesan cheese.
For dressing: In small bowl, whisk 15ml olive oil, lemon juice, salt, pepper.
In large bowl, combine roasted bell peppers, mixed salad greens, and thinly sliced red onion. Add crispy chicken cubes.
Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine.
Top with crispy garlic-Parmesan breadcrumbs and fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli Rabe and Pasta Salad with Crispy Salami
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of warm pasta salad fills a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl, its off-white surface showing slight imperfections. Orecchiette pasta, cooked al dente, has a soft golden hue, its cup-like shape cradling bits of garlic and red pepper flakes. Vibrant green, tender florets and chopped stems of sautéed broccoli rabe are unevenly mixed throughout, providing a pleasant contrast. Small, irregularly diced pieces of crispy salami are scattered, adding deep reddish-brown highlights and a textural crunch. The salad is lightly coated in a glistening olive oil and red wine vinegar dressing, allowing the natural colors of the ingredients to shine. A few fresh oregano leaves are casually sprinkled on top. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table, with warm, inviting light illuminating the scene. A simple, sturdy fork is placed beside the bowl, suggesting a comforting, home-cooked meal.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add orecchiette pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 60ml pasta water.
While pasta cooks, wash broccoli rabe. Trim tough ends. Chop stems into 2cm pieces. Separate florets.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced salami. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove salami with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in skillet.
Add broccoli rabe to the skillet with salami fat. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Combine drained pasta, sautéed broccoli rabe, crispy salami, and dressing in a large bowl. Toss well. Add reserved pasta water if needed for moisture.
Serve warm. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Tomato-Mushroom Pasta and Lemon Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Tomato-Mushroom Pasta and Lemon Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy pasta, featuring penne coated in a light pinkish-orange sauce, forms a neat mound slightly off-center. Visible within the pasta are sautéed golden-brown mushroom slices, vibrant green peas, bright yellow corn kernels, and halved red cherry tomatoes, providing a pleasant color contrast. Resting atop the pasta are two thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast medallions, their surfaces exhibiting a crisp, savory crust. Beside the pasta, a small cluster of roasted potato chunks, their skins slightly crisped and golden, are casually arranged. Each potato piece is irregularly shaped, showing a rustic appeal. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, bright green chopped Italian parsley, adding a final touch of color and freshness. The overall presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and a silver fork and knife. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a light-bodied red wine or sparkling water.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, lemon zest from half lemon, salt, and pepper. Spread on baking sheet. Roast 25-30 minutes until tender and golden.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120 ml of pasta cooking water.

Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 6-8 minutes per side. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest 5 minutes.
In the same skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until golden, about 5 minutes.

Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves and chili flakes to skillet. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add halved cherry tomatoes, green peas, corn kernels, reserved pasta water, and sugar. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and lemon juice from half lemon. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add cooked pasta. Toss to coat thoroughly. Cook 2 minutes to allow sauce to thicken slightly.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions.
Serve pasta immediately, topped with sliced chicken medallions. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or basil. Serve with roasted lemon potatoes on the side.
notes: Adjust chili flakes to desired spice level.
Ensure chicken is fully cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Sautéed Apples and Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared pork chop rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The thick-cut pork chop displays a rich, golden-brown crust from searing. Piled generously beside and slightly overlapping the pork chop are tender, translucent slices of yellow onion and soft, caramelized apple wedges, some with reddish skin visible. A sprinkle of fresh green thyme leaves garnishes the dish, adding a touch of color. The plating is natural and unforced, typical of a home-cooked meal. The dish sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, with a casually folded, simple cloth napkin visible. Lighting is warm and inviting, suggesting a cozy kitchen setting.
instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Core apples. Cut each apple into 8-10 uniform wedges. Peel and slice onion into thin half-moons.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Add pork chops to the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) is reached. Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Remove chops from skillet and set aside on a plate, tented with foil.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add sliced onions and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent.
Add apple wedges and 2 sprigs of thyme to the skillet with the onions. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, stirring gently, until apples are tender-crisp and lightly caramelized.
Pour in apple cider. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let the liquid reduce by half, about 3-4 minutes. Stir in Dijon mustard if using.
Return pork chops to the skillet, nestling them among the apples and onions. Spoon some of the apple-onion mixture over the chops. Cook for 1-2 minutes to warm through.
Remove thyme sprigs. Garnish with fresh thyme leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Potato Salad with Seared Chicken and Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mediterranean Roasted Potato Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Golden-brown roasted potato cubes, halved red cherry tomatoes, small diced green cucumber, thin purple red onion slices, and dark Kalamata olive halves are mixed. Small, tender seared chicken chunks are artfully placed amongst the vegetables. Crumbled white feta and finely chopped fresh green parsley and oregano are scattered over. A light, glossy vinaigrette coats the ingredients, reflecting natural light. The composition is organic, balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface with a cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty bread or pita.
Enjoy as a light lunch or a substantial side dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and quarter new potatoes. Toss with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden. Let cool slightly.

Pat chicken breast dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side until cooked through and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest, then cut into 2 cm chunks.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Dice cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice red onion. Halve Kalamata olives. Crumble feta cheese.
Finely chop fresh parsley and oregano.
For the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together remaining olive oil, red wine vinegar, juice of half a lemon, and minced garlic clove. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine roasted potatoes, seared chicken chunks, cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, sliced red onion, Kalamata olives, and chopped fresh herbs. Gently toss with the dressing.
Carefully transfer salad to a serving plate. Top with crumbled feta cheese. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Garlic Herb Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of roasted garlic herb chicken and potatoes is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, set upon a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, its skin deeply golden and crispy from roasting, is positioned prominently. Adjacent are rustic, roasted potato wedges, their exteriors slightly browned and crisp, revealing a fluffy interior. Interspersed among the potatoes are whole, caramelized garlic cloves, softened and golden. A few fresh sprigs of vibrant green rosemary and thyme are casually scattered over the dish, adding a touch of freshness and color. The dish exhibits natural browning and varied textures—crisp chicken skin, tender chicken meat, soft potatoes, and jammy garlic. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen. A plain linen napkin and basic flatware complete the homely setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in pan juices.

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Wash and pat dry chicken pieces. Season chicken generously with salt, pepper, and paprika if using.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into rustic 2-3 cm wedges or large chunks. Do not peel.
In a large roasting pan, combine chicken, potato wedges, and unpeeled garlic cloves.
Drizzle with olive oil. Add whole rosemary and thyme sprigs.
Toss all ingredients together directly in the pan to coat evenly.
Spread ingredients in a single layer. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 40-50 minutes. Chicken is done when internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Potatoes should be tender and lightly browned.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for food safety.
Potatoes can be cut into smaller pieces for faster cooking, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of golden-brown roasted chicken and potatoes rests on a rustic ceramic plate. Two crispy-skinned chicken thighs are positioned naturally. Thick-cut potato wedges, roasted to a deep golden hue with soft interiors, are scattered around the chicken. Bright red, blistered cherry tomato halves and softened, light brown roasted garlic cloves are interspersed among the potatoes, adding pops of color and texture. Fresh green rosemary and thyme leaves cling to the roasted ingredients. The arrangement is casual, as if scooped directly from a family pan, filling the plate without overcrowding. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Simple, everyday flatware and a casually folded cloth napkin are nearby. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the comforting, homely atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place chicken thighs, potato wedges, halved cherry tomatoes, and smashed garlic cloves in a large roasting pan.
Add rosemary sprigs and thyme sprigs to the pan.
Drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper.
Toss all ingredients together to coat evenly.
Arrange in a single layer in the roasting pan.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast, Blueberry-Thyme Gastrique, Celeriac Puree, Glazed Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared duck breast, with golden-brown, crosshatched crispy skin, is the focal point on a pristine white bone china plate. The duck is presented as a whole, unsliced piece. Beside it, a flowing, organic swirl of creamy white celeriac puree creates soft contrast. A rich, deep purple blueberry-thyme gastrique is artfully drizzled over the duck and around the plate. Three to four vibrant orange, glossy glazed baby carrots are precisely arranged. A delicate fresh thyme sprig garnishes the dish. The plate rests on a premium grey veined marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin and elegant flatware are subtly placed. Dramatic professional lighting emphasizes textures and colors. The ultra-minimalist background showcases abundant negative space, highlighting culinary artistry.
instructions: Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season duck breasts generously with salt and pepper.
Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, oven-safe pan. Render fat over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip duck breasts. Sear flesh side for 2-3 minutes. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 5-7 minutes for medium-rare. Rest duck breasts for 10 minutes before serving.

For the gastrique, combine blueberries, red wine vinegar, sugar, and 2 thyme sprigs in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 10-15 minutes, crushing blueberries, until thickened and syrupy. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Discard solids. Keep gastrique warm.

For the celeriac puree, peel and dice celeriac into 2cm cubes. Place celeriac in a saucepan. Cover with milk and enough water to just cover. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until very tender.

Drain celeriac, reserving a little cooking liquid. Return celeriac to the pan. Add 30g butter. Mash or blend until smooth, adding reserved liquid if needed for desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.

For the glazed carrots, scrub baby carrots clean. In a small pan, combine carrots, 20g butter, and 100ml stock or water. Bring to a simmer. Cook, shaking pan occasionally, until liquid evaporates and carrots are tender and glossy. Season with salt.
To plate, spoon a generous swirl of celeriac puree onto each plate. Arrange a duck breast (unsliced) next to the puree. Drizzle blueberry-thyme gastrique artfully over and around the duck.
Arrange 3-4 glazed baby carrots beside the duck. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Summer Fruit Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of fresh fruit salad is presented in a simple, deep white ceramic bowl with a slight imperfection, on a well-used wooden dining table. The fruits are naturally arranged, overlapping slightly, creating a casual mound. Quartered bright red strawberries, deep blue blueberries, halved green grapes, and vibrant orange cantaloupe alongside pale green honeydew are cut into rustic 2cm cubes, showcasing varied textures. A light sheen from the honey-lime dressing coats the fruit. A few fresh mint leaves are casually scattered over the top. The bowl sits on a beige linen placemat, next to a standard metal spoon. A crumpled white paper napkin rests beside the bowl, contributing to the lived-in, relaxed family kitchen atmosphere. Warm, soft natural lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the fruit's freshness.
instructions: Wash fruits.
Hull strawberries. Quarter them.
Halve grapes.
Dice melons into 2cm cubes.
Peel and segment oranges.
Combine all fruits in a large bowl.
Whisk honey and lime juice in a small bowl.
Pour dressing over fruit.
Gently toss to coat.
Chill 30 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pickled Onion, Cherry, and Tomato Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone, resting on a light reclaimed wood surface. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish. At the center, a generous mound of vibrant green mixed leaves forms the base, loosely arranged. Scattered throughout are plump, halved fresh cherries, their deep red contrasting with the greens. Thin, translucent slices of bright pink pickled red onions are strategically placed. Roughly chopped, golden-brown toasted walnuts provide earthy tones. A rich, reddish-orange roasted cherry tomato vinaigrette is lightly drizzled, binding elements without drowning them. Fine curls of dark, glossy chocolate shavings are delicately sprinkled over the top. The composition is clean and minimalist, emphasizing natural beauty and fresh textures. An undyed linen napkin is beside the plate; a small potted green plant is visible in the soft background. The entire plate is visible, showcasing mindful negative space.

ingredients.name: Walnuts, lightly toasted and roughly chopped
Fresh parsley or mint, roughly chopped

instructions: Prepare Pickled Red Onions: Combine 250 ml apple cider vinegar, 250 ml water, 15 g salt, and 15 g maple syrup in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer until salt dissolves. Place sliced red onions in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over onions. Ensure onions are fully submerged. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Prepare Roasted Cherry Tomato Vinaigrette: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss cherry tomatoes with 30 ml olive oil, 5 g salt, and 2 g black pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized. Let cool slightly. Blend roasted tomatoes with remaining 30 ml olive oil and 30 ml apple cider vinegar until smooth. Adjust seasoning.
Assemble Salad: In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, halved fresh cherries, and toasted walnuts.
Dress Salad: Add a desired amount of Roasted Cherry Tomato Vinaigrette to the salad. Toss gently to coat.
Plate and Garnish: Divide salad among 4 plates. Scatter pickled red onions over each salad. Garnish with dark chocolate shavings and fresh parsley or mint.

recipes.recipe_name: Maple Pecan Chicken Bites
recipes.visual_description: Maple Pecan Chicken Bites are presented as golden-brown, bite-sized cubes, glistening with a light maple glaze. Each piece features a visible, textured crust of finely chopped pecans, offering a rich, toasted appearance. The chicken pieces, approximately 2.5 cm cubes, are arranged organically on a clean white porcelain sharing platter, leaving moderate negative space. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped fresh chives provides a vibrant color contrast and herbaceous aroma. The overall presentation is clean and professional, placed on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside the platter. Natural, even lighting highlights the varied textures and warm tones of the dish, set against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2.5 cm cubes. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Finely chop pecans. Combine chopped pecans, flour, salt, and black pepper in a shallow dish.
Whisk egg in a separate shallow dish.
Dip each chicken cube into whisked egg. Dredge thoroughly in the pecan mixture. Press to ensure coating adheres.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Add butter.
Add coated chicken cubes to the hot pan in a single layer. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary.
Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken cooks, gently heat maple syrup in a small saucepan over low heat. Do not boil.
Transfer cooked chicken to a mixing bowl. Pour warm maple syrup over chicken. Toss gently to coat all pieces evenly.
Arrange chicken bites on a serving platter. Garnish with fresh chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sourdough Crostini with Fermented Onion and Potato-Mustard Spread
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist presentation of 8-12 bite-sized canapés arranged on a light reclaimed wood board. Each canapé features a crisp, golden-brown sourdough crostini, approximately 5 cm in diameter. A smooth, pale yellow whipped potato-mustard spread is generously spooned onto the crostini, creating a soft, inviting base. Crowned atop the spread is a vibrant mound of thinly sliced, ruby-red fermented red onion relish, offering a striking color contrast and textural variation. Small, fresh green dill sprigs are delicately placed on each canapé as a natural, sustainable garnish. The arrangement is clean and spaced, allowing ample white space on the board. The backdrop is a clean, minimalist setting with soft, natural lighting, subtly hinting at natural elements like a plant or stone texture, reinforcing the eco-conscious aesthetic. The overall impression is one of clean lines, natural beauty, and ingredient focus.
instructions: Thinly slice red onion. Place in a clean jar.
Add 5g salt and 5g sugar to the jar. Pour in 120ml filtered water. Ensure onions are submerged. Cover loosely with a lid or fermentation airlock.
Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermentation.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice sourdough baguette into 1 cm thick rounds.
Drizzle baguette slices with olive oil. Arrange on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely.
Peel and dice potato into 2 cm cubes. Place in a saucepan. Cover with cold, salted water.
Bring to a boil. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until very tender. Drain thoroughly.
Return hot potato to the saucepan. Mash until smooth. Add 15g Dijon mustard, 30ml plant-based milk, 5ml lemon juice, and 5ml soy sauce.
Whip the mixture until light and creamy. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Spoon a generous amount of potato-mustard spread onto each cooled sourdough crostini.
Top each canapé with a small mound of fermented red onion relish.
Garnish each canapé with a small sprig of fresh dill.

recipes.recipe_name: Asparagus, Cucumber, and Chicken Salad with Herb Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an elegant, matte white bone china plate, placed on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. A single, crisp white linen napkin, folded precisely into a triangle, rests beside the plate. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's textures. The composition is minimalist and organic. Blanched, vibrant green asparagus spears are artfully arranged, some whole, some halved lengthwise, creating gentle curves. Thin, translucent ribbons of compressed cucumber weave delicately among the asparagus. Two to three small, irregular, pristine white sous vide chicken morsels are nestled within the vegetables. A vivid, verdant herb emulsion is meticulously drizzled around and over the components, forming abstract pools. The plate's abundant negative space emphasizes the precise placement and pristine quality of each element. A few delicate microgreens or tiny edible flowers are scattered thoughtfully for a final touch of color and freshness.

ingredients.name: Microgreens (e.g., pea shoots or small dill sprigs)

instructions: Season chicken breast with salt, pepper, and olive oil. Place in a vacuum-sealable bag. Seal bag. Cook in a sous vide bath at 63°C for 1.5 hours. Remove from bath. Chill immediately in an ice bath. Once cold, cut chicken into small, irregular morsels (approx. 1cm).

Trim woody ends from asparagus. Bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Prepare an ice bath. Blanch asparagus in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

Peel cucumber. Using a mandoline, slice cucumber into very thin ribbons or rounds (1-2mm thick). Lay slices flat on a tray. Sprinkle with white wine vinegar and salt. Place another tray on top. Press with weight for 30 minutes to extract excess water and compress.

Blanch dill, chervil, and parsley briefly in boiling water (10 seconds). Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze out all excess water. Combine blanched herbs, grapeseed oil, white wine vinegar, salt, and pepper in a high-speed blender. Blend until very smooth and emulsified, adding a few drops of ice water if needed to achieve a pourable consistency. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a perfectly smooth emulsion.

Gently toss blanched asparagus and compressed cucumber with a small amount of the herb emulsion. Arrange asparagus and cucumber artfully on four individual fine-dining plates, creating natural, flowing shapes. Place 2-3 small chicken morsels among the vegetables on each plate. Drizzle additional herb emulsion around the components. Garnish with microgreens or edible flowers. Serve immediately.
notes: The sous vide method ensures incredibly tender chicken.
The compression technique enhances cucumber flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken with Fermented Tomato-Onion Preserve
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Chicken is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, set against a light, natural wood surface. The tender, golden-brown chicken thigh, kept whole, rests gently beside a rich, rust-colored dollop of chunky Fermented Tomato-Onion Preserve. Roasted carrot and parsnip chunks, their edges subtly caramelized, are thoughtfully arranged to create natural negative space. A few vibrant green fresh oregano leaves and delicate, crispy onion peels are scattered sparingly as a natural garnish. The composition is clean and minimalist, celebrating the pure textures and earthy colors of the ingredients. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its organic beauty. An undyed linen napkin sits beside the plate, complementing the sustainable aesthetic.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Peel carrots and parsnips. Cut into rough 3cm chunks. Reserve onion peels for stock if desired.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss carrot and parsnip chunks with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Dice one large onion and mince 2 garlic cloves. Add to the same pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Dice 2 large tomatoes. Add to the pan with the sautéed onion and garlic. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Add vegetable stock and 2 fresh oregano sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pan. Reduce heat to low. Slow cook for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is very tender. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C using a meat thermometer.
Remove chicken from pan. Discard oregano sprigs. Reduce pan sauce slightly if desired.

To plate, spoon a generous portion of Fermented Tomato-Onion Preserve onto each plate. Place one slow-cooked chicken thigh on top of or beside the preserve. Arrange roasted carrot and parsnip chunks alongside the chicken.
Garnish with fresh oregano leaves and a sprinkle of crispy onion peel if using.
notes: Prepare the Fermented Tomato-Onion Preserve 5-7 days in advance. To make it: Finely dice 300g ripe tomatoes and 1 medium onion. Mince 2 garlic cloves. Combine with 5g non-iodized salt and chopped leaves from 1 fresh oregano sprig. Pack tightly into a clean, sterile glass jar, leaving 2cm headspace. Cover completely with filtered, non-chlorinated water. Secure with an airlock lid or a regular lid, burping daily. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Store in the refrigerator.
Embrace zero-waste practices: Use chicken bones and vegetable trimmings (like onion skins, carrot tops) to make flavorful homemade stock instead of discarding them. Compost any remaining food scraps.

recipes.recipe_name: Artichoke Confit Salad with Sous Vide Chicken and Black Truffle Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an expansive, pristine white bone china plate, allowing abundant negative space to highlight the culinary artistry. At the center, an organic composition of golden-brown confit artichoke halves forms a natural base, their tender texture evident. Small, precisely cut, pale sous vide chicken chunks are nestled among the artichokes, their edges subtly defined. A scattering of vibrant green micro-herbs, like chervil and tarragon, adds a delicate pop of color and freshness. A glossy black truffle vinaigrette is artfully drizzled around and over the elements, creating elegant, flowing lines that catch the light. A single, crisp, irregular shard of golden-brown sourdough tuile stands upright, providing a textural counterpoint. The lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows that enhance depth and dimension. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin in the corner, conveying a refined, minimalist Michelin-starred dining experience.
