Beside the beef, a generous spoonful of vibrant mushroom and oregano confit is artfully arranged. The confit features glossy, deeply browned sliced mushrooms, softened, slightly burst cherry tomatoes in shades of red, and translucent small-diced red onion, all glistening with a light sauce. Fresh green oregano leaves are visibly integrated within the confit, adding a pop of color and texture. A delicate drizzle of pan juices or a light, savory reduction lightly coats the plate around the beef. The overall presentation is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the rich colors of the beef and the rustic elegance of the confit. The dish is placed on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin lies beside the plate. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, with a subtly blurred, casual restaurant-style background. Traditional flatware is positioned for dining.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Let sit at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to skillet. Cook until browned and liquid evaporates, about 7-10 minutes.
Add cherry tomatoes, minced garlic, and oregano sprigs to skillet. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften and burst slightly.
Deglaze with red wine, if using, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce until almost evaporated.
Pour in beef stock. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Remove oregano sprigs. Keep confit warm.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a separate heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place beef medallions in hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Do not overcrowd pan.
Remove beef from pan. Add remaining 15g butter to pan. Swirl to melt. Spoon butter over beef. Let beef rest for 5 minutes.
Plate beef medallions. Spoon mushroom and oregano confit alongside. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust cooking time for beef based on thickness and desired doneness.
Fresh oregano is essential for flavor.
Resting the beef is crucial for tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Loin Medallions with Creamy Mushroom-Mustard Sauce and Garlic Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared pork loin medallions and a golden-brown garlic potato gratin are elegantly plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two thick-cut, round pork medallions, pan-seared to a tender, juicy interior with a light golden crust, are slightly overlapped at the center. Beside them, a rectangular slice of garlic potato gratin showcases layers of thinly sliced potatoes, baked to a creamy tenderness with a crisp, cheesy top. A rich, creamy mushroom-mustard sauce, flecked with sautéed mushroom slices and minced garlic, is generously spooned over the pork. The dish features warm browns from the seared pork and gratin, contrasted with the creamy, earthy tones of the sauce. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the pork and sauce for a final pop of color. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, under natural, even lighting. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel potatoes. Slice potatoes into thin, uniform rounds (2-3mm thick).
Mince 2 cloves of garlic. Combine sliced potatoes, minced garlic, 100ml heavy cream, 25g grated Parmesan, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Mix well.
Arrange potato mixture in a single layer in a shallow baking dish (approx. 20x20cm).
Bake gratin for 40-50 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown. Let rest.
Slice pork loin into 8 thick-cut medallions. Season pork medallions generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork medallions for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 63°C/145°F). Remove pork from skillet and set aside to rest.
Finely dice the small onion. Slice mushrooms. Mince remaining 2 cloves of garlic.
In the same skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Sauté until browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Whisk in Dijon mustard and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in remaining 100ml heavy cream and 25g grated Parmesan. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning as needed.
Chop fresh parsley.

To serve, place a portion of potato gratin on each plate. Arrange two pork medallions next to the gratin. Spoon creamy mushroom-mustard sauce generously over the pork. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Earl Grey Glazed Pork Loin with Roasted Pineapple and Pear, Pecan Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Earl Grey Glazed Pork Loin is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Thick medallions of seared and roasted pork, with a golden-brown exterior and moist interior, are arranged slightly overlapping. A glossy, deep amber Earl Grey jus is generously spooned over the pork. Roasted pineapple wedges, displaying caramelized edges, and tender, light golden pear wedges are arranged organically beside the pork. A scattering of coarsely chopped, toasted pecans adds an earthy tone and textural contrast. The plate features balanced negative space, highlighting the dish's refined yet approachable presentation. A small fresh thyme sprig provides a vibrant green accent. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin lies beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, and the background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer pan to oven. Roast pork 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 65°C.
Remove pork from oven. Rest 10 minutes on a cutting board. The temperature will rise to 70-72°C.
For the jus: Steep Earl Grey tea bags in 100 ml hot water for 5 minutes. Remove tea bags. Discard tea bags.
In the same pan (after removing pork), add chopped shallots and minced garlic. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with a splash of water or white wine if desired.
Add steeped Earl Grey tea, chicken broth, honey, and apple cider vinegar. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce liquid by half, about 8-10 minutes, until slightly thickened. Whisk in butter until the jus is glossy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For the fruit: Cut pineapple into 2 cm wedges. Core and cut pears into 2 cm wedges.
Toss fruit with a little olive oil, salt, and 2 sprigs of fresh thyme.
Spread fruit on a baking sheet. Roast 15 minutes or until tender and lightly caramelized.
For the pecan crumble: Toast pecans in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 3 minutes. Coarsely chop.
To serve: Slice pork loin into 2 cm thick medallions.
Arrange pork medallions on each plate. Spoon Earl Grey jus generously over the pork.
Arrange roasted pineapple and pear wedges organically beside the pork.
Sprinkle toasted pecan crumble over the entire dish.
Garnish with a small fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Stuffed Eggplant with Lamb and Feta
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two substantial roasted eggplant halves, each brimming with a rich, savory ground lamb and tomato filling, centrally presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The eggplant skin retains its deep, glossy purple hue, providing a striking contrast to the warm, earthy tones of the filling. The filling itself is a robust blend of finely diced onion, minced garlic, browned ground lamb, and diced tomatoes, infused with dried oregano, presenting a slightly rustic yet cohesive texture. Generous crumbles of creamy white feta cheese are melted and lightly golden-browned over the top of each stuffed eggplant half, creating a bubbly, inviting crust. A vibrant scattering of fresh chopped parsley provides a fresh green accent. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, complemented by a neatly folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, set against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping in any remaining sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Wash eggplants. Cut each eggplant lengthwise in half.
Score the flesh of each eggplant half in a crisscross pattern, without cutting through the skin. Sprinkle lightly with salt.
Brush the cut sides of the eggplant halves generously with 30 ml of olive oil.
Place eggplants cut-side down on the prepared baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until very tender.
While eggplants roast, heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground lamb to the pan. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in canned chopped tomatoes and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly.
Remove roasted eggplants from oven. Carefully scoop out the tender flesh from each half, leaving a 1 cm border around the skin to maintain the shell's integrity. Chop the scooped eggplant flesh.
Add chopped eggplant flesh to the lamb mixture in the pan. Stir well to combine. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Spoon the lamb and eggplant filling generously into each roasted eggplant shell.
Place stuffed eggplants back on the baking tray. Top each with crumbled feta cheese.
Return to oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until feta is golden brown and bubbly.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Salting the eggplant before roasting helps draw out bitterness and excess moisture, resulting in a creamier texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Imam Bayildi (Stuffed Eggplant)
recipes.visual_description: A single Imam Bayildi (stuffed eggplant) half rests on a round white porcelain dinner plate. The eggplant's deep purple skin, slightly wrinkled from roasting, contrasts with the vibrant, rich red-orange tomato and vegetable filling overflowing from its center. The eggplant flesh is tender, appearing glistening from olive oil. Diced onions and bell peppers are clearly visible within the robust filling, interspersed with finely chopped fresh parsley and dill. A small cluster of fresh parsley leaves and a bright yellow lemon wedge are placed precisely beside the eggplant. The scene is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface and a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating an inviting ambiance. The background is gently blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain yogurt or rice pilaf.
Can be part of a meze spread.

ingredients.name: Ripe tomatoes
ingredients.quantity: 400g, peeled, deseeded, and diced (or 1 can diced tomatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Wash eggplants. Cut each in half lengthwise. Score the flesh deeply in a crosshatch pattern, leaving a 1 cm border. Do not cut through skin.
Sprinkle cut side with salt. Let sit 20 minutes. Pat dry thoroughly.

Heat 100 ml olive oil in large pan over medium-high heat. Fry eggplant halves flesh-side down until golden brown and softened, 5-7 minutes. Flip. Fry skin-side down 3 minutes. Remove. Drain on paper towels.
Add remaining 50 ml olive oil to same pan. Sauté diced onions until translucent, 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced bell peppers. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add diced tomatoes, sugar, salt, pepper. Cook 10-15 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Stir in chopped parsley, mint, dill. Remove from heat.
Arrange fried eggplant halves in baking dish. Gently press scored flesh to create hollow.
Fill each eggplant half generously with vegetable mixture.
Pour 100 ml hot water into baking dish around eggplants.
Cover dish with foil. Bake 30 minutes.
Remove foil. Bake additional 15-20 minutes. Eggplants should be very tender. Filling should bubble.
Serve warm or at room temperature. Garnish with fresh parsley and lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Eggplant with Spiced Lamb and Minted Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, offering a balanced, professional arrangement. Two to three thick, golden-brown roasted eggplant wedges are carefully placed, slightly overlapping. A generous mound of rich, savory spiced lamb mince is spooned directly over the eggplant. The lamb, deeply browned with visible specks of onion and tomato, is moist and aromatic. A creamy white, cool minted Greek yogurt sauce is artfully drizzled over the lamb and around the eggplant, creating soft, flowing lines. The vibrant green of fresh mint leaves, roughly chopped and scattered, provides a fresh garnish, contrasting with the warm tones of the dish. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The table setting features a simple wooden surface, a crisp white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and standard polished flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish without harsh shadows, set against a softly blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with warm pita bread for scooping.

ingredients.name: Fresh mint
ingredients.quantity: 10g, finely chopped, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Slice eggplants into 1.5 cm thick rounds or wedges. Place on a baking sheet. Drizzle generously with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until tender and golden brown.
While eggplant roasts, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add lamb mince. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, and cinnamon. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, combine Greek yogurt, chopped fresh mint, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Mix well.
To serve, arrange roasted eggplant pieces on individual plates. Spoon a generous amount of spiced lamb mixture over the eggplant. Drizzle with minted yogurt sauce. Garnish with fresh mint leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Thyme Oat Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant starter portion of creamy Mushroom and Thyme Oat Risotto is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is free-flowing, not molded, exhibiting a rich, earthy brown color from the sautéed cremini and shiitake mushrooms, which are tenderly integrated throughout. A scattering of golden-brown sautéed mushroom slices, reserved from cooking, are artfully placed atop the risotto, along with delicate shavings of aged Parmesan cheese. Fresh thyme leaves provide vibrant green contrast and aromatic appeal. The texture is visually creamy and inviting. The plate is set on a simple, light-toned wooden table. A folded light grey cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a gently blurred, casual bistro-style background, suggesting a relaxed yet refined dining experience. The entire plate is visible, showcasing balanced composition and appropriate negative space.

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme
ingredients.quantity: 2 sprigs, leaves removed, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced shallots. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 8-10 minutes. Remove half the mushrooms from the pan and set aside for garnish.
Add rolled oats to the pan with remaining mushrooms. Toast oats for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.

Add warm vegetable broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 20-25 minutes, or until oats are creamy and tender but still have a slight bite.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining butter, grated Parmesan, and fresh thyme leaves. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Let risotto rest for 2 minutes, covered.
Serve immediately.
notes: For best texture, use old-fashioned rolled oats, not quick oats.
Ensure broth is warm for consistent cooking.
Risotto should be fluid, not dry, and spread naturally on the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Eggplant Risotto with Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, off-white risotto is centrally mounded on a round, clean white porcelain plate. The risotto has a fluid, flowing consistency, not stiff. Scattered throughout the risotto are visibly tender, slightly caramelized 2 cm cubes of roasted eggplant. The eggplant pieces are a rich brown with subtle purple hues. A sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley adorns the top, adding a pop of fresh color. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese is visible. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware (fork and spoon) are arranged beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined restaurant portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto quality diminishes quickly upon standing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut eggplant into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread eggplant on a baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 30g butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges are translucent (tostatura).
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add warm broth, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for liquid to be almost absorbed before adding the next ladle.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and rice al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30g butter and grated Parmesan (mantecatura).
Gently fold in roasted eggplant cubes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Miso Glazed Eggplant with Shiitake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Japanese Miso Glazed Eggplant with Shiitake Mushrooms is elegantly presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Thick batons of eggplant, cooked until tender with a glossy, caramelized deep aubergine hue, are arranged neatly but not rigidly, slightly overlapping to create a dynamic flow. Interspersed among the eggplant are tender, sliced shiitake mushrooms, their dark caps providing a textural contrast. A rich, golden-brown miso glaze evenly coats all ingredients, catching the light. The dish is garnished with a scattering of vibrant green, thinly sliced scallions and a sprinkle of pale, toasted sesame seeds, adding fresh color and subtle crunch. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. Beside the plate, a pair of sleek black chopsticks rests on a small ceramic chopstick rest. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish's appealing textures and colors against a gently blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of steamed short-grain white rice.
Offer a small dish of pickled ginger (gari) or quick-pickled daikon as a palate cleanser.
instructions: Wash eggplants. Cut into 2cm thick batons or wedges. Place in a colander. Sprinkle generously with salt. Let sit for 30 minutes to draw out moisture.
Rinse eggplant well under cold water. Pat thoroughly dry with paper towels.
In a small bowl, whisk together miso paste, mirin, sake, soy sauce, sugar, grated ginger, and minced garlic until smooth. This is the miso glaze.
Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add eggplant in a single layer, working in batches if needed.
Cook eggplant for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and tender. Remove cooked eggplant and set aside.
Add remaining 30ml vegetable oil to the pan. Add sliced shiitake mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Return cooked eggplant to the pan with the shiitake mushrooms. Pour the prepared miso glaze over the eggplant and mushrooms. Add 60ml water or dashi.
Toss gently to coat all ingredients. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until the glaze thickens and coats the eggplant evenly.
Remove from heat. Drizzle with toasted sesame oil.
Plate immediately. Garnish generously with thinly sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Salting the eggplant before cooking helps to draw out bitterness and excess moisture, ensuring a tender texture.
Japanese or Chinese eggplants are preferred for their less bitter taste and firmer texture compared to globe eggplants.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Stuffed Eggplant
recipes.visual_description: A single large, deep purple eggplant half, generously filled with a vibrant, textural rice and vegetable stuffing, rests on a pristine white porcelain plate. The eggplant's roasted skin is slightly crinkled, contrasting with the golden-brown, crispy breadcrumb and melted Parmesan topping. The rich, red tomato sauce pools elegantly around the base of the eggplant, its color intensified by the natural light. Flecks of green basil and parsley from the stuffing are visible, along with diced red bell pepper and dark Kalamata olives, adding pops of color. Fresh basil leaves are artfully placed on top of the stuffing, alongside a delicate sprinkle of lemon zest. The plating is clean and professional, with thoughtful negative space. A simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin subtly complement the dish, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread to soak up the rich tomato sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve eggplants lengthwise. Scoop out flesh, leaving a 1cm border. Dice scooped-out eggplant flesh. Lightly salt eggplant shells and diced flesh. Set aside 15 minutes.
Pat eggplant shells and diced flesh dry with paper towels. Drizzle eggplant shells with olive oil. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes until tender.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, diced bell pepper, and diced mushrooms. Cook 8-10 minutes until vegetables are tender and liquid evaporates. Add diced eggplant flesh. Cook 5 minutes.

Stir in rice. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Pour in 250ml vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook 15 minutes, or until rice is almost tender and liquid is absorbed. Remove from heat. Stir in chopped basil, parsley, oregano, sliced olives, and 50g Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper.
In a separate saucepan, combine crushed tomatoes and remaining 250ml vegetable stock. Simmer gently 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon rice mixture evenly into roasted eggplant shells. Place stuffed eggplants in an oven-safe dish. Pour tomato sauce around eggplants.
Combine remaining 50g Parmesan and breadcrumbs. Sprinkle over stuffed eggplants.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and eggplants are heated through.
Grate lemon zest over baked eggplants before serving.
notes: For best flavor, use fresh, good quality herbs. Adjust seasoning to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Chicken Skewers with Lemon Herb Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of golden-brown grilled chicken skewers rests casually on a round, rustic ceramic plate. Each skewer holds three to four generous chunks of perfectly seared chicken breast, diced into 2-3 cm cubes, exhibiting a beautiful char on the edges and juicy interior. A creamy, bright white lemon herb yogurt dip is dolloped beside the skewers, its smooth texture contrasting with the chicken. A scattering of finely chopped fresh parsley and mint adds vibrant green flecks and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, filling the plate adequately without overcrowding. The setting is a warm, homely family kitchen, with the dish placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Everyday flatware and a casually folded cloth napkin complete the relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting appeal of the dish.
instructions: Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes. This prevents burning.
Dice chicken breast into 2-3 cm cubes. Pat dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, combine chicken cubes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Thread chicken cubes onto soaked skewers. Aim for 3-4 pieces per skewer.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Alternatively, preheat a grill pan or outdoor grill.
Add skewers to the hot pan or grill. Do not overcrowd.
Cook chicken skewers for 4-5 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While chicken cooks, prepare the yogurt dip. Finely chop parsley and mint.
Mince garlic cloves.
In a small bowl, combine yogurt, chopped parsley, chopped mint, minced garlic, zest of half lemon, and juice of half lemon. Stir well.
Season yogurt dip with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve grilled chicken skewers immediately with the lemon herb yogurt dip.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo e Pomodoro Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy Pollo e Pomodoro Risotto is presented in a shallow, clean white porcelain bowl. The risotto is fluid and lustrous, not stiff, allowing it to gently spread within the bowl. Scattered throughout the vibrant, orange-red rice are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, approximately 2 cm cubes, showcasing a slightly crisp exterior and tender interior. Bright red crushed tomato pieces are visible, adding bursts of color and texture. Fresh green basil leaves, torn, are generously sprinkled over the top, providing a verdant contrast and aromatic appeal. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese melts slightly into the warm risotto. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. Beside the bowl, a white cotton napkin is neatly folded, and a traditional silver fork and spoon are placed. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's warmth and inviting texture. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, creating a balanced and professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto quality diminishes quickly upon cooling.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
Offer crusty Italian bread for scooping up any remaining sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken breast dry. Cut into 2 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Remove chicken. Set aside.

In a separate heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice. Ensure all grains are coated and slightly translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well. Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously.
Wait until each ladleful of stock is almost completely absorbed before adding the next. Continue this process for 18-20 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and al dente. It should flow freely.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15 g butter and half of the grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute. This is 'mantecatura'.
Fold in the seared chicken chunks. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish with remaining Parmigiano Reggiano and fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Risotto should be creamy and flow freely, not dry or stiff. Adjust stock if needed to achieve this consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto ai Funghi Chanterelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, golden-hued Risotto ai Funghi Chanterelle is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is fluid and free-flowing, not rigidly shaped, forming a gentle mound in the center of the plate. Golden-brown, sautéed chanterelle mushrooms, some whole and some halved, are artfully nestled within and on top of the risotto, showcasing their distinct shape and color. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast. The texture of the risotto is visibly creamy and luxurious, with individual rice grains still discernable. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, soft, even light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its textures and colors. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting, possibly with a wine glass subtly visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately upon completion; risotto does not hold well.
Accompany with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Soave.
Offer additional grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
instructions: Clean chanterelle mushrooms. Brush off dirt. Cut larger mushrooms in half or quarters. Leave smaller ones whole.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chanterelles. Sauté 5-7 minutes until golden brown and tender. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from skillet. Set aside.
Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and 20 g butter over medium heat.
Add diced shallots. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened and translucent. Do not brown.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains are translucent. This is 'toasting the rice'.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add one ladleful (about 150 ml) of hot broth to the rice. Stir continuously until broth is almost fully absorbed. This takes about 2-3 minutes.

Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly after each addition until broth is absorbed. Repeat for 18-20 minutes. The rice should be creamy and al dente. It should still have a slight bite.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in remaining 40 g butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes. This is 'mantecatura', creating a creamy texture.
Fold in sautéed chanterelle mushrooms and most of the chopped parsley. Reserve some parsley for garnish.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and an extra sprinkle of Parmesan if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, matte-finished ceramic bowl on a dark wood table. The base is a vibrant, reddish-orange long-grain rice, cooked to a moist, free-flowing consistency. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs with crispy skin rest atop the rice. The chicken is not sliced. Accompanying the chicken are charred tomato wedges and small cubes of sautéed onion mixed within the grains. Garnishes include fresh, bright green cilantro leaves and thin wedges of lime placed on the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textural contrast between the crispy chicken skin and the soft rice. A linen napkin and a heavy silver fork sit beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with pickled red onions
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from guajillo and arbol chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chilies in 200ml hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend soaked chilies, tomatoes, half the onion, and garlic until smooth.
Pat chicken dry and season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes then remove from pot.
Add rice and remaining onion to the pot.
Toast rice for 3 minutes until opaque and slightly golden.
Pour blended chili-tomato mixture into the rice.
Cook for 5 minutes while stirring until sauce thickens.
Add chicken stock and return chicken to the pot.
Reduce heat to low and cover with a tight lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs to ensure the meat remains juicy during simmering
Do not over-toast the dried chilies as they can turn bitter
The rice should be moist and flavorful, absorbing all the chili-tomato broth

recipes.recipe_name: Apple Banana Mini Loaf Cakes
recipes.visual_description: A collection of 6-9 small, uniform Apple Banana Mini Loaf Cakes is arranged neatly on a simple white ceramic serving platter. Each miniature cake, cut into approximately 4x4 cm squares or rectangles, has a light golden-brown exterior with a slightly rustic, homemade appearance. A thin, simple white powdered sugar glaze is generously drizzled over the top of each cake, some glaze drips casually down the sides. The visible cut sides reveal a moist, tender crumb with natural variations in texture, showing scattered flecks of mashed banana and soft, small pieces of diced apple. The cakes are spaced consistently on the platter, creating an inviting, approachable display. The platter rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, evoking a relaxed, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. A casually placed, neutral-toned cloth napkin is nearby.

ingredients.name: Apple
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium (about 150 g), peeled, cored, and finely diced (small cubes)

ingredients.name: Milk
ingredients.quantity: 30 ml (for glaze, plus more if needed)

instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 20x10 cm loaf pan or a mini loaf pan.
In a large bowl, mash ripe bananas. Add diced apple.
Stir in granulated sugar, brown sugar, egg, vegetable oil, milk, and vanilla extract. Mix until just combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. If using mini loaf pans, adjust baking time to 20-30 minutes.
Cool cake in the pan for 10 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze: Whisk powdered sugar with milk until smooth.
Once cake is completely cool, drizzle generously with glaze.
Cut the loaf cake into 6-9 uniform miniature squares or rectangles.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Garlic Roasted Potatoes and Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Garlic Roasted Potatoes and Creamy Mushroom Sauce is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two thick-cut, pan-seared beef medallions, cooked to a perfect medium-rare with a dark golden-brown crust, are placed slightly off-center. They are whole, not sliced. Adjacent to the beef, a neat pile of garlic-roasted potato wedges, golden-brown and slightly crisp on the exterior, is arranged. A rich, creamy mushroom sauce, studded with tender, browned mushroom slices and finely minced shallots, is generously spooned over the beef medallions, cascading slightly onto the plate and mingling with the potatoes. The sauce has a warm, inviting beige-brown hue. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is sprinkled over the beef and sauce, with a small sprig of fresh rosemary placed decoratively beside the beef. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the appealing textures and natural colors of the ingredients. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded white cotton napkin positioned beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and emphasizing its professional presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.

Wash potatoes. Cut into 2cm wedges. In a large bowl, toss potato wedges with 30ml olive oil, 4 minced garlic cloves, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until golden brown and tender. Flip halfway through.
Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on all sides.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add beef medallions. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer to desired doneness. Do not overcrowd the pan. Work in batches if necessary.
Transfer seared beef to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.

In the same skillet, reduce heat to medium. Add butter. Add sliced mushrooms and minced shallot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender. Add 2 minced garlic cloves. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer. Cook until liquid reduces by half.
Stir in heavy cream and leaves from 1 sprig of fresh thyme. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Remove thyme sprig if using whole.

Place roasted potato wedges on one side of each plate. Arrange 1-2 beef medallions next to the potatoes. Spoon creamy mushroom sauce generously over the beef and slightly onto the potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a small sprig of fresh rosemary. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Banana & Roasted Apple Dessert
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, allowing ample negative space around the components. A single roasted apple half, golden-brown from caramelization, sits at the center, its natural contours visible. Beside it, a generous, organically shaped dollop of glossy, caramelized fermented banana puree, a rich amber hue, contrasts with the apple's lighter flesh. A delicate, fine dusting of reddish-brown apple skin powder is subtly scattered over a portion of the apple and plate, adding a textural and color accent. The overall presentation is minimalistic and clean, emphasizing the pure, natural beauty and textures of the ingredients. The scene is bathed in soft, natural light, highlighting the subtle sheen of the puree and the tender texture of the apple. A simple, undyed linen napkin in beige is folded neatly to one side, and the surface is light reclaimed wood, reinforcing the sustainable aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare fermented banana puree: Slice overripe bananas into 1 cm rounds. Place in a clean glass jar. Add filtered water and sea salt. Stir. Cover loosely with a cloth or lid. Let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly bubbly and tangy. Strain liquid, reserve. Blend fermented banana solids into a smooth puree.

Make caramelized banana puree: Transfer fermented banana puree to a small saucepan. Add 30 ml date syrup. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened and caramelized, about 10-15 minutes. Set aside.

Prepare apple skin dust: Peel firm apples, reserving all skins. Spread apple skins thinly on a baking sheet. Dehydrate in a low oven (50°C) or dehydrator until brittle, about 2-4 hours. Grind dehydrated skins into a fine powder using a spice grinder or mortar and pestle. Store in an airtight container.

Roast apples: Preheat oven to 180°C. Core firm apples. Halve each apple. Place cut-side up on a baking tray. Drizzle with remaining 30 ml date syrup and lemon juice. Roast for 20-30 minutes, or until tender but still holding shape. Do not overcook.
Assemble dessert: Place one roasted apple half on each plate. Spoon a dollop of caramelized fermented banana puree next to the apple. Lightly dust with apple skin powder just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Beef Bites with Tangy Rind Relish
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a minimalist, natural aesthetic on a light bamboo table surface. Handcrafted ceramic plates in earthy cream or beige tones hold the snack. Small, irregular rounds of dark red fermented beef, about 1 cm thick, are arranged casually on one side of the plate. Their edges show a slightly darker, cured ring, contrasting with the rich, dense interior. The beef rounds have a subtle, natural sheen. Adjacent to the beef, a small, unglazed ceramic bowl contains the Tangy Rind Relish. The relish is a vibrant, translucent green from the watermelon rind cubes, interspersed with dark mustard and dill seeds, and flecks of red pepper. The rind cubes are irregular, reflecting their hand-cut nature. The overall composition is clean and uncluttered, with ample negative space. A natural, undyed linen napkin in beige is casually draped beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures of the ingredients and the rustic pottery. A subtle, out-of-focus plant element in the background adds to the eco-conscious ambiance without distracting from the food. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a single sharing portion.

ingredients.name: Ground beef (80/20 lean to fat ratio)
Watermelon rind (white part, peeled, cut into 1 cm cubes)

instructions: Rehydrate starter culture in distilled water. Let sit 15 minutes.
Combine ground beef, curing salt, sea salt, dextrose, black pepper, garlic powder, and paprika in a large bowl. Mix thoroughly by hand until well combined and sticky.
Add rehydrated starter culture to the beef mixture. Mix again until evenly distributed.
Form the mixture into small logs, about 1.5 cm diameter and 5-7 cm long.
Hang or place logs on a rack in a fermentation chamber or controlled environment (temperature 18-22°C, humidity 75-85%) for 24-48 hours until pH drops (target pH 5.2-5.4).
Move logs to a drying environment (temperature 12-15°C, humidity 70-75%) for 2-4 weeks, or until they lose 30-35% of their original weight. Check for firmness.
Store cured beef bites in the refrigerator.
Prepare watermelon rind: Remove green skin and pink flesh. Cut white rind into 1 cm cubes.
In a saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, sea salt, mustard seeds, dill seeds, and red pepper flakes. Bring to a boil.
Add watermelon rind cubes to the boiling liquid. Reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, until rind is tender-crisp.
Remove from heat. Let cool completely.
Transfer relish and liquid to a clean jar. Store in refrigerator.
Slice Fermented Beef Bites into 1 cm thick rounds.
Serve beef rounds alongside Tangy Rind Relish.
notes: Dry curing requires specific conditions and attention to food safety. Ensure proper temperature, humidity, and pH monitoring.
The weight loss is critical for safety and texture.
Use a dedicated curing chamber or a temperature/humidity controlled environment for best results.

recipes.recipe_name: Deconstructed Hazelnut Sablé, Coconut Crémeux, Lemon Gel
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented on an expensive bone china plate with a subtle, organic pattern, resting on a white Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits elegantly beside the plate. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's architectural precision and abundant negative space. A single portion is artfully composed. A generous, flowing smear of creamy, pale ivory Coconut Crémeux forms a graceful curve across the plate. Beside it, a cluster of golden-brown Hazelnut Sablé Crumble, with irregular, rustic pieces, provides textural contrast. Small, translucent cubes of vibrant yellow Lemon Gel are strategically placed, catching the light and offering a burst of color. A few delicate, toasted coconut flakes are scattered with intention, adding a subtle warmth and additional texture. The composition is minimalist yet impactful, emphasizing the natural forms and sophisticated color palette of the individual components. The overall presentation is one of refined elegance and culinary mastery.
instructions: Prepare Hazelnut Sablé Crumble:
Combine flour, powdered sugar, ground hazelnuts, and salt in a bowl.
Add cold butter cubes.
Rub butter into dry ingredients until a crumbly texture forms.
Spread mixture on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake at 160°C (325°F) for 15-20 minutes.
Bake until golden brown and fragrant.
Cool completely.
Break into desired crumble size.
Prepare Coconut Crémeux:
Whisk egg yolks, sugar, cornstarch, and salt in a bowl.
Heat coconut milk and heavy cream in a saucepan until simmering.
Slowly temper hot milk mixture into egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring continuously, until thickened.
Cook until it coats the back of a spoon.
Strain crémeux through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl.
Cover surface with plastic wrap to prevent a skin from forming.
Chill in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Prepare Lemon Gel:
Combine lemon juice, sugar, and lemon zest in a small saucepan.
Whisk in agar-agar powder.
Bring to a boil, whisking constantly.
Boil for 1 minute.
Pour mixture into a shallow dish.
Chill until set, about 30 minutes.
Once set, cut into small cubes or blend until smooth for a gel.
For a very smooth gel, pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Assemble the Dessert:
Spoon a natural, organic smear or dollop of chilled Coconut Crémeux onto one side of the plate.
Scatter Hazelnut Sablé Crumble beside the crémeux. Create an abstract line or cluster.
Place a few small, precisely cut cubes of Lemon Gel, or carefully pipe small dots of Lemon Gel, strategically around the crémeux and crumble.
Sprinkle a few toasted coconut flakes as a garnish.
Add one or two tiny edible flowers or micro herbs for color contrast, if using.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto ai Gamberi e Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Risotto ai Gamberi e Pomodoro is presented in a pristine white porcelain shallow bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. The risotto is mounded naturally, its rich, fluid consistency evident, showing hints of the vibrant red crushed tomatoes and specks of finely diced onion. Several plump, pinkish-orange seared shrimp, some whole and some halved lengthwise, are artfully placed on top of the risotto. A light scattering of freshly chopped green parsley leaves provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness. The overall composition is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. A simple silver fork and spoon rest beside the bowl on a folded cotton napkin, completing the casual bistro setting under soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto loses its creamy texture quickly.
Offer additional freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up any extra sauce.
instructions: Warm shrimp stock in a saucepan. Keep it at a gentle simmer.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add finely diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing liquid to reduce slightly.
Add one ladle of warm shrimp stock to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding stock, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each addition is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 18-20 minutes.
While risotto cooks, sear shrimp. Heat a separate pan with a splash of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add shrimp. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Risotto is ready when rice is al dente (firm to the bite) and creamy. It should be fluid, not stiff.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano. This is 'mantecatura'.
Gently fold in seared shrimp. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Let risotto rest for 1 minute before serving.
notes: Ensure shrimp stock is always warm when adding to the risotto to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring continuously is key for releasing starch from the rice, creating the creamy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Butternut Squash Macaroni and Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of creamy butternut squash macaroni and cheese fills a deep, off-white ceramic bowl. The golden-yellow macaroni, coated in a rich, velvety cheese sauce, is prominently featured, interspersed with tender, roasted orange butternut squash cubes. The surface shows melted, slightly browned cheese and a light sprinkle of golden breadcrumbs, indicating a comforting, baked finish. The dish is presented on a well-used, light wooden dining table, reflecting a homely atmosphere. A simple, casual cloth napkin in a neutral tone is placed to the side, with a silver fork resting on it. The lighting is warm and inviting, suggesting a cozy, family kitchen environment. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the hearty portion and simple, unpretentious plating, characteristic of American comfort food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel, deseed, and cut butternut squash into 2cm cubes. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized.
Cook macaroni pasta according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.
While pasta cooks, melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour to create a roux. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in milk and cream until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in cheddar cheese and half of the Parmesan until melted and smooth. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Add roasted butternut squash and cooked macaroni to the cheese sauce. Stir to combine.
Pour mixture into a 2.5-litre baking dish. If desired, sprinkle remaining Parmesan and breadcrumbs over top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbling and golden brown on top. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Beluga Lentil Curry with Mango-Mint Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A deep, earthy brown beluga lentil curry, subtly thick, fills a clean white shallow porcelain bowl. Visible flecks of diced carrot and onion are integrated throughout. Centered atop the curry is a vibrant mound of fresh mango salsa. The salsa is a mosaic of bright yellow mango small cubes, crisp green cucumber small cubes, and finely chopped fresh herbs – coriander, parsley, and peppermint. A subtle, natural sheen from a touch of balsamic vinegar enhances the salsa's freshness. The dish is placed on a simple wooden table surface. A small, clean white porcelain side bowl holds fluffy white basmati rice. A neatly folded neutral-toned cotton napkin rests beside the main bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a soft-focus modern bistro background providing a subtle, casual atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm naan bread or basmati rice.
Offer a side of plain yogurt or raita to cool the palate.
instructions: Rinse beluga lentils thoroughly under cold water. Drain.
Dice onion and carrots into small, even cubes.
Grate ginger. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion and carrots. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add grated ginger and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in curry powder, ground cumin, ground cinnamon, and paprika. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until aromatic.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Add rinsed lentils.
Bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
Season curry with salt and white pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with more broth if needed.
For the mango salsa: Dice ripe mango and cucumber into small, even cubes.
Finely chop fresh coriander, parsley, and peppermint leaves.
In a medium bowl, combine diced mango, cucumber, chopped coriander, parsley, and peppermint.
Add balsamic vinegar and lime juice. Stir gently to combine. Season with a pinch of salt.
Ladle hot lentil curry into serving bowls. Top each portion with a generous spoonful of fresh mango-mint salsa.
Serve immediately.
notes: Beluga lentils hold their shape well during cooking, providing a pleasant texture.
Adjust the amount of curry powder to suit your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Butternut Squash Ravioli with Sage Brown Butter and Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of golden butternut squash ravioli is artfully arranged on a round, matte white designer plate, showcasing a minimalist yet elegant composition. Each plump ravioli, with its delicate, thin pasta, glistens with a rich, amber sage brown butter sauce. The arrangement is organic and flowing, creating visual interest with ample negative space around the central elements. A crisp, golden-brown shard of Parmesan stands upright, providing architectural contrast and a textural counterpoint. A small, vibrant cluster of fresh green microgreens adds a precise touch of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a premium grey marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin in a precise triangle beside the plate. Dramatic, soft lighting casts subtle shadows, enhancing the textures and the sophisticated color palette of golden, amber, and deep green against the pristine white. The scene is ultra-minimalist, focusing entirely on the refined dish.
instructions: Prepare pasta dough: Combine flour, whole eggs, egg yolks, olive oil, and salt. Knead until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes. Wrap in cling film. Rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Prepare squash filling: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel, deseed, and cube butternut squash. Roast until very tender, about 25-30 minutes. Mash roasted squash until smooth. Cool completely.
Mix cooled squash with ricotta, 50 g grated Parmesan, nutmeg, salt, and black pepper. Stir well. Chill filling for 15 minutes.

Make Parmesan crisp: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Sprinkle 80 g finely grated Parmesan into a thin, even circle or rectangle. Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely, then break into shards.

Assemble ravioli: Divide pasta dough into four portions. Roll each portion very thinly using a pasta machine or rolling pin. Place small spoonfuls of squash filling about 3 cm apart on one half of the pasta sheet. Moisten edges with water. Fold the other half of the pasta over. Press around filling to seal, removing air. Cut into desired ravioli shapes (squares or rounds) using a cutter. Ensure edges are well-sealed.
Cook ravioli: Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Carefully add ravioli in batches. Cook for 3-4 minutes, or until al dente and floating. Reserve 60 ml pasta cooking water.

Prepare sage brown butter sauce: While ravioli cook, melt unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add sage leaves. Cook until butter browns and sage becomes crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Be careful not to burn. Remove sage leaves. Add reserved pasta water to the brown butter.

Finish and plate: Drain cooked ravioli. Add directly to the skillet with brown butter sauce. Gently toss to coat. Place 5-6 ravioli per plate in an organic, flowing arrangement. Spoon extra sauce over ravioli. Garnish each plate with a Parmesan crisp shard and a small cluster of microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.visual_description: The Hearty Chicken Noodle Soup is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The soup is a warm, golden-yellow hue from the broth, with generous portions of tender, shredded chicken chunks visibly suspended alongside vibrant orange diced carrots, pale green diced celery, and translucent diced onion. The egg noodles are soft and plump, intertwined throughout the hearty liquid. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley rests on top, providing a fresh contrast. The broth has a comforting, slightly opaque appearance, suggesting its rich flavor. The bowl is filled to a natural, comfortable level, with some steam gently rising. The scene is lit by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. A simple cloth napkin and a standard spoon are casually placed next to the bowl. The background is minimal, showing just a hint of a comfortable family kitchen, ensuring the focus remains on the comforting bowl of soup.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with crusty bread or crackers
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Add bay leaf. Bring to a boil.
Add chicken pieces to the boiling broth. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken from the pot. Shred the cooked chicken into bite-sized chunks using two forks. Discard bay leaf.
Return shredded chicken to the pot.
Add egg noodles to the simmering soup. Cook according to package directions, typically 7-10 minutes, until tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Lentil and Herb Fritters with Mango-Cucumber Raita
recipes.visual_description: A clean white porcelain sharing platter holds a cluster of 8-10 golden-brown, round Spiced Lentil and Herb Fritters, each approximately 5 cm in diameter. The fritters exhibit a slightly irregular, rustic shape with visible flecks of green herbs and reddish lentil texture. They are lightly drizzled with dark, glossy balsamic vinegar and clear olive oil, catching the light. Small, vibrant green fresh coriander sprigs are artfully placed among the fritters. Beside the platter, a small, elegant white ceramic bowl contains the Mango-Cucumber Raita, showing creamy white yogurt with distinct, finely diced yellow mango and green cucumber cubes. The setting is a simple wooden table, illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting from the side, creating gentle shadows. A neutral-colored cotton napkin rests beside the serving ware. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere, focusing entirely on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a shared appetizer or snack.
Can be accompanied by other Indian chutneys or dips.
instructions: Rinse lentils thoroughly. Place in a saucepan with 500ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, until lentils are tender but hold their shape. Drain well.
In a large bowl, combine cooked lentils, chopped red onion, minced garlic, grated ginger, chopped coriander, parsley, basil, and peppermint.
Add curry powder, cumin, cinnamon, and white pepper. Mix well.
Add egg and flour to the lentil mixture. Season with salt. Mix until just combined.
Form into 12-16 small, flat fritters, about 4-5 cm in diameter.
Heat 2-3 cm of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry fritters in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
In a separate bowl, combine yogurt, diced cucumber, diced mango, and finely chopped peppermint.
Season with white pepper and salt. Stir gently.

Arrange fritters on a serving platter. Serve immediately with the mango-cucumber raita on the side. Drizzle fritters lightly with balsamic vinegar and olive oil. Garnish with fresh coriander or basil sprigs.
notes: Ensure lentils are well-drained after cooking to prevent soggy fritters.
Do not overcrowd the pan when frying to maintain oil temperature and ensure even browning.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Lentil and Mango Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Spiced Lentil and Mango Curry is centrally mounded on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, orange-yellow curry highlights the soft texture of cooked red lentils, topped with a subtle swirl of white coconut cream. Vibrant small diced cubes of firm mango and crisp small diced cucumber provide fresh contrast. A generous sprinkle of fresh chopped coriander finishes the dish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table. A small white bowl of fluffy basmati rice and a folded piece of warm naan bread are placed beside the main plate. A grey cotton napkin is neatly folded. Natural, even lighting creates a modern bistro atmosphere with an authentic Indian culinary touch.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed basmati rice.
Accompany with warm naan bread.
Offer a side of plain yogurt or raita.

ingredients.name: Fresh Coriander
ingredients.quantity: 30 g, chopped, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Rinse lentils thoroughly under cold water.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion, grated ginger, and minced garlic. Sauté until onion is softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in curry powder, ground cumin, white pepper, and cinnamon stick. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, salt, and sugar to the pot. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender and liquid is absorbed, stirring occasionally.
Remove cinnamon stick. Stir in half of the diced mango and the white vinegar.
Fold in chopped fresh coriander, parsley, peppermint, and basil.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. The curry should be creamy but not dry.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Brie-White Chocolate Emulsion and Passion Fruit Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared beef medallions is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two thick, oval-shaped beef medallions, showcasing a deep golden-brown crust from searing and a tender, rosy interior, are centrally placed. A rich, golden-orange passion fruit jus is elegantly pooled beside and slightly beneath the beef, its glossy surface reflecting light. A creamy, off-white brie-white chocolate emulsion is artfully drizzled in delicate lines over the beef and the jus, adding a contrasting texture and color. A vibrant green and off-white cashew-mint gremolata, composed of roughly chopped toasted cashews and finely chopped fresh mint leaves, is sprinkled generously over the beef and around the plate, providing a fresh, crunchy element. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork and knife and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional, inviting appearance against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Prepare Cashew-Mint Gremolata: Roughly chop cashews and mint. Combine with lemon zest. Set aside.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness. Transfer beef to a plate, tent with foil, and let rest for 5 minutes.
For the Passion Fruit Jus: In the same skillet, add finely diced shallot and minced garlic. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes.

Deglaze skillet with 100 ml white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Add beef stock and passion fruit pulp. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve for smoothness, if desired. Keep warm.
For the Savory Brie-White Chocolate Emulsion: In a small saucepan, combine remaining 100 ml white wine and a pinch of culinary lavender. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half. Remove from heat.

Add cubed brie and white chocolate to the reduced wine. Whisk constantly until cheese and chocolate are melted and smooth. Gradually whisk in 30 g cold unsalted butter, one piece at a time, to emulsify. Season with a tiny pinch of salt if needed. Keep warm, but do not boil.
To plate: Place 2 seared beef medallions on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of Passion Fruit Jus around the beef. Drizzle the Savory Brie-White Chocolate Emulsion artfully over the beef and jus.
Sprinkle the Cashew-Mint Gremolata over the beef and sauces. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Mexican Beef and Potato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous single serving of Spicy Mexican Beef and Potato Pasta is presented in a clean, deep white porcelain bowl. The hearty stew features rich reddish-brown sauce coating small shell pasta, substantial diced beef chunks, tender diced potatoes, vibrant orange diced carrots, and plump kidney beans. The beef is braised to a tender texture, potatoes and carrots are cooked through but retain shape. The dish has a glistening, saucy consistency. It is naturally mounded in the bowl, creating an inviting, comforting appearance. A fresh scattering of bright green chopped cilantro provides a vibrant color contrast. A lime wedge rests on the bowl's rim. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. A small stack of warm corn tortillas are placed nearby, suggesting a traditional accompaniment. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and rich colors. The background is minimal, hinting at a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer lime wedges to squeeze over the dish for brightness.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (approx. 300g), peeled and diced into 2cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef cubes in batches until seared on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally. This forms the sofrito base.
Add minced garlic, dried oregano, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and beef broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return beef to the pot. Add diced potatoes. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until beef is very tender.
Add drained kidney beans and shell pasta. Stir well. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for 10-12 minutes, stirring frequently, until pasta is al dente and sauce has thickened.
Stir in sliced pickled jalapenos and their brine. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle generous portions into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve immediately with lime wedges.
notes: Adjust cayenne pepper to your preferred spice level.
For extra richness, a dollop of sour cream or crema can be added when serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Passion Fruit White Chocolate Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden-brown exterior, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, presented as a whole, succulent piece, is generously draped with a creamy, pale yellow passion fruit white chocolate sauce, subtly flecked with tiny black passion fruit seeds. Alongside the chicken, two thick, irregular chunks of soft, creamy brie cheese are carefully placed. Fresh, vibrant green mint leaves are scattered over the sauce and around the plate, adding a burst of color and aromatic freshness. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional yet approachable presentation with moderate negative space. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter, cold, cut into cubes

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and let rest on a cutting board.
While chicken rests, add chopped shallots and minced garlic to the same skillet. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and softened.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Cut passion fruit in half. Scoop out the pulp and seeds into the skillet. Add chicken stock and 30ml water. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce liquid by one-third. Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in chopped white chocolate until it is completely melted and the sauce is smooth.
Whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, until fully incorporated and the sauce is glossy. Season sauce with salt and black pepper to taste.
Slice brie cheese into thick, irregular pieces.
Place one whole pan-seared chicken breast on each dinner plate. Generously spoon the passion fruit white chocolate sauce over and around the chicken.
Arrange the brie cheese pieces alongside the chicken on the plate. Garnish with fresh mint leaves before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Butternut Squash
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Roasted Chicken and Butternut Squash rests on a rustic, round ceramic plate with an earthy, muted tone. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is the centerpiece, positioned naturally. Alongside it are irregularly shaped, tender 2-3 cm chunks of roasted butternut squash, exhibiting vibrant orange hues and slight caramelization. Thick, tender red onion wedges, softened and slightly charred at the edges, intersperse with the squash. A few whole, creamy roasted garlic cloves are nestled among the vegetables. Freshly chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of green. The arrangement is casual, with components touching and overlapping, reflecting a homely plating style. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. A casually folded linen napkin completes the inviting, lived-in scene under warm, cozy kitchen lighting. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space around the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking tray with parchment paper.
Peel butternut squash. Cut squash into 2-3 cm chunks.
Peel red onion. Cut onion into thick wedges.
Do not peel garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, combine chicken thighs, squash chunks, onion wedges, and whole garlic cloves.
Drizzle with olive oil. Add dried rosemary, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper. Toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Spread ingredients in a single layer on the prepared baking tray. Do not overcrowd the tray.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip chicken and vegetables.
Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, squash is tender, and chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Roughly chop fresh parsley. Sprinkle over the roasted chicken and vegetables before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Brie, Passion Fruit & White Wine Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown seared chicken thigh is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, plump and whole, shows a subtle hint of creamy melted brie peeking from within. A generous pool of vibrant, glossy golden-orange passion fruit and white wine sauce surrounds the chicken, with some spooned artfully over the top. The sauce has a smooth, rich texture. Bright green, fresh mint leaves are scattered lightly over the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of contrasting color and freshness. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the dish. The setting is a modern bistro style, featuring a simple wooden table surface, standard flatware, and a folded cotton napkin positioned neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its appealing colors and textures against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Butterfly each chicken thigh. Season both sides with salt and black pepper.
Place a portion of sliced brie inside each butterflied thigh. Fold the chicken over the brie. Secure edges with toothpicks if needed.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, folded side down first, for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced shallot to the skillet. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Deglaze the skillet with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Add passion fruit pulp, chicken broth, and chopped white chocolate to the skillet. Stir until white chocolate melts.
Bring sauce to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce has slightly thickened and reduced by about one-third.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, until sauce is glossy and emulsified. Season sauce with salt and black pepper to taste.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet with the sauce. Spoon sauce over the chicken.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh mint leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Broccoli Orecchiette with Poached Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Garlic Broccoli Orecchiette is presented in a clean, white porcelain dinner bowl. The orecchiette pasta forms a gentle nest, showcasing its characteristic ear shape and creamy, light-yellow coating. Vibrant green broccoli florets and thinly sliced, tender broccoli stems are visibly integrated throughout the pasta, offering a pleasing textural contrast. A perfectly poached egg, with a glistening, soft golden yolk, rests centrally on top of the pasta. The dish is garnished with fine gratings of white Parmesan cheese and bright yellow lemon zest. The overall color palette is natural and appealing, with the creamy pasta contrasting the fresh green broccoli and the rich yellow egg yolk. The bowl is placed on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. Beside the bowl, an authentic Italian fork and spoon are neatly arranged, accompanied by a small side plate holding a slice of crusty artisan bread and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish without creating harsh shadows, emphasizing its fresh ingredients and inviting textures. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space ensuring a professional, uncluttered presentation.
instructions: Cut broccoli into small florets. Thinly slice the tender broccoli stems.
Thinly slice garlic cloves.
Cook orecchiette pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, do not brown.
Add broccoli florets and sliced stems to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if the pan becomes dry.
Pour in chicken or vegetable broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened.
