Add the drained orecchiette pasta to the skillet with the broccoli sauce. Toss to combine. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese.
Add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until the sauce reaches a creamy consistency that coats the pasta well.
Season the pasta with salt and black pepper to taste.
While the pasta finishes, poach the 4 eggs in a separate pot of simmering water for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are runny.
Divide the creamy garlic broccoli orecchiette among 4 serving bowls. Carefully place one poached egg on top of each pasta portion.
Garnish with freshly grated lemon zest and additional Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Pork Medallions with Pomme Dauphine and Port Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A refined, minimalist presentation on a pristine bone china plate with a subtle grey pattern. Three perfectly seared pork medallions, golden-brown with tender interiors, are positioned organically on one side. Adjacent, a small, artfully arranged cluster of crisp, golden Pomme Dauphine provides textural contrast. Four vibrant green asparagus spears, blanched to tender-crisp perfection, rest beside the potato. A glossy, deep ruby-red Port Wine Reduction is elegantly drizzled across the plate, connecting the components. Abundant negative space highlights each element. A single, delicate fresh thyme sprig garnishes the pork. The setting features a luxurious white Carrara marble surface with a folded white linen napkin and elegant silver flatware, under dramatic professional lighting with soft shadows.
instructions: Prepare Port Wine Reduction: Sauté shallots and garlic in a small saucepan with a touch of olive oil until softened. Deglaze with red wine and port wine. Reduce by half. Add beef stock and thyme. Simmer until sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Strain, discard solids. Keep warm.
Prepare Pomme Dauphine: Peel and cut potatoes into large chunks. Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender. Drain well. Pass potatoes through a ricer or mash thoroughly until smooth. Set aside.

Make choux pastry: In a separate saucepan, combine 100 ml water, 50 g butter, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Add flour all at once. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon over medium heat until mixture forms a ball and pulls away from the sides (about 2 minutes). Remove from heat. Beat in eggs one at a time until dough is smooth and glossy. Fold in mashed potatoes and a pinch of nutmeg. Mix until just combined.

Pipe and fry Pomme Dauphine: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 170°C. Transfer potato-choux mixture to a piping bag. Pipe small, walnut-sized portions directly into hot oil. Fry until golden brown and crispy, turning occasionally. Drain on paper towels. Season with salt.

Cook Pork Tenderloin: Season pork tenderloin generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork tenderloin on all sides until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Rest pork for 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions.

Blanch Asparagus: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add asparagus spears. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

Plate: Arrange 2-3 pork medallions artfully on one side of a large plate. Place a small cluster of Pomme Dauphine next to the pork. Arrange 4 asparagus spears alongside. Spoon a generous drizzle of the Port Wine Reduction across the plate, connecting elements. Garnish with a single fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Fermented Lentil & White Bean Spread with Root Vegetable Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist composition on a light, natural bamboo board. A handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic bowl holds the creamy, smooth, light brown fermented lentil and white bean spread, its surface subtly textured. Beside the bowl, several thin, irregularly shaped, golden-orange carrot crisps are casually arranged, some slightly curled, showcasing their delicate crispness. A few pale yellow corn crisps are interspersed, adding a contrasting texture. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space. The presentation emphasizes the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural plant elements, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic. No artificial garnishes are used; the focus is solely on the pure beauty of the ingredients.

ingredients.name: Water or reserved bean cooking liquid
Starter culture liquid (e.g., sauerkraut juice or whey)

instructions: Soak cannellini beans overnight. Drain and rinse.
Cook soaked beans in fresh water until very soft, about 1 hour. Reserve cooking liquid. Drain beans.
Rinse red lentils. Cook lentils in water until very soft, about 15 minutes. Drain.
Combine cooked beans, lentils, pitted dates, reserved bean cooking liquid (or water), and sea salt in a blender. Blend until very smooth. Adjust liquid for desired consistency.

Stir in starter culture liquid. Transfer mixture to a clean jar. Cover loosely. Allow to ferment at room temperature for 4-6 hours, or until a subtle tangy flavor develops. Refrigerate after fermentation.
Wash carrots. Use a mandoline or sharp knife to slice carrots very thinly, 1-2 mm thick. Save carrot peels for stock.
Blanch corn kernels for 2 minutes. Drain well.
Arrange carrot slices and corn kernels in a single layer on baking sheets lined with parchment paper.
Bake at 120°C (250°F) for 45-60 minutes, or until crisp and lightly golden. Turn halfway. Cool completely.
Serve fermented lentil and bean spread in a small bowl. Arrange carrot and corn crisps around the bowl.
notes: Ensure fermentation time is short for a subtle tang, or longer for a more pronounced flavor, adjusting to taste and temperature.
Carrot peels can be added to a vegetable stock pot for zero waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Butternut Squash with Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken and butternut squash is presented on a round, rustic ceramic plate with a cream glaze. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, with crispy skin, sits slightly off-center. Beside it are generous, irregularly shaped chunks of butternut squash, roasted to a deep golden-orange with caramelized edges and creamy interiors. Thick, tender wedges of roasted red onion and a few smashed garlic cloves are interspersed. Components are naturally arranged, touching and overlapping, forming a comforting mound. Charred rosemary and thyme leaves cling to the vegetables. The plate rests on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded off-white linen napkin and standard silver flatware are casually placed. Warm light from a kitchen window illuminates the scene, highlighting textures. The background is minimally blurred, showing hints of a homely kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad or crusty bread.

ingredients.name: Butternut squash
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium (approx. 1 kg), peeled, deseeded, cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine butternut squash chunks, red onion wedges, smashed garlic, olive oil, rosemary, and thyme. Toss well to coat. Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange squash mixture in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Place seasoned chicken thighs, skin-side up, on top of the squash mixture. Ensure chicken skin is exposed to crisp.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip chicken thighs. Stir squash mixture.
Continue roasting for 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and squash is tender and caramelized.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: For extra crispy skin, ensure chicken is very dry before seasoning.
Do not overcrowd the baking tray; use two if necessary.

recipes.recipe_name: German Apfelmus Meringue Törtchen
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine miniature German Apfelmus Meringue Törtchen are casually arranged on a simple, well-used, off-white ceramic serving platter. The tartlets feature golden-brown, crumbly shortcrust pastry shells, filled with a light amber, chunky apple compote made with cider. Each tartlet is topped with a generous swirl of pale golden meringue, showing soft peaks and a slightly toasted exterior. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, as if just placed on the table for a family gathering. The platter sits on a worn wooden dining table, with a casually folded, cream-colored cloth napkin nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere typical of a German home kitchen. A simple, sturdy ceramic mug, slightly out of focus, sits in the background, hinting at a Kaffee und Kuchen setting. The focus is entirely on the homely, comforting dessert, showcasing its natural textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of 'Kaffee und Kuchen' (coffee and cake) in the afternoon.
Enjoy with a cup of strong filter coffee or black tea.

ingredients.name: Apples, peeled, cored, diced (e.g., Braeburn, Honeycrisp)

instructions: Prepare the pastry dough (Mürbeteig): Combine flour, 30g sugar, and salt in a bowl. Add cold butter. Cut butter into flour with a pastry blender or fingertips until coarse crumbs form. Add cold water. Mix until dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a mini muffin tin or small tartlet molds.

Roll out chilled dough thinly on a lightly floured surface. Cut out circles to fit molds. Press dough into molds. Prick bottoms with a fork. Blind bake for 10-12 minutes, until lightly golden. Remove from oven. Let cool slightly.

Make the apple compote (Apfelmus): Combine diced apples, 50g sugar, and apple cider in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until apples are soft and liquid has reduced. Mash lightly with a fork for a chunky texture. Let cool completely.

Make the meringue: In a clean, dry bowl, whisk egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add remaining 50g sugar, one tablespoon at a time, while continuing to whisk. Whisk until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Fill cooled tartlet shells with apple compote. Pipe or spoon meringue on top of each tartlet, creating a small peak or swirl.
Return tartlets to the oven. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until meringue is lightly golden and set. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Remove from oven. Let cool on a wire rack. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Ensure the apple compote is completely cool before adding meringue to prevent it from weeping.

recipes.recipe_name: Confit Pork Belly, Pomme Purée, Carrot Emulsion, Pork Jus
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist composition on a pristine white bone china plate. A single, perfectly seared confit pork belly chunk, skin crisp and golden, rests off-center. Adjacent, a fluid swirl of ultra-smooth, creamy pomme purée forms an elegant curve. A vibrant, glossy dot of bright orange carrot emulsion provides a precise pop of color. A small pool of rich, dark pork jus is carefully spooned alongside. A delicate, irregular savory Parmesan tuile stands artfully, adding textural contrast. Abundant negative space highlights flawless execution. Finely chopped fresh chives scatter over the purée. The scene is set on light grey veined marble with dramatic professional lighting, a folded white linen napkin, and minimalist silver flatware.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served with a glass of robust red wine.
instructions: Confit Pork Belly:
Cut pork belly into 4 equal portions (approx. 250g each).
Season pork belly generously with salt, pepper, and fresh thyme leaves.
Place pork belly in a deep oven-safe dish. Add pork or duck fat until pork is fully submerged. Add 2 crushed garlic cloves and 2 thyme sprigs.
Confit in oven at 140°C for 3-4 hours, until fork-tender.
Remove pork from fat. Press pork between two trays with weight overnight in refrigerator to flatten and compact.
Before serving, score skin. Sear skin-side down in a hot pan until crisp and golden. Finish in oven at 180°C for 10-15 minutes until heated through.
Pomme Purée:
Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform 2 cm pieces.
Place potatoes in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil.
Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or a potato ricer into a saucepan.
Heat milk and 100g butter in a separate saucepan until butter is melted.
Gradually whisk hot milk-butter mixture into riced potatoes until smooth and creamy. Season with salt.
Pass purée through a fine sieve for ultimate smoothness. Keep warm.
Carrot Emulsion:
Peel carrots. Cut into small rounds.
Steam or boil carrots until very tender.
Blend cooked carrots with 50g butter, a splash of water, and a pinch of salt until perfectly smooth and emulsified. Adjust consistency with water if needed.
Pass through a fine sieve. Keep warm.
Pork Jus:
Roast pork bones/trimmings in oven at 200°C until deeply browned.
Sauté mirepoix in a pot until softened. Add roasted bones.
Deglaze with red wine. Reduce completely.
Cover with cold water. Add 1 sprig thyme, 1 clove garlic.
Simmer gently for 4-6 hours, skimming impurities.
Strain liquid. Reduce until desired consistency and flavor. Season.
Savory Parmesan Tuile:
Whisk flour, water (50ml), and melted butter (15g) until smooth. Stir in grated Parmesan.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour a small amount of batter onto the hot pan to create thin, irregular shapes.
Cook until crisp and golden, about 1-2 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool.
notes: For optimal texture, ensure pork belly is thoroughly pressed after confit.
The pomme purée should be incredibly smooth and light; do not overmix.
The carrot emulsion should be vibrant and have a slightly acidic note to cut through the richness.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Chicken Breast with Creamy Mushroom and Gruyère
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single, plump, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast positioned centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cooked whole, boasts a beautifully caramelized exterior with subtle char marks, indicating a precise sear. A delicate opening reveals a glimpse of the creamy, rich mushroom and melted Gruyère cheese filling, showcasing its inviting texture and earthy tones. The chicken breast is juicy and firm. A light, glossy pan sauce, subtly glistening, is spooned around the base of the chicken, forming a natural pool. The sauce is a warm, light brown. A scattering of vibrant green fresh thyme leaves provides a pop of contrasting color and freshness atop the chicken and within the sauce. The overall presentation is elegant and balanced, with moderate negative space on the plate, highlighting the dish as the focal point. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting that enhances the food's natural colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted asparagus or a light green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Cut a deep pocket into the thickest side of each chicken breast. Do not cut all the way through.
Heat butter and 5ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and liquid evaporates, about 5-7 minutes.
Add diced shallot to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 2 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce wine by half.
Stir in heavy cream and fresh thyme. Bring to a gentle simmer. Remove from heat.
Stir in grated Gruyère cheese until melted and combined. Season mushroom mixture with salt and pepper.
Spoon mushroom and cheese filling into each chicken pocket. Secure opening with toothpicks if needed.
Heat remaining 10ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a cutting board. Let rest for 5 minutes.

While chicken rests, add 125ml chicken stock to the same skillet. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce slightly to form a light pan sauce. Season with salt and pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuna Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuna Pasta Bake is presented in a modest oval white ceramic gratin dish, placed on a simple, well-used wooden dining table. The casserole features a golden-brown, slightly crispy breadcrumb topping. Beneath, the creamy pasta mixture is visible, showcasing penne pasta, flakes of light pink tuna, vibrant green whole peas, and small diced pieces of softened onion and celery. The texture appears hearty and comforting, with a bubbly sauce around the edges. A white ceramic plate sits underneath the baking dish. A silver fork and knife are placed casually to the right, with a folded cloth napkin to the left. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing on the comforting dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad on the side.

ingredients.name: Canned tuna in oil or water, drained

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 1-litre baking dish.
Cook pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion and sliced celery. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant. Remove vegetables from saucepan.
In the same saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove from heat. Stir in cottage cheese, salt, and black pepper. Mix until smooth.
Add cooked pasta, drained tuna, frozen peas, and sautéed vegetables to the sauce. Stir to combine thoroughly.
Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Sprinkle breadcrumbs evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and bubbly. Serve hot.
notes: This dish is great for meal preparation and reheating.
Feel free to add other cooked vegetables like mushrooms or bell peppers.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Butternut Squash Salad with Seared Chicken and Chili-Coriander Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: Perfectly uniform 1.5 cm cubes of caramelized butternut squash, golden-orange with slightly crisped edges, form the base, artfully arranged in an organic, flowing composition across a pristine white bone china plate with a wide rim. Scattered among the squash are 1 cm cubes of perfectly seared chicken, golden-brown and glistening, integrated seamlessly into the vegetable components. A vibrant green chili-coriander vinaigrette is precisely drizzled over the components, creating a subtle sheen. Toasted pumpkin seeds provide a textural contrast and visual warmth, while delicate clusters of bright green microgreens add a final touch of freshness and height. Abundant negative space surrounds the dish, emphasizing its minimalist elegance. The setting features a premium grey veined marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's textures and colors against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.

Peel butternut squash. Cut into precise 1.5 cm cubes. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread evenly on a baking tray. Roast 15-20 minutes until tender and caramelized. Let cool completely.

Cut chicken thighs into uniform 1 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes 4-5 minutes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove from pan and let rest.

For chili-garlic oil: In a small saucepan, combine 30ml olive oil, dried arbol chilis, and 2 thinly sliced garlic cloves. Heat gently over very low heat for 10 minutes; do not brown the garlic. Let cool. Strain the oil into a small bowl, discard solids.

For vinaigrette: In a separate bowl, whisk the strained chili-garlic oil, lime juice, honey, and the remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Finely chop 2 tablespoons of fresh coriander and whisk into the dressing. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a large bowl, gently combine the cooled roasted butternut squash cubes and the seared chicken cubes. Add half of the prepared vinaigrette and gently toss to coat.
To plate: Arrange the squash and chicken mixture artfully on each of 4 wide-rimmed bone china plates, leaving ample negative space for a minimalist presentation.
Garnish each plate with a sprinkle of toasted pumpkin seeds and a small, delicate cluster of microgreens. Drizzle the remaining vinaigrette around the dish.
notes: Precision in dicing both squash and chicken is crucial for a fine-dining presentation.
Avoid over-dressing; the vinaigrette should enhance, not overpower, the natural flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with White Wine, Onions, and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of French braised chicken is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh sits prominently, surrounded by tender, translucent wedges of braised yellow onion and glistening deep purple-black Kalamata olives. A rich, glossy amber-hued sauce, thickened naturally from the braise, pools elegantly around the chicken and vegetables. Scattered generously over the dish are golden-brown, crispy 2 cm croutons, adding texture. A sprinkle of vibrant fresh green chopped parsley provides a final pop of color. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and warm colors of the dish in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional crusty bread for soaking up the sauce.
Pair with a glass of the dry white wine used in the recipe.

ingredients.name: Yellow onions, cut into 8 wedges each
Crusty bread (e.g., baguette or sourdough), cut into 2 cm cubes
Dry white wine (e.g., Chardonnay or Sauvignon Blanc)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion wedges to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Add sliced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, creating a roux.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add chicken broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Return chicken to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in liquid.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is tender.

While chicken braises, preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss bread cubes with 15 ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy. These are your croutons.
Remove pot from oven. Stir in Kalamata olives and butter until butter is melted and sauce is glossy. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve chicken with braised onions, olives, and a generous spoon of sauce. Top with crispy croutons.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best flavor, use good quality dry white wine that you would enjoy drinking.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette al Pomodorini Arrosto e Ricotta Salata
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Orecchiette al Pomodorini Arrosto e Ricotta Salata is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente orecchiette pasta, resembling small ears, is generously coated in a vibrant, rustic sauce of roasted cherry tomatoes. The tomatoes are soft and slightly collapsed, showcasing their deep red hue and concentrated sweetness. Thin, golden caramelized garlic slices are interspersed throughout the dish. Fresh, torn basil leaves provide bright green accents and aromatic contrast. The entire dish is lightly dusted with finely grated white ricotta salata, adding a delicate salty tang and textural interest. The plating is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space around the pasta mound. The dish sits on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and spoon, and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating an authentic bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for soaking up the sauce.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine like Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash cherry tomatoes. Place in a large roasting dish.
Add sliced garlic, 60 ml olive oil, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper to tomatoes. Toss to coat.
Roast for 25-30 minutes. Tomatoes should burst and soften.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add orecchiette pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Before draining pasta, reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the roasting dish with tomatoes.
Add torn basil and remaining 20 ml olive oil. Add reserved pasta water gradually.
Toss everything gently to combine. Sauce should coat pasta.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with grated ricotta salata.
notes: Use ripe, sweet cherry tomatoes for best flavor.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Mushroom Risotto with Roasted Butternut Squash
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a rich, creamy Beef and Mushroom Risotto, generously portioned on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto has a fluid, flowing consistency, not dry or molded, showcasing its creamy texture from the starch and Parmesan. Interspersed within the golden-brown risotto are tender, savory chunks of seared beef and earthy, sautéed mushrooms, providing depth in color and texture. Scattered on top are vibrant, caramelized cubes of roasted butternut squash, their orange hues contrasting beautifully with the risotto. A light sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley provides a final touch of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, embodying a refined yet approachable modern bistro aesthetic. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's inviting warmth and rich textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up excess risotto.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a glass of Italian red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Prepare squash: Peel, deseed, and dice butternut squash into 2cm cubes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast 25-30 minutes until tender and caramelized.

Prepare beef: Cut beef sirloin into 2-3cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd pan. Remove beef; set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. Melt butter in the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Cook mushrooms: Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Toast rice: Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir 2 minutes until grains are translucent at edges.
Deglaze (optional): Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Cook risotto: Add hot chicken stock, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Allow each ladleful to be mostly absorbed before adding the next. Continue 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Finish risotto: Stir in 100g Parmesan cheese and seared beef chunks. Stir gently to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve: Ladle hot risotto onto individual plates. Top with roasted butternut squash cubes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan.
notes: Ensure chicken stock is hot when adding to risotto for consistent cooking.
Do not wash Arborio rice before cooking to preserve starch.
traditional_techniques: Risotto making (gradual liquid addition, constant stirring)

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Sustainable Seafood with Fermented Asparagus and Chili-Coconut Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of seared seafood is presented on a handcrafted, natural cream-colored ceramic plate, resting on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. The composition is minimalistic, highlighting the inherent beauty of each ingredient. The plate features a smooth, light green asparagus end puree at its base. Beside it, vibrant green 5 cm lacto-fermented asparagus spears are neatly arranged. Seared large shrimp, golden-crusted scallops, and tender 2 cm squid rings and tentacles are artfully placed as whole pieces atop and around the puree and spears. A creamy, pale yellow chili-coconut emulsion is drizzled elegantly over the seafood, adding a subtle sheen. Bright red halved fresh cherries provide pops of color. A fine dusting of grated, cured egg yolk adds a delicate texture and golden hue. Fresh dill sprigs or microgreens offer a final touch of verdant freshness. The overall color palette is earthy and organic, with natural variations in greens, creamy whites, and the pinks and oranges of the seafood. The setting is clean and uncluttered, with an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, casting gentle shadows. The background is minimalist, featuring a subtle, out-of-focus green plant element that reinforces the sustainable theme.

ingredients.name: Squid (cleaned, bodies cut into 2 cm rings, tentacles separated)
White chocolate (high quality, unsweetened or very low sugar)

instructions: Cure Egg Yolks: Combine 50g salt and 50g sugar. Bury egg yolks in mixture. Refrigerate 3-5 days. Rinse yolks clean. Gently dehydrate in oven at 60°C for 2-3 hours until firm. Grate before serving.

Lacto-Ferment Asparagus: Trim tough asparagus ends (reserve ends for puree). Cut spears into 5 cm lengths. Prepare brine: Dissolve 20 g salt per 500 ml water. Pack asparagus into clean jar. Cover with brine. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature 3-5 days until tangy. Refrigerate.

Make Asparagus End Puree: Simmer reserved tough asparagus ends in minimal water until very tender. Drain thoroughly. Blend with 15 g butter and 5 ml lemon juice until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Chili-Coconut Emulsion: Gently heat coconut milk in small saucepan. Add white chocolate, grated ginger, and chili flakes. Whisk until chocolate melts and mixture emulsifies. Stir in 10 ml lemon juice. Season with salt. Keep warm.
Prepare Cherries: Halve fresh cherries. Remove pits.

Sear Seafood: Pat shrimp, scallops, and squid dry. Season all seafood lightly with salt. Heat remaining butter in large pan over medium-high heat. Sear scallops 2 minutes per side until golden. Remove. Sear shrimp 1-2 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Remove. Sear squid rings and tentacles 1-2 minutes until opaque and tender. Remove.

Plate: Spoon a dollop of asparagus end puree onto the center of each handcrafted ceramic plate. Arrange fermented asparagus spears beside the puree. Artfully place seared shrimp, scallops, and squid on the plate, ensuring seafood pieces remain whole. Drizzle chili-coconut emulsion generously over the seafood. Garnish with fresh cherry halves, a sprinkle of grated cured egg yolk, and fresh dill or microgreens. Finish with a few drops of toasted sesame oil and a grating of fresh lemon zest.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Sustainable Seafood with Fermented Cherry Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of this modern sustainable dish is presented on a round, handcrafted cream-colored ceramic plate with a natural, unglazed rim, resting on a light reclaimed wood surface. Three perfectly seared, golden-brown scallops, plump shrimp, and tender squid rings/tentacles are arranged naturally. Each piece of seafood retains its whole form. Vibrant green asparagus spears, blanched to tender-crisp, are placed alongside. A glossy, deep red Cherry-Ginger Glaze, subtly speckled with chili and ginger, is drizzled over the seafood. A delicate pool of creamy Coconut-Lemon sauce contrasts at the plate's edge. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space, highlighting natural colors and textures. An undyed linen napkin and simple ceramic bowl accompany. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene.

ingredients.name: squid, cleaned, body cut into rings, tentacles kept whole
sea salt, freshly ground black pepper
green asparagus spears, woody ends snapped off

instructions: Prepare Fermented Cherries: Combine pitted cherries, water, 5g salt, sliced ginger, and pinch of chili flakes in a clean jar. Ensure cherries are fully submerged. Seal with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days until desired tanginess. Store in refrigerator.
Prepare Asparagus: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch asparagus spears for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Make Coconut-Lemon Sauce: In a small saucepan, combine coconut milk, lemon zest, and juice of 1/2 lemon. Heat gently. Whisk in egg yolk off heat to emulsify. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Cherry-Ginger Glaze: In a small saucepan, combine chopped fermented cherries, cherry brine, grated ginger, pinch of cinnamon, and pinch of chili flakes. Simmer for 5-7 minutes until slightly reduced and thickened. Stir in white chocolate until melted and smooth. Finish with 15g butter and juice of 1/2 lemon. Keep warm.
Sear Seafood: Pat shrimp, scallops, and squid dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat sesame oil and 15g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear scallops first for 2 minutes per side until golden brown crust forms. Remove.
Add shrimp to the pan. Sear for 1-2 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Remove.
Add squid rings and tentacles. Sear for 1-2 minutes until opaque and slightly curled. Do not overcook. Remove.

Plate the Dish: Arrange blanched asparagus on a handcrafted ceramic plate. Place seared seafood artfully over and around the asparagus. Drizzle the warm Cherry-Ginger Glaze over the seafood. Spoon the Coconut-Lemon sauce around the base of the dish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken and Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken thigh rests centrally on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The chicken skin is a rich golden-brown, with tender meat visible underneath. A generous mound of soft, deeply caramelized onion strands, ranging from amber to mahogany brown, is piled on top of the chicken. A glossy, dark brown braising liquid pools around the chicken, reflecting the warm light. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant contrast. The chicken thigh is presented whole, not sliced. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. Simple, everyday silver flatware is casually placed beside the plate. A loosely folded plain cloth napkin rests nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family dining area. The background is minimal, allowing the comforting dish to be the focal point, reflecting a home-cooked, unpretentious meal. Portions are modest and satisfying.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy mashed potatoes to soak up the rich sauce
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deep golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot; set aside.
Slice yellow onions thinly. Add sliced onions to the pot, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce heat to medium-low.
Cook onions slowly, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and very soft, about 25-35 minutes. They should be amber to deep brown.
Mince garlic cloves. Add minced garlic to the pot with onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the onions and broth. Ensure chicken skin is above the liquid if possible.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer pot to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from pot. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Skim any excess fat from the sauce.
Return pot to stovetop over medium heat. Simmer sauce, reducing slightly if desired, until it thickens to your preference.
Serve chicken thighs topped with caramelized onions and sauce. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The longer the onions caramelize, the deeper their flavor will be.

recipes.recipe_name: Caribbean Chicken Curry with Coconut Rice and Fried Plantains
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Caribbean Chicken Curry is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, well-formed mound of fluffy coconut rice sits on one side of the plate. Beside the rice, substantial chunks of tender chicken, approximately 4 cm, are nestled in a rich, golden-yellow curry sauce. The sauce, thick and vibrant, pools invitingly around the chicken, showcasing diced red and green bell peppers. Several golden-brown, slightly caramelized fried plantain ovals, 1 cm thick, are arranged neatly but organically next to the curry, adding a contrasting texture and color. The dish is garnished with a vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped green scallions and bright green cilantro, enhancing its freshness. A quarter lime wedge rests on the rim of the plate. The setting is a modern bistro style with a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Traditional metal flatware (fork and knife) is placed to the right of the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background that suggests a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of hot sauce (e.g., Scotch Bonnet sauce) for those who prefer more heat.
Traditionally enjoyed with a cool drink like sorrel or ginger beer.
Often served as a hearty family meal, encouraging communal dining.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs
ingredients.quantity: 600 g, boneless, skinless, cut into 4 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.quantity: 1 (optional, whole, for flavor, remove before serving)

instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with 15 g curry powder, 5 ml salt, and 2.5 ml black pepper.
Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken in batches until lightly browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the pot. Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, remaining 15 g curry powder, dried thyme, ground allspice, and bay leaf. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and coconut milk. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. If using, add whole Scotch bonnet pepper.

Return seared chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and sauce has thickened slightly. Remove Scotch bonnet pepper and bay leaf before serving.
While curry simmers, prepare coconut rice. Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.

In a medium saucepan, combine rinsed rice with 250 ml water and 200 ml coconut milk. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand covered 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Peel plantains. Slice on the bias into 1 cm thick ovals.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry plantain slices 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and slightly caramelized. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Serve curry hot alongside coconut rice and fried plantains. Garnish with fresh scallions and cilantro.
notes: For extra heat, you can prick the Scotch bonnet pepper a few times before adding it to the curry. Be careful not to break it open.
The ripeness of the plantains affects their sweetness; riper plantains will be sweeter and softer when fried.
traditional_techniques: Browning chicken to build flavor base.
Layering spices for depth in the curry.
Simmering slowly to tenderize meat and meld flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Coconut-Coffee Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared salmon fillet, approximately 180g, rests atop a generous pool of creamy, pale beige coconut-coffee sauce on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The salmon features a crisp, golden-brown skin and moist, flaky pink flesh. The sauce gently swirls around the base of the salmon, showcasing its smooth, velvety texture. Bright green fresh cilantro leaves and a thin, vibrant lime wheel are artfully placed on and beside the salmon, providing a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting, with moderate negative space around the dish. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside steamed jasmine rice.

ingredients.name: Red chili, thinly sliced (seeds removed for less heat)
Espresso powder or strong brewed coffee
Fresh cilantro or Thai basil, for garnish

instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and half of the sliced red chili. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk. Stir in espresso powder (or brewed coffee), fish sauce, and brown sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in vanilla extract. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Keep warm.
Heat remaining 15 ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crisp and golden.
Flip salmon fillets. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F) and flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Stir lime juice into the warm coconut-coffee sauce.
To plate, spoon a generous pool of sauce onto each serving plate. Place one seared salmon fillet on top of the sauce.
Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves or Thai basil and remaining sliced red chili. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee Coconut Panna Cotta with Lime-Chili Syrup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coffee Coconut Panna Cotta is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain dessert plate. The panna cotta stands in the center, a smooth, creamy, off-white cylindrical shape with a subtle sheen. A dark, glossy lime-chili syrup is artfully drizzled in a crescent curve around the base of the panna cotta, forming a small, inviting pool. A scattering of golden-brown toasted coconut-oatmeal crumble is arranged on one side, offering a delightful textural contrast with varied sized pieces. A delicate curl of lime zest garnishes the panna cotta. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface. A silver dessert spoon rests to the right of the plate, and a neatly folded white cotton napkin lies to the left. Natural, soft, even lighting highlights the dish, ensuring a professional and appealing presentation.
instructions: Soak gelatin leaves in cold water for 5 minutes. If using powder, bloom in 30 ml cold water.
Combine coconut milk, heavy cream, and 80g granulated sugar in a saucepan. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from gelatin leaves and stir into warm cream mixture until fully dissolved. If using bloomed powder, add to warm cream mixture.
Stir in espresso and vanilla extract.
Pour mixture evenly into four 150 ml ramekins or molds. Chill for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until set.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Combine rolled oats, desiccated coconut, melted butter, brown sugar, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Mix well until crumbly.
Spread crumble mixture onto a baking sheet. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Let cool completely.
For the syrup, combine lime juice, 20g granulated sugar, water, deseeded chili, sliced ginger, and coriander seeds in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until slightly thickened. Strain the syrup to remove solids. Let cool.
To serve, carefully unmold panna cotta onto individual dessert plates. Drizzle generously with lime-chili syrup. Sprinkle with toasted coconut-oatmeal crumble.
notes: Ensure panna cotta is fully chilled for best texture and easy unmolding.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Coconut-Coffee Glaze, Savory Oatmeal Pilaf, and Tomato-Lime Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared salmon fillet, with its crispy, golden-brown skin facing upwards, rests atop a neat mound of creamy, savory oatmeal pilaf. The oatmeal, a light beige, provides a subtle contrast to the rich, deep amber-brown coconut-coffee glaze artfully drizzled over the salmon and pooling slightly around its base. Alongside, a vibrant, fresh salsa made from finely diced red tomatoes, bright green coriander, and hints of red chili offers a burst of color. The salmon is presented as a whole, un-sliced piece. A few fresh coriander leaves are scattered as a garnish, adding a pop of green. The dish is centrally placed on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate.
instructions: Prepare the Coconut-Coffee Glaze: Mince 2 garlic cloves and 1 cm ginger. Finely dice half an onion and one red chili. Heat 10 ml olive oil in a small saucepan. Sauté diced onion, minced garlic, ginger, and chili until fragrant. Add coconut milk, strong brewed coffee, brown sugar, and vanilla extract. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook until the sauce thickens to a syrupy consistency, about 10-15 minutes. Season with salt. Set aside.

Prepare the Savory Oatmeal Pilaf: Finely dice the remaining half onion. Mince 2 garlic cloves and 2 cm ginger. Heat 10 ml olive oil in a medium saucepan. Sauté diced onion, minced garlic, and ginger until softened, about 5 minutes. Add rolled oats and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer until liquid is absorbed and oats are tender, about 15-20 minutes. Stir occasionally. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare the Tomato-Lime Salsa: Dice tomatoes into small cubes. Finely dice the remaining red chili. Roughly chop fresh coriander. In a small bowl, combine diced tomatoes, diced chili, and chopped coriander. Squeeze the juice of one lime over the mixture. Season with salt to taste. Mix gently. Set aside.

Cook the Salmon: Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides. Heat 10 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes until the skin is crispy and golden brown. Flip the fillets and cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C. The salmon should be flaky and cooked through.

To Serve: Spoon a generous portion of the savory oatmeal pilaf onto the center of each plate. Carefully place a pan-seared salmon fillet on top of the pilaf. Drizzle the coconut-coffee glaze over the salmon and around the plate. Spoon a dollop of the fresh tomato-lime salsa beside the salmon. Garnish with a few fresh coriander leaves and a lime wedge. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Salmon & Oatmeal Bites
recipes.visual_description: A collection of 8-10 golden-brown, rustic salmon and oatmeal cakes are casually arranged on a simple, light-colored ceramic platter, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The cakes are round and slightly irregular, showcasing their homemade nature, with visible flecks of green coriander and red chili throughout. Each cake is gently drizzled with a glossy, light caramel-colored coconut-coffee sauce, which pools slightly around their bases. A small, separate ceramic bowl of vibrant, fresh tomato salsa, with diced red tomatoes, green coriander, and white onion, sits alongside the platter. The scene is bathed in warm, natural kitchen light, suggesting a comfortable family meal. A casually folded plain linen napkin is visible in the background, adding to the homely atmosphere. The overall presentation is unpretentious, highlighting the inviting, comforting appeal of the dish. The salmon cakes are presented as whole pieces.

ingredients.name: strong brewed coffee (espresso or strong brew)

instructions: Poach or bake salmon: Place salmon fillet in a small pot with enough water to cover. Simmer gently for 8-10 minutes until cooked through. Alternatively, bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes. Drain and let cool slightly. Flake salmon into a large bowl, removing skin and bones.

Sauté aromatics: Heat 15ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and chopped chili. Cook for 2 more minutes until fragrant. Remove from heat.

Prepare salmon cake mixture: Add sautéed aromatics to flaked salmon. Add quick-cooking oats, half of the chopped coriander, lime zest, 15ml lime juice, salt, and pepper to the bowl. Mix well until combined. Form mixture into 10-12 small, bite-sized cakes (about 30g each).
Cook salmon cakes: Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Place salmon cakes in the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and heated through.

Make coconut-coffee drizzle: In a small saucepan, combine coconut milk, strong brewed coffee, and vanilla extract. Bring to a gentle simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt.
Prepare tomato salsa: In a small bowl, combine diced tomatoes, remaining chopped coriander, and remaining lime juice. Stir gently.
Serve: Arrange warm salmon cakes on a platter. Drizzle generously with coconut-coffee sauce. Serve with a side of fresh tomato salsa.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Roasted Chicken Supreme with Red Pepper Coulis, Pomme Purée, and Pickled Jalapeño Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-roasted chicken supreme, its skin a deep golden-brown and perfectly crisp, rests gracefully on a pristine white bone china plate. Beside it, a generous, fluid swoosh of velvety, off-white pomme purée creates a soft, organic curve. A vibrant, rich red roasted bell pepper and tomato coulis forms an elegant, asymmetrical pool, its smooth surface reflecting the light. Precisely dotted around the plate are tiny drops of a bright green pickled jalapeño vinaigrette, offering a sharp visual contrast and hint of piquancy. A few golden-brown, translucent crispy garlic chips are artfully scattered atop the chicken and coulis, adding texture. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing their architectural placement and refined simplicity. The scene is set on a premium grey-veined marble surface with a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and elegant composition.

ingredients.name: Chicken Supreme (skin-on, bone-in breast with wingette)

instructions: Pat chicken supreme dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Let sit at room temperature for 20 minutes.

Preheat oven to 190°C. Halve bell peppers, core and deseed. Halve tomatoes. Slice 2 garlic cloves. Toss peppers, tomatoes, and sliced garlic with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.

For the coulis: Blend roasted peppers, tomatoes, and garlic with 100ml chicken stock. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky texture. Transfer to a small saucepan. Simmer gently, reducing until slightly thickened. Season with salt, pepper, and sherry vinegar. Keep warm.

For the pomme purée: Peel and roughly dice potatoes. Place in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain thoroughly. Pass potatoes through a food mill or ricer into a clean saucepan.

Heat milk and 100g butter in a separate small saucepan until butter is melted and milk is hot. Gradually add hot milk mixture to riced potatoes, whisking vigorously until very smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For the pickled jalapeño vinaigrette: Finely mince 30g pickled jalapeños. Mince 1 garlic clove. Combine minced jalapeños, minced garlic, 30ml olive oil, and lime juice. Season with a pinch of salt.

For crispy garlic chips: Thinly slice remaining 3 garlic cloves. Heat 15ml olive oil in a small pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced garlic. Cook slowly until golden brown and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towel. Season with a pinch of salt.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken supreme skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Add thyme sprigs and 50g butter to the skillet. Baste chicken with melted butter.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven, let rest in the skillet for 5 minutes.

To plate: Create a flowing swoosh of pomme purée on one side of a large plate. Place one chicken supreme elegantly beside the purée. Spoon a generous pool of red pepper coulis next to the chicken. Drizzle the pickled jalapeño vinaigrette precisely around the plate. Garnish with a few crispy garlic chips.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Rubbed Pan-Seared Salmon with Coconut-Lime Chili Sauce and Crispy Oats
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a pan-seared salmon fillet, golden-brown and flaky, resting atop a creamy, pale ivory coconut-lime chili sauce. The salmon's surface reveals hints of a dark coffee rub, providing a textural contrast to its tender interior. Beside the salmon, a vibrant mound of diced red tomato, minced garlic, and thinly sliced red chili, interspersed with fresh green cilantro, adds a pop of color and freshness. A scattering of golden-brown crispy toasted oats provides a subtle, earthy crunch over the salmon and sauce. The composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. It is served on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. A simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin are visible, with soft, natural, even lighting. A lime wedge is placed beside the salmon, ready to be squeezed. The overall presentation is refined yet approachable, showcasing distinct colors and textures.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.quantity: 2, 1 juiced, 1 cut into wedges for garnish

instructions: Prepare Coffee Rub: Combine ground coffee, 2.5g salt, and 1g black pepper. Rub evenly onto salmon fillets.
Toast Oats: In a dry pan over medium heat, toast rolled oats until golden brown and fragrant, about 3-4 minutes. Set aside.
Prepare Sauce Base: Heat 15ml oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced red onion, 2 minced garlic cloves, and 1 thinly sliced chili. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.

Simmer Sauce: Pour in coconut milk. Add grated ginger, fish sauce, brown sugar, and vanilla extract. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.

Sear Salmon: Heat remaining 15ml oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Place salmon fillets skin-side down (if skin-on). Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy. Flip and sear for another 3-4 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 60°C (145°F) for medium.
Finish Sauce: Stir in lime juice (from 1 lime) into the coconut sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Prepare Tomato Garnish: In a small bowl, combine diced Roma tomatoes, remaining 2 minced garlic cloves, remaining 1 thinly sliced chili, and chopped cilantro.

Plate Dish: Ladle coconut-lime chili sauce onto the center of each plate. Place a pan-seared salmon fillet on top of the sauce. Spoon the fresh tomato garnish next to the salmon. Sprinkle toasted oats over the salmon and sauce. Garnish with a lime wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple & Banana Compote with Toasted Seed Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Apple & Banana Compote is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic bowl, centrally placed on a light, textured bamboo surface. The compote itself is a soft, earthy beige with visible small, tender cubes of apple and banana, indicating gentle cooking after fermentation. Its texture is naturally thick and slightly chunky. Generously scattered over the compote, and spilling gently onto the bowl's rim, is the toasted seed crumble. This crumble showcases varied textures and warm, golden-brown hues from the buckwheat groats, pumpkin seeds, and sunflower seeds, providing a striking textural contrast to the soft compote. The presentation is minimalistic, allowing ample white space around the bowl to emphasize the dish's natural beauty. A simple, clean wooden spoon rests beside the bowl. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a subtle hint of a green plant in soft focus, enhancing the sustainable, natural aesthetic. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the ingredients' natural colors and textures.

ingredients.name: Sugar (or natural sweetener like maple syrup)
Starter culture (e.g., unpasteurized kombucha, water kefir, or whey)

instructions: Wash apples. Do not peel. Core apples. Cut into 1 cm cubes.
Peel bananas. Cut into 1 cm cubes.
Combine apple cubes, banana cubes, 500 ml water, 20 g sugar, and starter culture in a large clean glass jar.
Stir gently. Cover jar loosely with a cloth or lid. Allow air exchange.
Place in a cool, dark place for 2-3 days. Fermentation is complete when small bubbles appear and a pleasant, tangy aroma develops. Taste for desired tanginess.
Pour fermented fruit mixture into a medium saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fruit softens and liquid thickens into a compote.
Remove from heat. Stir in lemon juice and vanilla extract. Adjust sweetness if desired.
Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat. Add buckwheat groats, pumpkin seeds, and sunflower seeds.
Toast for 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden brown and fragrant.
Remove from heat. Transfer to a plate to cool. Once cool, lightly crush the toasted mixture for varying textures. Do not pulverize.
Stir in a pinch of sea salt.
Spoon warm or chilled compote into individual serving bowls.
Sprinkle generously with toasted seed crumble.
notes: Use very ripe bananas for natural sweetness.
Adjust fermentation time based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.
The apple skin adds fiber and color to the compote.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Sausage Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of al dente pappardelle pasta is gently tossed with a rich, slow-cooked chicken and sausage ragu, presented in a deep, pristine white ceramic bowl. The ragu, a deep reddish-brown, features tender, diced chicken thighs and crumbled Italian sausage, infused with sweet sautéed onions, carrots, and celery, and simmered in a robust tomato and red wine sauce. A sprinkle of freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese melts slightly into the warm sauce, adding a sharp, salty counterpoint. The dish is finished with a vibrant scattering of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley and a delicate shower of golden, toasted garlic breadcrumbs, providing a delightful crunch. The presentation is rustic yet refined, set on a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin, suggesting a casual but authentic Italian trattoria experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2 cm chunks. Remove sausage casings. Crumble sausage.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add crumbled sausage. Brown sausage, breaking it up with a spoon. Remove sausage from pot; set aside. Drain excess fat, leaving 15 ml in pot.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Brown chicken chunks on all sides. Remove chicken from pot; set aside. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery (soffritto). Cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer until wine is reduced by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Return browned sausage and chicken to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, bay leaf, and dried oregano. Stir to combine.
Bring ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 1.5 hours, or up to 2.5 hours, stirring occasionally. Ragu should be thick and rich.

While ragu simmers, make toasted breadcrumbs. Pulse stale bread in a food processor until coarse crumbs form. Heat a small pan over medium heat. Add breadcrumbs. Toast, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crispy. Set aside.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Remove bay leaf from ragu. Stir Pecorino Romano into ragu. If ragu is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Add drained pappardelle directly to the ragu pot. Toss gently to coat pasta thoroughly.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped parsley and toasted breadcrumbs.
notes: The longer the ragu simmers, the more developed its flavors will be. Cook low and slow.
Adjust seasoning (salt and pepper) at the end, after cheese has been added, as Pecorino is quite salty.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Chicken & Mushroom Stuffed French Toast
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Savory Chicken & Mushroom Stuffed French Toast is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two halves of the thick, golden-brown brioche sandwich are cut diagonally and arranged to reveal the rich, creamy interior filling. The exterior crust is perfectly seared, showcasing a crisp texture. The exposed filling is a medley of tender, cubed chicken, sautéed brown cremini mushrooms, melted shredded Gruyere, and a creamy, off-white hazelnut-infused cream cheese base, flecked with bright green fresh chives and thyme. A scattering of additional chopped chives rests over the top for garnish. The plate features moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro style, with a simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its warm colors and inviting textures. Each element is arranged organically, highlighting the quality of ingredients and the refined yet approachable preparation.
instructions: Dice cooked chicken breast into small cubes. Slice mushrooms.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.

In a medium bowl, combine softened cream cheese, savory hazelnut butter, diced chicken, sautéed mushrooms, shredded Gruyere, chopped fresh thyme, and half of the chopped chives. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a shallow dish, whisk eggs and milk. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Spread a generous amount of the chicken and mushroom filling onto one slice of brioche bread. Top with another slice of brioche to form a sandwich. Repeat for all sandwiches.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Heat a large non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat. Add half of the unsalted butter.
Dip each sandwich briefly into the egg mixture, ensuring both sides are coated but not soggy. Allow excess liquid to drip off.
Place dipped sandwiches into the hot skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Add remaining butter as needed.
Transfer seared sandwiches to a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until the filling is hot and the cheese is melted.
Remove from oven. Cut each sandwich diagonally in half. Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Soy-Glazed Salmon with Asparagus and Crispy Salmon Skin
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a refined, sustainable main course. The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone, placed on a light bamboo table. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene. A single, unsliced salmon fillet, its skin crisp and golden-brown, sits prominently. A generous cluster of vibrant green, roasted asparagus spears, retaining their natural shape and slight char, is arranged alongside. A glistening, deep amber soy-miso glaze is artfully drizzled over the salmon and asparagus. Scattered across the dish are shards of golden, irregularly shaped crispy salmon skin, adding textural contrast. The composition is minimalistic, with ample negative space. Thinly sliced spring onion greens and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds provide subtle, natural garnishes. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply beside the plate. The background is clean and uncluttered, with hints of natural elements. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful arrangement and natural beauty of each ingredient.
instructions: Prepare salmon. Pat fillets dry. Carefully remove skin from salmon. Reserve skin. Season salmon fillets with salt and pepper.

Make glaze. In a small saucepan, combine soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, brown sugar, grated ginger, minced garlic, and miso paste. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook 5 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. Set aside.
Cook asparagus. Trim tough ends from asparagus. Toss asparagus with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast on a baking sheet at 200°C (390°F) for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp.

Cook salmon. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear salmon fillets flesh-side down for 3 minutes until golden. Flip salmon. Brush with glaze. Transfer pan to oven. Roast 8-10 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).

Make crispy skin. While salmon roasts, place reserved salmon skin between two sheets of parchment paper. Place another baking sheet on top to press flat. Bake at 200°C (390°F) for 10-12 minutes until golden and crisp. Break into shards.

Plate dish. Arrange roasted asparagus on handcrafted ceramic plates. Place a salmon fillet beside asparagus. Drizzle remaining glaze over salmon and asparagus. Garnish with crispy salmon skin shards. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onion greens if desired.
notes: Emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing salmon skin for a crispy garnish.
Asparagus ends can be used for stock or vegetable purees in other dishes.

recipes.recipe_name: Rye Crostini with Osetra Caviar and Dill Butter
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve exquisite canapés are artfully arranged on a large, dark grey slate or polished black granite platter. Each canapé features a perfectly round, crisp dark rye crostini, approximately 4 cm in diameter, baked to a deep golden-brown. A thin, even layer of pale green dill butter is spread across the crostini, providing a subtle color contrast. Centered atop the butter is a generous, glistening mound of Osetra caviar, its individual pearls shimmering with deep charcoal and amber tones. Each canapé is precisely garnished with a single, delicate sprig of fresh dill, adding a vibrant green accent. The composition is minimalist, with ample negative space between each piece, emphasizing the luxurious ingredients and precise execution. The platter rests on a polished dark wood table, with a pristine white linen napkin folded precisely to one side. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and sheen of the caviar.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with well-chilled vodka.

ingredients.name: Fresh dill
ingredients.quantity: 15 g, finely chopped, plus small sprigs for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F).
Cut rye bread slices into 4 cm diameter rounds. Arrange on a baking sheet.
Bake bread rounds 8-10 minutes until crisp. Let cool completely on a wire rack.
In a small bowl, combine softened butter, chopped dill, lemon zest, salt, and white pepper. Mix well.
Spread a thin layer of dill butter onto each cooled rye crostini.
Carefully spoon 4-5 grams of Osetra caviar onto the center of each buttered crostini.
Garnish each canapé with a tiny fresh dill sprig.
Serve immediately on a chilled platter.
notes: Use a non-metallic spoon (e.g., mother-of-pearl or plastic) when handling caviar to preserve its delicate flavor.
Ensure caviar is served very cold.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Salmon, Asparagus, Dashi-Soy Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly slow-cooked salmon fillet, glistening with a delicate, pale pink hue, rests off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. The salmon is a thick, succulent piece, its natural form preserved. Beside it, four vibrant green asparagus spears, precisely blanched to retain their crisp-tender texture, are artfully arranged in a flowing, natural composition. A golden, silken dashi-soy emulsion is artfully pooled beside the salmon, its rich color contrasting subtly with the white plate. A whisper of finely sliced chives provides a delicate, verdant accent atop the salmon. The presentation is minimalist with abundant negative space, highlighting the purity of each component. The plate sits on a smooth, grey-veined Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and a single piece of modern, polished silver flatware are positioned to the side. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and luxurious simplicity.
instructions: Preheat oven to 65°C. Season salmon fillets generously with sea salt and white pepper.
Place salmon fillets in an oven-safe dish. Pour olive oil over salmon, ensuring fillets are fully submerged.
Bake for 25-35 minutes, or until salmon is tender and flakes easily. Do not overcook. Carefully remove salmon from oil and drain on paper towels.

Prepare dashi: Combine kombu and water in a saucepan. Heat gently over medium-low heat until just simmering. Remove kombu just before water boils. Add bonito flakes. Simmer for 30 seconds. Remove from heat. Let steep 5 minutes. Strain dashi through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.
In a clean saucepan, combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sake. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce liquid by half, about 10-12 minutes.
Remove from heat. Gradually whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, until the sauce is emulsified and glossy. Keep warm.
Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Blanch asparagus in boiling salted water for 1-2 minutes until vibrant green and crisp-tender. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
To plate: Gently place a slow-cooked salmon fillet on a warm, minimalist plate. Arrange 4-5 blanched asparagus spears neatly beside the salmon.
Spoon a generous pool of the dashi-soy emulsion beside and slightly under the salmon. Garnish with a sprinkle of finely sliced chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Lamb Loin with Rosemary-Basil Crust
recipes.visual_description: The Roasted Lamb Loin with Rosemary-Basil Crust is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally positioned on a simple wooden table. Three thick-cut lamb medallions, each about 2 cm, display a crisp golden-brown herb crust contrasting with a tender, rosy pink interior. The lamb is arranged naturally. Roasted baby potatoes, their skins lightly crisped and golden, are artfully scattered alongside. A bundle of vibrant green beans, cooked crisp-tender, adds a fresh color element. A rich, glossy red wine jus is elegantly spooned over the lamb and around the plate, providing a deep, complementary hue. The composition is balanced with negative space, showcasing quality ingredients. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate with classic European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors against a soft, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Wash baby potatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, pepper. Roast 30-35 minutes until tender and golden.
Prepare herb crust: Finely chop rosemary leaves, basil leaves, and garlic cloves. In a small bowl, combine chopped herbs, garlic, Panko, and 30ml olive oil. Mix well.
Season lamb loin generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sear lamb loin on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side. Remove lamb from pan.
Brush seared lamb loin evenly with Dijon mustard. Press herb crust firmly onto all sides of the lamb.

Return crusted lamb to the pan. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 15-20 minutes for medium-rare (internal temperature 57-60°C). Cook to 63°C for medium (minimum safe temperature for chicken is 75°C, but this is lamb).
Remove lamb from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Rest 10 minutes, loosely tented with foil.
While lamb rests, make red wine jus: Discard excess fat from pan. Add chopped shallots to pan. Sauté 2-3 minutes until softened.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan bottom. Reduce wine by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Add beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half again, until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in 15g butter. Season jus with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Blanch green beans: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add green beans. Cook 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender. Drain. Toss with remaining 15g butter.
Slice rested lamb loin into thick medallions, about 2 cm thick. Do not fan.
Plate: Arrange 2-3 lamb medallions on each plate. Add a portion of roasted potatoes and green beans. Spoon red wine jus over and around the lamb.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Soy-Ginger Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared salmon and roasted asparagus rests on a modest, everyday ceramic plate. The salmon fillet, skin-side up, displays a golden-brown, crispy exterior, contrasting with its moist, flaky pink interior. It is presented as a whole piece. Alongside, a generous serving of bright green asparagus spears, some slightly charred from roasting, are loosely arranged. A glossy, amber-hued soy-ginger glaze lightly coats both the salmon and asparagus, pooling slightly on the plate. A sprinkle of white sesame seeds and thin slices of vibrant green spring onion garnish the dish. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen light, evoking a comfortable, lived-in family setting. A simple, slightly crumpled cloth napkin and basic flatware are casually placed nearby. The overall impression is hearty, approachable, and comforting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Steamed jasmine rice
Simple cucumber salad
instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and black pepper.
Trim woody ends from asparagus spears.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, grated ginger, minced garlic, honey, and sesame oil. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Carefully place salmon fillets, skin-side down, in the hot pan. Sear for 4 to 5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown.
Flip salmon fillets. Add asparagus spears to the pan around the salmon.
Cook for another 3 to 4 minutes, or until salmon is cooked through to your desired doneness and asparagus is tender-crisp.
During the last minute of cooking, pour half of the prepared soy-ginger glaze over the salmon and asparagus in the pan. Let it reduce slightly.
Remove salmon and asparagus from the pan. Arrange on serving plates.
Drizzle the remaining glaze over the salmon and asparagus. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust cooking time for salmon based on thickness and desired doneness. For medium-rare, cook less; for well-done, cook longer.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Tomato and Olive Spaghetti with Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a generous, elegant swirl of al dente spaghetti, glistening with a vibrant, glossy arrabbiata-style tomato sauce. The sauce, made from slow-simmered, halved cherry tomatoes, offers both rich, broken-down pieces and some still-intact, slightly caramelized halves, creating textural contrast. Dark, plump Kalamata olives, halved, are interspersed throughout, providing a striking color counterpoint. A light, even dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese covers the pasta, with a few larger, delicate shavings placed on top. Bright green, roughly torn fresh basil leaves are scattered generously, adding freshness and aromatic appeal. Served in a clean, white porcelain bowl on a simple wooden table with a folded white linen napkin and a classic silver fork.
