Spread vegetables on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. If using, toss with red wine vinegar after roasting.
Pat beef sirloin steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously on both sides with remaining 3g salt and 2g black pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place steaks in the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached (internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare).
Transfer steaks to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 5-7 minutes.
To plate, place one pan-seared sirloin steak on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of the roasted pepper-tomato-olive medley beside the steak.
Garnish each plate with shaved Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Tomatoes and Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single, succulent braised chicken thigh is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its golden-brown skin, achieved through searing, contrasts with the rich, deep red tomato sauce that generously coats and surrounds it. Interspersed within the vibrant sauce are tender, softened strips of red and green bell peppers and diced yellow onions, adding pops of color and varied textures. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a fresh garnish. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with standard polished flatware and a folded cotton napkin positioned neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting appeal and professional execution, with moderate negative space on the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce
Serve over creamy polenta or pasta like tagliatelle
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, cored and sliced into strips
Green bell pepper, cored and sliced into strips

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper strips to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine reduces by half, about 3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, dried oregano, and bay leaf. Bring sauce to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste sauce and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve chicken with a generous spoon of braised tomatoes and bell peppers. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Trout with Roasted Summer Vegetables and Dill Mustard Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate on a simple wooden table. Roasted vegetables, including golden-brown fennel wedges, vibrant red and yellow bell pepper strips, and burst cherry tomato halves, are artfully arranged. A whole, moist smoked trout fillet, with its pink-orange hue and flaky texture, rests elegantly atop the roasted vegetables. A generous, creamy pool of pale yellow dill mustard sauce is spooned beside the trout, with some drizzled over. The sauce shows visible flecks of fresh green dill. Garnish with delicate sprigs of fresh dill and small, bright green cucumber cubes, adding crisp texture and fresh aroma. The composition is balanced and inviting, with a natural arrangement. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh colors. A simple cotton napkin and standard flatware complete the modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut fennel bulbs into 2 cm thick wedges. Core and cut bell peppers into 2 cm wide strips. Halve cherry tomatoes.
On a large baking tray, toss fennel, bell peppers, and cherry tomatoes with 45 ml olive oil, 5 ml sea salt, and 2 ml black pepper.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, prepare the sauce. Finely chop 20 g fresh dill.
In a small bowl, whisk together crème fraîche, Dijon mustard, chopped dill, juice from half a lemon, 2 ml sea salt, and 1 ml black pepper.
Thinly slice remaining 10 g fresh dill for garnish. Dice 1/2 English cucumber into 0.5 cm cubes for garnish.
Gently warm smoked trout fillets for 5-7 minutes in the preheated oven alongside vegetables. Do not overcook.
To plate, arrange roasted vegetables on each plate. Place a warm smoked trout fillet on top or beside the vegetables.
Spoon generous amount of dill mustard sauce over the trout and vegetables.
Garnish with fresh dill sprigs and diced cucumber. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika White Bean Steaks with Fermented Fresno Chili Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial Smoked Paprika White Bean Steak rests centrally on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a warm beige tone. The steak, a robust disc about 2 cm thick, exhibits a rich, deep golden-brown crust. It is topped with a vibrant mound of Fermented Fresno Chili Relish, showcasing thinly sliced red Fresno chilies and finely diced red onion in a glossy, reddish-orange hue. A scattering of golden-brown, crispy onion petals, from outer layers, are thoughtfully placed, adding textural contrast and a zero-waste element. The plate’s clean, ample negative space emphasizes the dish’s simplicity and natural beauty. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, diffused natural light, creating an eco-conscious, minimalist aesthetic. The overall presentation is clean, unfussy, highlighting natural ingredients.

ingredients.name: Outer layers of 1 large yellow onion

instructions: Prepare Fermented Fresno Chili Relish (3-5 days prior): Combine thinly sliced Fresno chilies, finely diced red onion, and minced garlic in a clean jar. Dissolve non-iodized sea salt in filtered water to create brine. Pour brine over ingredients, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight. Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Store in refrigerator after fermentation.

Prepare Crispy Onion Petals: Carefully peel off the outermost intact layers of a yellow onion. Separate them into individual petals. Toss onion petals with cornstarch and a pinch of salt until lightly coated. Heat a thin layer of olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry onion petals in batches until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towel.

Prepare White Bean Steaks: In a small bowl, combine ground flaxseed and 60ml water. Stir and let sit for 5 minutes to form a flax egg. In a large bowl, mash cooked white beans until mostly smooth but still some texture remains. Heat 15ml olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add finely diced yellow onion and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add sautéed onion and garlic to mashed beans. Add flax egg, chopped parsley, nutritional yeast (if using), smoked paprika, salt, pepper, and stale breadcrumbs. Mix well until combined. Divide mixture into 4 equal portions. Form each portion into a thick, round steak about 2 cm thick.

Cook White Bean Steaks: Heat a generous amount of olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Carefully place bean steaks in hot oil. Cook for 5-7 minutes per side, until deeply golden brown and crispy.
Assemble and Serve: Place one bean steak on each plate. Top generously with Fermented Fresno Chili Relish. Garnish with crispy onion petals. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, prepare the Fermented Fresno Chili Relish 3-5 days in advance. If time is short, a quick pickled relish (using hot vinegar and sugar) can be substituted, but it will lack the complex fermented flavor.
Utilize any remaining onion trimmings, parsley stems, or bean cooking liquid for homemade vegetable stock to further minimize food waste.
This recipe is designed to be plant-forward and emphasizes using ingredients fully to reduce waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Chickpeas and Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Moroccan Braised Chicken is elegantly presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown, tender chicken thigh sits amidst a rich, aromatic stew. The stew features vibrant orange thick-cut carrot chunks, plump chickpeas, and diced tomatoes, all coated in a deep reddish-brown, spiced sauce. Freshly chopped green coriander leaves are sprinkled over the dish, with a few bright yellow preserved lemon strips offering a zesty contrast. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, showcasing the dish's hearty yet refined nature. The plate rests on a simple wooden table. A small, fluffed mound of couscous in a separate bowl, a piece of rustic Moroccan Khobz bread, and a small ceramic dish of crimson harissa paste accompany the main plate. Natural, soft lighting highlights the textures and colors, evoking a warm, inviting casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of fluffy couscous
Offer crusty Moroccan bread (Khobz) for dipping
Provide extra harissa paste on the side for those who prefer more heat

ingredients.name: Carrots, peeled and cut into thick diagonal chunks
Preserved lemon, pulp removed, rind thinly sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down first, until golden brown on both sides. This takes about 4-5 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, and cinnamon. Stir constantly for 30 seconds to toast spices.
Stir in harissa paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes, carrot chunks, chickpeas, and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Cover the pot.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in sliced preserved lemon and fresh chopped coriander during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Italian Sausage and Bell Pepper Ragu with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, rustic Italian dish presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generous dollop of creamy, golden polenta forms the base, its smooth texture contrasting with the rich, chunky ragu. The ragu features tender, browned Italian sausage pieces, not sliced, interspersed with bright red, yellow, and orange bell pepper strips and diced onion, all coated in a deep red, glistening tomato sauce. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green basil leaves provides a fresh aromatic contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano crowns the dish. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, traditional flatware, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the ragu.
Pair with a robust red Italian wine like Chianti or Montepulciano d'Abruzzo.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Break into rough chunks.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Thinly slice fresh red chili. Slice bell peppers into 1 cm wide strips.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add sausage chunks. Brown well on all sides, breaking up any large pieces. Remove sausage from pot; drain excess fat, leaving 15ml.
Add diced onion to pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes (soffritto base).
Add minced garlic and sliced fresh chili. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add bell pepper strips. Cook until slightly softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of pot (sfumare). Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and broth. Return sausage to pot.
Bring ragu to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally (lenta cottura).
While ragu simmers, prepare polenta. Bring 1 litre water (or milk/water mix) to a boil in a separate saucepan. Add a pinch of salt.
Slowly whisk in cornmeal, ensuring no lumps form.
Reduce heat to low. Cook polenta, stirring frequently, for 20-30 minutes until creamy and smooth.
Stir butter and 50g Parmigiano Reggiano into polenta. Keep warm.
Season ragu with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in fresh basil leaves just before serving.
Serve generous portions of ragu over creamy polenta. Garnish with extra fresh basil and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
notes: For extra heat, add more fresh chili or a pinch of red pepper flakes to the ragu.
The ragu can be made ahead and reheated; flavors often improve the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Stuffed Chicken Breast
recipes.visual_description: A single, plump, golden-brown seared chicken breast, oven-finished, rests centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, left whole, showcases a crispy, caramelized exterior. A light, savory pan sauce is drizzled around its base. Inside, the stuffing reveals vibrant red chopped sun-dried tomatoes, creamy crumbled feta cheese, and deep green wilted spinach. Fresh green oregano leaves are scattered artfully over and beside the chicken, adding a pop of color and freshness. The presentation is simple, professional, and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, standard modern flatware, and a cotton napkin, all under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of roasted vegetables or couscous.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Butterfly each chicken breast. Do not cut completely through.
In a small bowl, combine chopped sun-dried tomatoes, crumbled feta, chopped spinach, and minced garlic. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Divide the filling mixture evenly among the butterflied chicken breasts. Spoon filling into each breast.
Fold the chicken breast over the filling. Secure edges with toothpicks if needed.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a cutting board; tent with foil. Let rest for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add chicken broth to deglaze the pan. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Remove toothpicks from chicken. Serve chicken with a drizzle of pan sauce. Garnish with fresh oregano or basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Oven-Baked Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of roasted chicken and vegetables rests on an off-white, rustic ceramic plate. One golden-brown, skin-on chicken thigh, perfectly roasted, is positioned centrally. Around it, a medley of roasted vegetables: thick potato wedges with crisp edges, softened red and yellow bell pepper chunks, caramelized onion quarters, and burst cherry tomato halves. Vegetables are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, showcasing their varied textures and vibrant, roasted colors. A light scattering of fresh chopped parsley adds a touch of green. The plate sits on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and classic silver flatware are casually placed alongside. Soft, warm ambient light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper
ingredients.quantity: 1, cored and cut into 3 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Yellow bell pepper
ingredients.quantity: 1, cored and cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, bell pepper chunks, onion wedges, cherry tomato halves, and smashed garlic.
Drizzle vegetables with 30 ml olive oil. Season with 2g salt and 2g black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Rub chicken thighs with remaining 30 ml olive oil. Season generously with paprika, oregano, remaining salt, and black pepper.
Place chicken thighs on top of the vegetables on the baking sheet.

Roast for 30 minutes. Turn chicken and vegetables. Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Hearty Beef and Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew features tender, irregular chunks of browned beef, approximately 3-4 cm, nestled amongst soft, diced carrots (1.5 cm cubes) and creamy, diced potatoes (2 cm cubes). The rich, dark brown gravy, thickened slightly, coats all ingredients, with a gentle sheen from slow cooking. A few vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh parsley leaves are sprinkled over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The bowl sits on a well-worn, light wooden dining table. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a home kitchen. A simple, off-white linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. The overall presentation is homely, comforting, and unpretentious, reflecting a satisfying family meal.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 150g, peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in beef broth, stirring to scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef to the pot. Add bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 hours, or until beef is tender.
Add diced potatoes and carrots to the pot. Stir well.
Cover and continue to cook for 30-40 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. The stew should be thick.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Serve the risotto on a flat white porcelain dinner plate. The consistency is fluid and spreads naturally across the plate, appearing free-flowing rather than molded. The rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, creamy sauce. Large 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are distributed throughout the rice. Sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms show deep caramelization and earthy brown tones. The dish features a pale golden hue. Finely minced flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the surface. The arrangement is organic. Beside the plate sits a heavy silver spoon and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the consistency remains fluid
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Dice onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until moisture evaporates and edges brown.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the pan. Add onion and garlic.
Cook until softened but not browned.
Add rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast the grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Add 200ml warm stock. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Repeat stock additions one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is tender but firm.
Return chicken and mushrooms to the pan.
Remove from heat.
Vigorously stir in remaining 30g butter and Parmesan cheese to create a creamy emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper. Fold in chopped parsley.
notes: Keep the chicken stock at a low simmer in a separate pot to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is essential to release rice starches for a creamy texture.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C during the initial searing phase.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Chicken and Potato Bake is presented in a deep, white ceramic bowl, sitting on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features golden-brown chicken chunks, roasted to perfection, nestled among tender, rustic potato cubes. Bright orange carrot rounds and softened onion pieces are visible throughout. A rich, savory broth coats all components, reflecting the warm kitchen light. The chicken is cooked until juicy, with slightly browned edges, while the potato cubes hold their shape, offering a soft texture. The dish is garnished simply with fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley scattered over the top. The background includes a casual cloth napkin and a metal fork, emphasizing a cozy, home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of crusty bread for dipping.
Ideal for a family dinner.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt, pepper, and half the thyme.
Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Peel and chop onion into 1 cm pieces.
Peel and slice carrots into 0.5 cm thick rounds.
Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 3-4 minutes until lightly golden. Remove chicken.
Add onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add garlic and remaining thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add diced potatoes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Uncover the pot. Bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Check seasoning. Adjust as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: This dish is excellent for meal prepping.
Leftovers can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Parmesan with Penne Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-fried chicken breast, its crisp exterior contrasting with the melted, bubbling mozzarella and vibrant red marinara sauce topping. The chicken is placed centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. Beside it, a neat mound of al dente penne pasta, lightly coated in the same rich marinara. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the chicken and pasta, adding a pop of color and freshness. The sauce glistens invitingly. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, with natural, even lighting. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with garlic bread for dipping in the marinara sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness.
Set up a dredging station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten eggs, one with Panko breadcrumbs seasoned with salt, pepper, and 25g Parmesan.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, then egg, then Panko, pressing to coat fully.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Pan-fry chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Transfer to the prepared baking sheet.
In the same skillet, add remaining 30ml olive oil. Sauté diced onion over medium heat until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
While sauce simmers, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Top each cooked chicken breast with a generous ladle of marinara sauce. Arrange sliced mozzarella over the sauce.
Bake chicken in the preheated oven for 8-10 minutes, or until mozzarella is melted and bubbly.
Toss drained penne pasta with some of the remaining marinara sauce. Arrange pasta on plates. Place a baked chicken breast beside the pasta.
Garnish with fresh basil and a sprinkle of remaining Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Pounding the chicken to an even thickness ensures even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Gratin with Cheesy Broccoli and Peas
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of golden-brown Chicken and Potato Gratin is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin has a visibly bubbling, melted cheese crust with hints of roasted potato edges peeking through. Within the gratin, distinct layers are visible: tender, thinly sliced potatoes, seared chicken chunks, vibrant green broccoli florets, and bright green peas are suspended in a creamy, rich sauce. The chicken is cut into substantial, irregular chunks, not sliced. The dish exhibits a harmonious blend of creamy textures from the sauce, softness from the potatoes and vegetables, and a slight crispness from the baked cheese topping. The setting features a simple wooden table surface with a natural finish. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its inviting warmth and textures.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs
Gruyere or sharp cheddar cheese, grated

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel potatoes. Thinly slice potatoes into 2-3mm rounds. Place in cold salted water.
Dice chicken into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook thoroughly to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Finely dice onion. Mince garlic. Add onion and garlic to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Drain potatoes. In a large pot, blanch broccoli florets and green peas in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain immediately. Refresh in ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
Melt butter in a separate saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Remove sauce from heat. Stir in grated cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg.
Lightly grease a 20x30 cm gratin dish.

Layer half of the thinly sliced potato rounds in the prepared dish. Top with half of the sautéed onion and garlic mixture. Distribute half of the seared chicken chunks over the layer. Scatter half of the blanched broccoli florets and green peas. Pour half of the cheese sauce evenly over the layers.
Repeat the layering with the remaining potatoes, onion-garlic mixture, chicken, broccoli, peas, and cheese sauce.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the top is golden and bubbly. Cover with foil if browning too quickly.
Let gratin rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beer-Braised Short Ribs
recipes.visual_description: Two generously sized, dark mahogany braised beef short ribs, presented as whole, tender chunks, are carefully placed upon a creamy, golden yellow bed of polenta. The dish is centered on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. A glossy, rich, dark brown braising sauce, reduced to a luscious consistency, is elegantly drizzled over and around the ribs, catching the light. A small, vibrant cluster of fresh, finely chopped green chives garnishes the top, offering a bright color contrast. The plate rests on a simple light wood table surface. A folded grey linen napkin is positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating soft highlights and shadows, with a subtly blurred, inviting restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread for dipping in the rich sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F).
Pat short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add beef broth, hot sauce, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Stir to combine.
Return seared short ribs to the pot. Ensure ribs are mostly submerged in liquid.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Braise for 3 to 3.5 hours, or until short ribs are fork-tender.
Remove short ribs from the pot. Set aside. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids.
Skim any excess fat from the surface of the sauce.
Place saucepan over medium-high heat. Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce until thickened to desired consistency.
Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot short ribs over creamy polenta. Spoon generous amounts of reduced sauce over the ribs. Garnish with fresh chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Cucumber Peanut Noodle Salad with Crispy Tofu
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing a vibrant medley of colors and textures. Light beige rice vermicelli noodles form the base. Bright green julienned cucumber, orange julienned carrots, thin red bell pepper strips, and finely shredded purple cabbage are interwoven throughout, creating a dynamic, colorful composition. Golden-brown, crispy tofu cubes, 1.5 cm, are strategically placed on top for textural contrast. A creamy, light brown peanut dressing is visibly drizzled over. The dish is finished with vibrant green sliced green onions, fresh cilantro leaves, and roughly chopped roasted peanuts, adding freshness and crunch. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table. Dark wooden chopsticks are neatly placed on a ceramic rest. A white cotton napkin is folded beside. Natural, even lighting highlights freshness, with a softly blurred casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges on the side for added zest.
Offer additional chili sauce for those desiring more heat.
Traditionally eaten with chopsticks.
instructions: Press tofu to remove excess water. Dice into 1.5 cm cubes. In a bowl, toss tofu with cornstarch, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1 tsp sesame oil.
Heat 2 tbsp neutral oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes to the hot pan. Cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Remove crispy tofu from pan and set aside.
Cook noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking, then drain again thoroughly.

Prepare dressing: In a medium bowl, whisk together peanut butter, remaining 60ml soy sauce, rice vinegar, lime juice, 15ml sesame oil, grated ginger, minced garlic, chili garlic sauce, and brown sugar (if using). Gradually whisk in warm water until the dressing reaches a smooth, pourable consistency.
Julienne the cucumber and carrots. Thinly slice the red bell pepper. Finely shred the red cabbage. Thinly slice the green onions and roughly chop the cilantro and roasted peanuts.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooked noodles, julienned cucumber, julienned carrot, thinly sliced red bell pepper, and shredded red cabbage.
Pour most of the prepared dressing over the noodle and vegetable mixture. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Divide the salad among four serving bowls. Top each portion generously with the crispy tofu cubes.
Garnish each bowl with sliced green onions, chopped fresh cilantro, and chopped roasted peanuts. Serve immediately.
notes: For extra crispness, air fry tofu at 200°C for 15-20 minutes, flipping halfway, after coating with cornstarch.
Dressing can be made ahead and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pineapple & Salami Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. A mound of golden-hued fusilli pasta is loosely arranged in the center, allowing for natural negative space on the plate. Interspersed within the pasta are tender, dark green wilted kale leaves and translucent, pale yellow chunks of fermented pineapple. Small, reddish-brown crispy salami cubes are visible throughout, providing textural contrast. The pasta is coated in a light, emulsified sauce, giving it a subtle sheen. A scattering of golden, irregular crispy pasta bits rests on top, adding a textural highlight. The overall composition is clean, minimalistic, and celebrates the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The plate sits on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a natural beige undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the purity of the ingredients.

ingredients.name: Seasonal greens (e.g., kale, spinach, or broccoli rabe)
Broken pasta pieces or small dry pasta bits

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Before draining, reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced salami. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove crispy salami with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
In the same skillet with rendered salami fat, add broken pasta bits. Fry until golden and crispy. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the skillet. Add sliced garlic and chili flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add chopped seasonal greens. Sauté until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Add drained fermented pineapple chunks to the skillet. Stir gently.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet. Pour in 150 ml reserved pasta water. Toss well to combine.
Continue to toss over medium heat, allowing sauce to emulsify and coat pasta. Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Stir in crispy salami. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with crispy pasta bits.
notes: To quick-ferment pineapple: Dice pineapple. Place in a clean jar. Cover with a brine (15g salt per 500ml non-chlorinated water). Ensure pineapple is submerged. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chia-Crusted Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chia-crusted chicken breast rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is a whole, substantial piece, exhibiting a beautiful golden-brown, textured crust with a crisp appearance. Beside it, vibrant green roasted asparagus spears are neatly arranged. A vibrant, smooth red pepper coulis is artfully pooled on the plate, adding striking color contrast. The dish is garnished with finely chopped fresh parsley. The composition is balanced and professional with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table. A cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors against a soft, casual background.
instructions: Prepare red pepper coulis: Halve and deseed red bell peppers. Place skin-side up on a baking tray. Roast in oven at 200°C for 20 minutes until skin blisters. Remove, cover with foil, and let steam for 10 minutes. Peel skins.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add shallot and cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook 1 minute. Add peeled red pepper flesh and chicken stock. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Transfer coulis mixture to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky texture. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten egg in a second, and chia seeds in a third.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, allowing excess to drip off. Press firmly into chia seeds, ensuring a thick, even crust on both sides.
Roast asparagus: Toss trimmed asparagus spears with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast in oven at 200°C for 10-12 minutes until tender-crisp.
Sear chicken: Heat remaining 30ml olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chia-crusted chicken breasts to hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Use a meat thermometer.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes.

Plate dish: Place one chicken breast on each plate. Arrange a portion of roasted asparagus alongside. Spoon red pepper coulis artfully next to chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Arrabbiata con Penne
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo Arrabbiata con Penne is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, resting on a simple wooden table. Al dente penne pasta is generously coated in a rustic, deep red tomato sauce with visible specks of finely minced garlic and chili flakes. Seared chicken thigh chunks, golden-brown and irregular in shape, are interspersed throughout the pasta. Halved vibrant red cherry tomatoes add bursts of color and freshness. The dish is garnished with a scattering of freshly chopped bright green parsley leaves. A light dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese covers some of the pasta and chicken. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish. A silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese
Offer crusty bread for 'scarpetta' (sopping up the sauce)
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Finely dice the onion. Mince the garlic. Thinly slice the red chilies, removing seeds for less heat if desired.
Add onion to the same skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook for 15 minutes.
While sauce simmers, cook penne according to package instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml of pasta water.
Halve the cherry tomatoes. Add them to the sauce with the seared chicken chunks. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing chicken to finish cooking through.
Add drained penne to the sauce. Toss to coat. Add reserved pasta water if needed to adjust consistency.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half into the pasta. Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to your preferred spice level. For a milder dish, use less chili or remove all seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Lemon Herb Butter and Asparagus
recipes.special_requests: simple, very high quality ingredients, a dish that hasnt changed in 50 years
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared salmon is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The salmon fillet features a beautifully crispy, golden-brown skin on top, contrasting with its tender, flaky, pale pink flesh. Alongside, a neat cluster of vibrant green, tender-crisp asparagus spears is arranged. Small, creamy, lightly smashed new potatoes, some with their skins on, are placed next to the asparagus. A glossy, pale yellow lemon-herb butter sauce is drizzled over the salmon and vegetables, with flecks of fresh green parsley and dill visible. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits nearby, ready for squeezing. The overall presentation is clean and elegant, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware, under natural, even lighting, creating a classic bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Wash and halve new potatoes. Place in a pot with cold, salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook for 15 minutes or until tender. Drain well.
Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Set aside.
Pat salmon fillets thoroughly dry with paper towel. Season both sides generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place salmon fillets, skin-side down, in the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes until the skin is golden brown and crispy.

Flip salmon fillets. Add butter, the juice of half a lemon, chopped parsley, and chopped dill to the skillet. Tilt the pan and spoon the melted butter mixture over the salmon repeatedly for 1-2 minutes.
Transfer the skillet with the salmon to the preheated oven. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until salmon reaches desired doneness (internal temperature 63°C/145°F for medium-rare).
While salmon bakes, steam or blanch asparagus in salted water for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Add a small knob of butter, salt, and pepper to the cooked potatoes. Lightly smash some potatoes with a fork for texture.

Plate one salmon fillet per dish. Arrange asparagus spears and smashed new potatoes alongside. Spoon the lemon herb butter sauce from the skillet over the salmon and vegetables. Garnish with a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Fermented Salmon & Crispy Pepperoni Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thai-inspired pasta is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, resting on a light, naturally textured bamboo placemat on a reclaimed wood table. The linguine pasta is gently coiled into a loose nest, coated in a glistening, light brown tamarind-lime sauce. Tender-crisp julienned red bell pepper and vibrant green bok choy leaves are naturally interspersed throughout the pasta, adding pops of color and fresh texture. Two substantial, golden-brown seared fermented salmon chunks, with their skin crisped, are placed prominently and organically on top of the pasta. A scattering of dark red, irregularly shaped crispy pepperoni crumbles adds a contrasting texture and deep hue. The dish is garnished with bright green, roughly chopped cilantro and thin slices of red chili, offering a final touch of freshness and subtle heat. The overall plating is minimalistic, with generous white space around the food, highlighting the pure beauty and natural colors of each ingredient. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, casting gentle shadows. In the background, an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone and a subtle hint of green foliage from a plant provide a clean, organic backdrop. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined restaurant portion with an emphasis on natural, unfussy composition.
instructions: Prepare fermented salmon: Pat salmon dry. Mix sea salt and brown sugar. Rub mixture generously over salmon flesh. Place salmon skin-side down in a non-reactive dish. Cover. Refrigerate for 24-36 hours. Rinse salmon thoroughly under cold water. Pat very dry. Cut into 3 cm thick chunks.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 125 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.

Crisp pepperoni: Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add pepperoni slices. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove pepperoni with a slotted spoon. Place on paper towels to drain. Crumble once cool. Reserve rendered pepperoni fat in the skillet.

Cook salmon: Add vegetable oil to the skillet with pepperoni fat, if needed. Sear salmon chunks skin-side down for 4 minutes until skin is crispy. Flip. Cook for 2-3 minutes until internal temperature reaches 60°C. Remove salmon. Set aside.

Sauté aromatics and vegetables: In the same skillet, add garlic and shallots. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Add red bell pepper. Stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add bok choy leaves. Cook until just wilted.
Make sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together tamarind paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice until palm sugar dissolves.
Combine: Add cooked pasta to the skillet with vegetables. Pour in the sauce. Add reserved pasta water. Toss to coat the pasta evenly. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Serve: Divide pasta among four plates. Arrange seared salmon chunks on top. Sprinkle generously with crispy pepperoni crumble, fresh red chili slices, and chopped cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Corn Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of golden-brown, pan-fried fritters is presented on a round, light-colored ceramic plate. Two to three generously sized, irregularly shaped fritters are stacked casually. The exterior is crisp, revealing a soft interior with visible shredded chicken pieces, bright yellow corn kernels, and flecks of red chili. The natural colors are warm and inviting. Beside the fritters, a small, rustic ceramic bowl holds a creamy, pale orange-red chili-lime dipping sauce. The overall arrangement is organic and unforced, as if served directly from a home kitchen. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, with soft, warm lighting illuminating the dish. A casually placed simple cloth napkin completes the homely scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a comforting starter. Pairs well with a casual family meal.

ingredients.name: Canned or frozen corn kernels, drained

instructions: Shred cooked chicken breast into small pieces.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg and milk.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in shredded chicken, corn kernels, and finely diced red chili.
Heat vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon 2-3 tablespoons of batter per fritter into the hot oil. Flatten slightly.
Cook 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Transfer cooked fritters to a plate lined with paper towel to drain excess oil.
For the dip: Combine mayonnaise, lime juice, and chili powder in a small bowl. Stir well.
notes: Adjust the amount of red chili to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli and Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Broccoli and Rice Salad is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The salad is arranged casually, with components naturally overlapping, as if served in a family kitchen. Bright green, bite-sized broccoli florets are mixed with fluffy, off-white cooked Basmati rice. Interspersed throughout are small, uniform cubes of sharp orange cheddar cheese and tiny, delicate dices of purple-red red onion, adding pops of color and texture. A light, glossy vinaigrette glistens, coating the ingredients evenly. The composition is loose and inviting, showcasing the fresh, wholesome ingredients. The plate is adequately filled but not overcrowded, allowing for some negative space. Warm, natural light from a kitchen window illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural colors. A simple, folded cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate, completing the homely setting.
instructions: Cook Basmati rice according to package directions. Let it cool completely.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add chopped broccoli florets. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately drain and plunge broccoli into ice water to stop cooking. Drain very well and pat dry.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper until dressing is emulsified.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled rice, blanched and dried broccoli, diced cheddar cheese, and finely diced red onion.
Pour the prepared vinaigrette over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to ensure all components are evenly coated.
Serve immediately, or chill for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Garlic Chili Chicken Noodles
recipes.visual_description: The Spicy Garlic Chili Chicken Noodles are presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing a generous single serving. Glistening egg noodles, coated in a rich, savory dark sauce, form a neat, organic mound. Interspersed throughout are golden-brown chunks of pan-seared chicken, each piece tender and slightly caramelized. Vibrant slices of red bell pepper and bright green spring onion pieces add pops of color and crisp texture. The dish is artfully garnished with a scattering of fresh, finely chopped cilantro and a few thin, bright red chili slices, indicating its savory heat. The overall composition is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space around the central dish. The textures are varied: tender chicken, firm noodles, and crisp-tender vegetables. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's appealing colors. It rests on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a pair of elegant chopsticks beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks
Offer a small side dish of pickled daikon or cucumber for contrast
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2.5 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook egg noodles according to package directions. Drain well.
Combine soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, chicken broth, and sesame oil in a small bowl. Stir in cornstarch slurry.
Heat 15ml cooking oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add chicken. Stir-fry 5-7 minutes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from wok.
Add remaining 15ml oil to wok. Add minced garlic, thinly sliced red chilies, and white parts of spring onions. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add thinly sliced red bell pepper. Stir-fry 2 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return cooked chicken to wok. Add cooked noodles and sauce mixture.
Toss well to coat all ingredients. Stir-fry 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens and coats noodles.
Stir in green parts of spring onions.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and extra chili slices.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Ham and Chili Macaroni Bake
recipes.visual_description: A generous, comforting portion of Cheesy Ham and Chili Macaroni Bake fills a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The top crust is a rich golden-brown, with visible crispy edges from the baked cheese and breadcrumbs. Underneath, creamy, thick macaroni noodles are coated in a vibrant, molten cheddar cheese sauce. Scattered throughout are tender, small cubes of savory ham and subtle flecks of red chili powder, indicating a gentle warmth. The dish is presented on a well-worn wooden dining table, suggesting a home kitchen setting. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard fork rest beside the bowl. Warm, inviting lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's hearty and appealing texture. The overall impression is one of simple, satisfying comfort food, ready to be enjoyed.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Serve with a side of steamed green beans.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook macaroni according to package directions. Drain.
Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk. Cook until thickened, stirring.
Remove from heat. Stir in shredded cheese, chili powder, salt, and pepper until melted and smooth.
In a separate pan, sauté diced onion until soft.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced ham. Cook 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Combine cooked macaroni, ham mixture, and cheese sauce in a large bowl. Mix well.
Transfer mixture to a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and golden brown on top.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli Chicken Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous, unpretentious portion of Broccoli Chicken Salad is presented in a large, shallow, white ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The vibrant green, bite-sized broccoli florets are the dominant visual, interspersed with small, even cubes of cooked chicken breast. Thinly diced red onion provides subtle purple accents, while small, irregular cubes of sharp yellow cheddar cheese add color and texture. Scattered throughout are plump, deep red dried cranberries and golden-brown toasted sunflower seeds, offering contrasting textures and pops of color. The creamy, off-white dressing lightly coats all ingredients, creating a cohesive, comforting appearance without being overly sauced. The salad is casually mounded, allowing some components to naturally overlap. The scene is set on a well-used, light wooden dining table, with a simple blue and white checkered cloth napkin placed casually beside the bowl. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the dish, emphasizing its fresh, homely appeal. A standard metal fork rests beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Often served at potlucks, barbecues, or as a side dish with grilled meats or sandwiches.
instructions: Wash broccoli. Cut into small, bite-sized florets.
In a large bowl, combine broccoli florets, diced cooked chicken, finely diced red onion, cheddar cheese cubes, dried cranberries, and toasted sunflower seeds.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, granulated sugar, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently until all ingredients are evenly coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Serve chilled.
notes: For best flavor, prepare ahead and chill.
Adjust sweetness of dressing to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, classic white porcelain bowl. Long strands of pappardelle pasta are generously coated and intertwined with a rich, deeply colored beef ragu. The ragu features tender, browned beef mince mixed with finely diced soffritto vegetables—onion, carrot, and celery—creating a hearty, textured sauce that clings beautifully to the pasta. The sauce boasts a vibrant, earthy red hue from slow-cooked tomatoes, punctuated by hints of green from dried oregano. A scattering of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese forms a delicate white layer over the top, melting slightly into the warm ragu. Several fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully placed on top as a garnish, providing a pop of color and aromatic contrast. The overall impression is one of rustic elegance and comforting abundance. The bowl sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, bathed in soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese.
Offer crusty Italian bread for soaking up the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine.
instructions: Finely dice onion, carrot, and celery for the soffritto.
Mince garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef mince. Brown thoroughly, breaking it apart with a spoon. Cook until no pink remains. Drain any excess fat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Reduce heat to medium. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables soften and onion is translucent.
Stir in minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer until wine is mostly evaporated, about 5 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Stir to combine.
Bring the ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover partially and cook for at least 2 hours, or up to 3 hours, stirring occasionally. The sauce should thicken and flavors should meld.
Season the ragu with salt and black pepper to taste.
Just before serving, cook pappardelle pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add it directly to the ragu. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately in deep bowls, garnished with fresh basil leaves and freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality beef mince with around 15-20% fat content.
San Marzano tomatoes are recommended for authentic Italian flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Onion and Goat Cheese Tart
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous wedge of the Caramelized Onion and Goat Cheese Tart is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pastry crust is golden and visibly flaky, supporting a rich, deep amber layer of slowly caramelized onions. Scattered atop the onions are creamy white chunks of goat cheese, some lightly browned from baking. The custard filling is set, with flecks of green thyme visible. A small, vibrant sprig of fresh thyme rests elegantly beside the tart on the plate. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and warm colors. Traditional flatware is neatly arranged beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Slice onions thinly.
Melt butter and olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat.
Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and very soft. Do not rush.
Stir in balsamic vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside to cool slightly.
Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Roll out puff pastry onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Score a 1 cm border around the edge, but do not cut through. Prick the inside base with a fork.
Spread cooled caramelized onions evenly over the pricked pastry base, staying within the border.
Crumble half the goat cheese over the onions.
Whisk eggs and cream in a bowl. Stir in chopped thyme, salt, and pepper.
Pour egg mixture carefully over the onions and goat cheese.
Sprinkle remaining goat cheese on top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until pastry is golden and filling is set and lightly browned.
Let tart cool for 5-10 minutes before slicing into 4 wedges.
notes: Slow caramelization of onions is crucial for flavor development.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Oven-Roasted Chicken and Herb Vegetables
recipes.special_requests: в духовке, с тимьяном и орегано
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of oven-roasted chicken and vegetables is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic dinner plate, centered on a rustic wooden dining table. A golden-brown, skin-on chicken thigh, its surface slightly crisped, rests amidst a colorful medley of roasted vegetables. Surrounding the chicken are thick potato wedges, their edges caramelized to a deep golden hue, alongside tender, sweet bell pepper strips (red and yellow), and softened onion wedges. Scattered among them are plump, burst cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly wrinkled from roasting. The dish is lightly garnished with fresh, chopped parsley, adding a touch of green. The overall arrangement is casual and natural, reflecting a homely, comforting meal. A simple metal fork and knife rest beside the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the inviting textures and natural colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs or drumsticks
Bell peppers
ingredients.quantity: 2 (e.g., red, yellow), cored and cut into thick strips

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
In a large mixing bowl, combine chicken pieces, potato wedges, onion wedges, bell pepper strips, and whole cherry tomatoes.
Add olive oil, dried thyme, dried oregano, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper. Toss well to coat all ingredients evenly.
Spread the chicken and vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet or roasting pan. Ensure chicken skin is facing up.
Roast for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender and caramelized. Flip vegetables once halfway through cooking for even browning.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Allowing the chicken to rest briefly after cooking helps keep it juicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chipotle Beef and Bean Macaroni
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, vibrant dish presented in a deep, clean white ceramic bowl. The macaroni is generously coated in a rich, reddish-brown beef and bean ragu, showcasing tender ground beef chunks, soft kidney beans, and al dente macaroni. Melted sharp cheddar and Monterey Jack cheese create a creamy, cohesive texture. The surface is scattered with bright green, freshly chopped cilantro, contrasting the deep, savory tones. The dish is centered, leaving appropriate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A polished fork is to the right, a folded cotton napkin to the left. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors, creating an approachable yet refined restaurant-style appearance. No distracting elements in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm cornbread or tortilla chips for dipping.
Offer a side of sour cream or crema for a cooling contrast.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with a lime vinaigrette.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add ground beef. Brown beef, breaking it apart with a spoon. Cook until no pink remains. Drain excess fat. Set beef aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, minced chipotle peppers, and adobo sauce. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chili powder, smoked paprika, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until spices are fragrant.
Return browned beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes and kidney beans. Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing flavors to meld. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
While ragu simmers, cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Stir heavy cream into the simmering ragu. Gradually add grated cheddar and Monterey Jack cheeses, stirring until melted and smooth. Reserve a small amount of cheese for garnish.
Add cooked macaroni to the ragu. Stir gently to combine, ensuring pasta is fully coated.
Serve immediately in individual bowls. Garnish each serving with fresh chopped cilantro and a sprinkle of reserved grated cheese.
notes: Adjust chipotle peppers to control spice level. For milder flavor, use less chipotle and more adobo sauce.
Ensure beef is well-browned for maximum flavor depth.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Baked Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Homestyle Baked Chicken and Vegetables rests on a simple, round ceramic plate. A robust, golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is the focal point. Surrounding it are rustic, roasted potato wedges with tender interiors and slightly crisped edges. Large, caramelized onion wedges and vibrant red and yellow bell pepper strips are interspersed, alongside softened, bursting halved cherry tomatoes. All components are naturally arranged, touching and slightly overlapping, conveying a comforting, homely meal. A light sprinkle of fresh green parsley adds a fresh, contrasting touch. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate, with everyday, sturdy flatware resting on it. The background suggests a relaxed family dining area with warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a lived-in atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Onions
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (approx. 300g total), cut into thick wedges

ingredients.name: Bell peppers (red or yellow)
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (approx. 300g total), deseeded, cut into 3cm strips

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with 2g salt and 1g black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, onion wedges, bell pepper strips, cherry tomato halves, smashed garlic, olive oil, dried oregano, 3g salt, and 1g black pepper. Toss until well coated.
Arrange seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray or roasting pan.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up among the vegetables. Ensure chicken skin is exposed for browning.
Bake for 40-45 minutes. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C. Skin should be golden and crisp. Vegetables should be tender and caramelized.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Tofu & Chickpea Loaf with Fermented Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick, golden-brown slice of the Smoked Tofu & Chickpea Loaf is centered on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a creamy beige tone. The loaf presents a firm, rustic texture with visible specks of herbs and vegetables. Adjacent to the loaf, a soft, organic dollop of creamy herbed cottage cheese rests. A small, vibrant pile of quick fermented relish, showcasing finely diced, colorful seasonal vegetables, is placed nearby. Crispy, irregularly shaped pieces of cured ham crumble are scattered over the loaf and around the plate, adding texture. The plating is clean and minimalistic, allowing ample white space. The table surface is light, natural wood. An undyed linen napkin in a neutral beige lies beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene. The background is simple and uncluttered, hinting at natural elements like green plants, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined restaurant portion.

ingredients.name: Mixed Seasonal Vegetables (e.g., cabbage, bell pepper, radish), finely diced

instructions: Prepare the Quick Fermented Relish: In a clean jar, combine finely diced seasonal vegetables. In a separate bowl, whisk together white vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt until sugar dissolves. Pour liquid over vegetables. Seal jar. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight for best flavor. This process mimics fermentation for immediate use.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a loaf pan (approx. 20x10cm) with baking paper.
For the Loaf: Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion, garlic, grated carrot, and diced celery until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, mash smoked tofu and chickpeas with a fork until mostly smooth but still some texture remains.
Add sautéed vegetables, flaxseed meal, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper to the tofu-chickpea mixture. Mix well to combine.
Press the mixture firmly into the prepared loaf pan. Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until golden brown and firm to the touch.
While the loaf bakes, prepare the Crispy Ham Crumble: Dice cured ham into small, irregular pieces. Cook in a dry pan over medium heat until crispy. Drain on paper towel. Set aside.
Prepare Herbed Cottage Cheese: In a small bowl, stir cottage cheese with a pinch of salt and a small amount of fresh chopped chives or parsley, if desired.
Remove loaf from oven. Let cool slightly before slicing into thick pieces. This prevents crumbling.
Serve each slice of Smoked Tofu & Chickpea Loaf with a dollop of herbed cottage cheese and a spoonful of the quick fermented relish. Sprinkle crispy ham crumble over the top. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pad Krapow Nua (Thai Basil Beef Stir-fry)
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Pad Krapow Nua is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. A mound of fluffy white jasmine rice occupies one side of the plate. Adjacent to the rice, the vibrant stir-fry is piled neatly: thinly sliced, caramelized beef pieces are mixed with crisp-tender, brightly colored red, green, and yellow bell pepper strips and translucent onion wedges. Dark green holy basil leaves are visibly wilted throughout the mixture, adding contrast. The dish is topped with a perfectly fried sunny-side-up egg, its golden yolk glistening and edges slightly crispy. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with natural, even lighting. A simple cotton napkin rests beside the plate, and a set of chopsticks and a spoon are placed nearby, maintaining a modern bistro aesthetic with authentic Thai serving elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Traditionally topped with a fried egg (kai dao).
Offer prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies) on the side for additional seasoning.

ingredients.name: Beef sirloin or flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
Fresh red bird's eye chilies, thinly sliced (adjust to taste)
Holy basil leaves (or Thai basil if unavailable)

instructions: Prepare sauce: In a small bowl, combine fish sauce, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, and palm sugar. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until smoking.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add thinly sliced beef to the wok. Spread beef in a single layer. Sear for 1-2 minutes without moving, then stir-fry until browned and cooked through. Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add sliced bell peppers and onions to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return beef to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce. Toss quickly to coat all ingredients.
Add holy basil leaves. Stir-fry for 30-60 seconds until basil wilts. Do not overcook basil.
Remove from heat immediately. Serve hot over jasmine rice.
Optional: Fry an egg sunny-side up for each serving. Place on top of the stir-fry.
notes: For best results, use a very hot wok or skillet to achieve 'wok hei' (breath of the wok) char.
Ensure ingredients are prepped and ready before cooking due to the fast stir-fry method.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto al Prosciutto, Piselli e Peperoncino
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy, fluid Risotto al Prosciutto, Piselli e Peperoncino is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The pale yellow risotto spreads naturally, maintaining a flowing consistency. Visible are vibrant green peas and substantial, tender chunks of diced cooked ham. Small flecks of bright red chili are interspersed throughout. The top is lightly garnished with finely chopped fresh parsley and a delicate dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table surface, set with standard European flatware and a clean cotton napkin.
