Finish cooking: Carefully flip the fillets. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
Serve: Place a cod fillet on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of fresh tomato relish alongside the fish. Garnish with a lime wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Wagyu Striploin and Buta Rosu with Cha Soba and Negi Dashi
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine, large, round bone china plate with a subtle, matte finish, resting on a premium light grey marble surface. A single, perfectly seared Wagyu striploin, showing a deep mahogany crust and hints of medium-rare interior, is positioned to the left. Beside it, a smaller, precisely cut medallion of sous vide and seared pork loin displays a delicate pink hue and a golden sear. A small, elegant nest of vibrant green cha soba noodles is coiled neatly, nestled against the proteins, providing a subtle textural contrast. A few pieces of caramelized Tokyo Negi, golden-brown and tender, are artfully arranged near the meats. A rich, amber-hued Negi Dashi Reduction is sparingly drizzled around the proteins, forming a delicate pool. The dish is garnished with a few finely snipped bright green chives, adding a precise touch of color. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing their exquisite quality and precise placement. The scene is lit with dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows that enhance depth and texture. High-quality Japanese chopsticks rest on a minimalist ceramic chopstick rest beside the plate, and a crisp white linen napkin is folded into a precise triangle.
instructions: For the Pork Loin: Season pork loin portions with salt and pepper. Vacuum seal each portion. Cook in a sous vide bath at 60°C for 2 hours. Remove from bath, pat dry thoroughly. Sear in hot oil until golden brown on all sides. Rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions.

For the Wagyu Striploin: Season Wagyu portions generously with sea salt and black pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan or cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Add a small amount of neutral oil. Sear Wagyu 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, turning frequently to build a crust. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.

For the Cha Soba: Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil. Add cha soba noodles and cook according to package instructions (typically 4-5 minutes). Drain immediately. Rinse thoroughly under cold water to remove excess starch. Drain well. Toss lightly with a few drops of sesame oil to prevent sticking.

For the Negi Dashi Reduction: Thinly slice Tokyo Negi. Mince shallots, garlic, and ginger. Heat 15ml neutral oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Sauté shallots, garlic, and ginger until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Add Tokyo Negi and sauté until softened and lightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes. Add dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and gently simmer until the liquid has reduced by half and slightly thickened, about 10-15 minutes. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing on solids to extract all liquid. Keep warm.

Plating: On a large, minimalist plate, create a small, neat coil of cha soba noodles slightly off-center. Place one seared Wagyu striploin piece and one sous vide pork loin medallion beside the noodles. Arrange a few pieces of caramelized Tokyo Negi next to the meats. Drizzle a small amount of the warm Negi Dashi Reduction artfully around the proteins. Garnish with finely snipped chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mozzarella and Green Onion Stuffed Chicken Breast
recipes.visual_description: A single, plump, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, generously stuffed, rests prominently on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The chicken shows a slight bulge from the melted mozzarella and finely chopped green onion peeking out from the seam. A few thinly sliced green onion rings are scattered over the chicken as a minimal garnish. The plate is centered on a well-used, dark wooden dining table, showing natural grain. A simple, casually folded off-white linen napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is lit with warm, inviting light, suggesting a cozy evening meal in a family kitchen. Standard dining flatware is subtly placed next to the plate. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with simple side dishes like roasted potatoes, steamed green beans, or a garden salad.
Enjoy as a hearty family dinner.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Cut a deep pocket into the thickest side of each chicken breast. Do not cut through.
Finely chop the white and light green parts of the green onions.
In a small bowl, combine shredded mozzarella and chopped green onions. Mix well.
Carefully stuff each chicken pocket with the mozzarella and green onion mixture. Close the opening as much as possible.
In a separate small bowl, combine olive oil, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and paprika. Mix to form a paste.
Rub the seasoned oil mixture evenly over each stuffed chicken breast.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of extra olive oil if needed.
Place stuffed chicken breasts in the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown crust forms.
Transfer the skillet with chicken to the preheated oven.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Use a meat thermometer to check.
Remove skillet from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Berry Custard Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single Berry Custard Tartlet sits centered on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The tartlet features a golden-brown, crisp shortcrust pastry shell, approximately 9 cm in diameter. Inside, a smooth, pale yellow vanilla custard is generously spooned, filling the shell to the brim. Neatly arranged on top of the custard are an abundance of fresh, vibrant mixed berries: plump, deep red raspberries, glossy, dark blue blueberries, and bright red strawberry halves. The berries are arranged naturally, creating a burst of color against the creamy custard and golden crust. A subtle sheen from a light apricot glaze covers the fruit. A casually folded beige cloth napkin rests beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting, homestyle atmosphere.
instructions: Combine flour, icing sugar, and salt in a bowl. Cut in cold butter until crumbly. Add egg yolk; mix until dough forms. Do not overmix. Wrap dough and chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll dough 3 mm thick. Line 4 tartlet molds (8-10 cm diameter). Prick bases with a fork. Line with parchment paper, fill with baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes.
Remove beans and parchment. Bake tartlet shells for 5-7 more minutes until light golden. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Whisk 2 egg yolks, caster sugar, and cornflour in a bowl until smooth.
Heat milk and vanilla extract in a saucepan until simmering. Gradually pour hot milk into egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Bring to a gentle boil for 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Transfer custard to a bowl. Cover surface with cling film to prevent a skin. Cool completely.
Spoon cooled custard into baked tartlet shells. Arrange mixed berries neatly on top of the custard.
Gently warm apricot jam with a teaspoon of water. Brush over berries for a subtle glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Mushroom and Cheddar Macaroni Bake
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Rustic Mushroom and Cheddar Macaroni Bake rests in a clean white porcelain bowl. The top is a rich golden brown, with visible bubbly, melted sharp cheddar and crisp panko breadcrumbs. Below the crust, the creamy pasta is studded with various earthy mushrooms, including browned cremini slices and whole shiitake caps, mixed with tender elbow macaroni. Bursting, slightly caramelized roasted cherry tomatoes add pops of vibrant red throughout the dish. The texture is a comforting blend of creamy sauce, tender pasta, and meaty mushrooms. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, creating a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Toss cherry tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 20 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
Clean mushrooms. Slice larger mushrooms into 5 mm thick pieces. Leave smaller ones whole.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until browned and tender, about 8-10 minutes. Remove mushrooms from skillet. Set aside.
Melt butter in the same skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk and vegetable broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer, whisking, until sauce thickens.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in 250 grams of grated cheddar cheese, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until cheese is melted and sauce is creamy.
Add cooked macaroni, roasted cherry tomatoes, and cooked mushrooms to the cheese sauce. Stir to combine.
Combine panko breadcrumbs with remaining 50 grams of grated cheddar cheese. Sprinkle evenly over the pasta mixture.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and bubbly.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: For best flavor, use a mix of fresh, high-quality mushrooms.
Adjust seasoning to taste before baking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Tenderloin, Cherry Gastrique, Potato Pavé, Garlic Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared beef tenderloin medallion, displaying a deep golden-brown crust and a succulent, medium-rare interior, rests elegantly on an expensive bone china plate. Adjacent to the beef, a precisely cut, golden-crisp rectangular block of layered potato pavé showcases its delicate, tender interior. A vibrant, glossy cherry gastrique, with its rich ruby hue, is artfully swept across the plate, creating a dynamic visual line. A few soft, pale golden garlic confit cloves are thoughtfully placed near the beef, adding a subtle textural and color contrast. A tiny, fresh sprig of chervil provides a precise touch of green. The composition is highly minimalist, utilizing abundant white space on the pristine plate to emphasize the quality and precise execution of each component. The scene is set on a premium grey-veined marble surface, with a pristine white linen napkin folded into a sharp triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Prepare Garlic Confit: Place peeled garlic cloves in a small saucepan. Cover with olive oil. Add a pinch of salt. Cook over very low heat for 45-60 minutes until cloves are golden and tender. Do not brown. Cool in oil.

Prepare Potato Pavé: Peel potatoes. Slice very thinly using a mandoline (1-2mm). Melt 100g butter. Layer potato slices tightly in a parchment-lined 20x10cm loaf pan, brushing each layer with melted butter and seasoning with salt and pepper. Press firmly. Bake at 180°C for 60-75 minutes until tender and golden. Cool completely under weight. Once cold, slice into 4 equal rectangular pavé blocks.

Prepare Cherry Gastrique: In a saucepan, combine sugar and 2 tablespoons water. Cook over medium heat until caramelized to an amber color. Deglaze with red wine vinegar; simmer until reduced by half. Add diced shallot, pitted cherries, red wine, thyme, and bay leaf. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until cherries soften and liquid reduces to a syrupy consistency. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Discard solids. Return liquid to pan. Whisk in 20g cold butter. Keep warm.

Cook Beef Tenderloin: Season beef medallions generously with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons butter and 1 tablespoon olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Sear beef 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until internal temperature reaches 54-57°C. Baste with pan juices. Remove beef. Rest on a wire rack for 5 minutes.
Finish Potato Pavé: Just before serving, heat a non-stick pan with remaining butter. Sear potato pavé blocks 3-4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

Plate Dish: Place a potato pavé block slightly off-center on each plate. Rest a beef medallion next to it. Spoon or swipe cherry gastrique artfully across the plate. Arrange a few garlic confit cloves near the beef. Garnish with microgreens or chervil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Oven-Baked Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of roasted chicken and vegetables rests on an off-white, rustic ceramic plate. One golden-brown, skin-on chicken thigh, perfectly roasted, is positioned centrally. Around it, a medley of roasted vegetables: thick potato wedges with crisp edges, softened red and yellow bell pepper chunks, caramelized onion quarters, and burst cherry tomato halves. Vegetables are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, showcasing their varied textures and vibrant, roasted colors. A light scattering of fresh chopped parsley adds a touch of green. The plate sits on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and classic silver flatware are casually placed alongside. Soft, warm ambient light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper
ingredients.quantity: 1, cored and cut into 3 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Yellow bell pepper
ingredients.quantity: 1, cored and cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, bell pepper chunks, onion wedges, cherry tomato halves, and smashed garlic.
Drizzle vegetables with 30 ml olive oil. Season with 2g salt and 2g black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Rub chicken thighs with remaining 30 ml olive oil. Season generously with paprika, oregano, remaining salt, and black pepper.
Place chicken thighs on top of the vegetables on the baking sheet.

Roast for 30 minutes. Turn chicken and vegetables. Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Apple Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of classic apple crumble served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with subtle rim imperfections. The topping is a rugged, golden-brown crust featuring coarse flour crumbs and toasted rolled oats. Soft, 2cm chunks of stewed Granny Smith apples are visible beneath the topping, with thick, caramelized amber juices bubbling slightly at the dish's edges. A single, generous pour of thick, pale yellow vanilla custard pools naturally on one side, partially melting into the warm crumble. The bowl sits on a dark, weathered oak table beside a folded linen napkin and a tarnished silver spoon. Soft, warm kitchen light emphasizes the crunchy textures and steam rising from the fruit.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with hot vanilla custard
Accompany with a dollop of clotted cream
Pair with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel, core, and cut apples into 2cm chunks.
Toss apples with 50g sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Transfer apple mixture to a 20cm baking dish.
Cut cold butter into small cubes.
Rub butter into flour using fingertips until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Stir in remaining 100g sugar and rolled oats.
Spread crumble topping evenly over the apples.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden brown and fruit is bubbling.
Remove from oven and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use cold butter to ensure a crisp, crumbly texture.
Do not overwork the dough or it will become tough.
Granny Smith apples provide the best tart balance to the sweet topping.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Braised Chicken with Peppers and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Spanish-Style Braised Chicken and Vegetables is centrally mounded on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks, approximately 4-5 cm, are nestled among the vibrant vegetables. Rustic chunks of tender-firm Yukon Gold potatoes, about 3 cm, mingle with softened diced red and green bell peppers and caramelized onion pieces. A rich, reddish-brown tomato-based sauce, glossy and clinging to the ingredients, pools slightly at the plate's base. The dish showcases earthy tones of chicken and potatoes contrasted with bright red and green from bell peppers and the deep red of the sauce. It is garnished with a generous sprinkling of coarsely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish's inviting textures and colors, emphasizing its hearty and authentic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread for dipping into the flavorful sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar on the side.

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500 g, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Dry white wine
ingredients.quantity: 125 ml (optional, can substitute with more broth)

instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with white wine (if using), scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes until wine reduces slightly.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add potato chunks and chicken broth. Ensure potatoes are mostly submerged.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Cherry-Tomato Gastrique, Confit Potato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast, whole and unsliced, rests elegantly on an oversized white bone china plate with a subtle rim. A rich, glossy, reddish-brown cherry-tomato gastrique forms an organic pool beneath and around the chicken. Its deep hue contrasts with the golden-crisp, beautifully rendered skin of the chicken. Two or three golden-brown confit potato batons are artfully arranged beside the chicken, their edges slightly softened. A cluster of three to four small, deeply caramelized pearl onions, glistening with a dark amber sheen, adds visual depth. Abundant negative space emphasizes the dish's refined simplicity. A tiny sprig of fresh thyme provides a precise, verdant accent. The composition is natural and flowing. The dish is presented on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, accompanied by elegant silver flatware and a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, focused lighting enhances textures against an ultra-minimalist background.

ingredients.name: Large Maris Piper or Yukon Gold potatoes

instructions: Prepare Confit Potatoes: Peel potatoes. Cut into thick batons (approx. 6cm x 2cm x 2cm). Place in a small saucepan. Cover completely with 80ml olive oil. Add 4 crushed garlic cloves and 2 fresh thyme sprigs. Cook over very low heat for 30-40 minutes until fork-tender but not falling apart. Season with salt. Drain potatoes, reserving oil.

Prepare Cherry-Tomato Gastrique: In a small saucepan, combine 30g sugar and 30ml water. Cook over medium heat until a golden caramel forms. Deglaze with 60ml red wine vinegar. Add pitted cherries, halved cherry tomatoes, 2 crushed garlic cloves, and 2 fresh thyme sprigs. Simmer for 10 minutes until cherries soften. Add 250ml chicken stock. Reduce by half until slightly thickened. Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract liquid. Season with salt and black pepper. Keep warm.

Caramelize Pearl Onions: Blanch pearl onions in boiling water for 1 minute. Drain, peel. In a small pan, melt 15g butter with a splash of water. Add peeled pearl onions. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until tender and deeply caramelized, about 15-20 minutes. Season lightly.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts very dry. Season skin generously with salt and black pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Add 20g butter and 2 fresh thyme sprigs to the pan. Baste chicken continuously with pan juices for 5-7 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from pan, rest for 5 minutes.

Plate Dish: Spoon a generous pool of cherry-tomato gastrique onto the center of each plate. Place a whole chicken breast on top of the sauce. Artfully arrange 2-3 confit potato batons beside the chicken. Arrange 3-4 caramelized pearl onions around the chicken. Garnish with a small fresh thyme sprig.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Resting the chicken after cooking is crucial for juiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Mustard and Pearl Onions
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic bowl, showcasing a generous individual portion. At the center are substantial, dark mahogany-braised beef chunks, each with a rich, glossy surface from the sauce. Interspersed among the beef are tender, golden-brown pearl onions and vibrant red diced tomatoes, providing pops of color and textural contrast. The thick, dark brown, glossy sauce, infused with red wine and Dijon mustard, coats the ingredients generously and pools at the bottom of the bowl. Scattered crispy lardons add a savory crunch. A light sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding freshness. The bowl is placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a white linen napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the deep colors and comforting textures of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for dipping in the rich sauce.
Accompany with mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles.
Pair with a glass of robust red wine, such as Pinot Noir or Merlot.
instructions: Render lardons in a large Dutch oven over medium heat until crispy. Remove lardons; set aside. Keep rendered fat.
Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Sear beef in rendered fat and olive oil in batches until well browned on all sides. Remove beef; set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the Dutch oven. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and minced garlic. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Gradually pour in red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in beef stock and Dijon mustard. Add seared beef, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the Dutch oven.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
While beef braises, blanch pearl onions in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and peel.
In a separate pan, melt butter. Add peeled pearl onions and fresh diced tomatoes. Sauté until tender and slightly caramelized, about 10-12 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Once beef is tender, remove from oven. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Stir in cooked pearl onions, diced tomatoes, and rendered lardons into the braised beef.
Simmer on stovetop for 10-15 minutes to allow flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Stuffed Pasta Shells with Ricotta and Potato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of baked stuffed pasta shells rests in a rustic white ceramic bowl. Three large, golden-brown pasta shells, generously filled with creamy ricotta and mashed potato, are nestled in a vibrant, rich red tomato-olive sauce. The pasta edges are slightly crisped from baking, revealing glimpses of the creamy white filling. A generous topping of golden Panko breadcrumbs and melted Parmesan cheese adds a textural contrast. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered artfully over the top, providing a pop of color. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin, reflecting a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting. A small side dish of crusty bread is placed alongside.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar
instructions: Cook pasta shells in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes. Drain. Mash thoroughly.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Add chopped olives. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, ricotta cheese, 30g grated Parmesan, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Mix well.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce in the bottom of a 20x30cm baking dish.
Carefully fill each pasta shell with the ricotta-potato mixture using a spoon.
Arrange filled shells in a single layer in the baking dish.
Pour remaining tomato sauce evenly over the shells.
In a small bowl, combine Panko breadcrumbs and remaining 20g grated Parmesan. Sprinkle this mixture over the sauced shells.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until sauce is bubbly and topping is golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mandarin Meringue Nests with Honey Walnuts
recipes.visual_description: A single, rustic meringue nest sits on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The meringue is crisp, slightly irregular, and off-white. Inside the nest, bright orange mandarin segments are piled generously, their juicy texture visible. A thick, golden drizzle of warm honey flows over the mandarins and onto the meringue, creating glistening rivulets. Roughly chopped walnuts are scattered throughout the honey, adding a deep brown contrast and crunchy texture. A few delicate strands of bright orange zest are sprinkled over the top. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A cream-colored linen napkin is casually folded beside the plate, with a simple silver spoon resting upon it. Soft, warm light illuminates the dessert, highlighting its homely appeal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Whisk egg whites with salt and white vinegar in a clean bowl until soft peaks form.
Gradually add caster sugar, one tablespoon at a time. Continue whisking until stiff, glossy peaks form and sugar is dissolved.
Gently fold in orange zest.
Spoon meringue mixture onto the prepared tray. Form 4 individual nests with a slight indentation in the center.
Bake for 90 minutes. Turn off oven. Leave meringues inside the oven to cool completely for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
While meringues cool, roughly chop walnuts.
Peel and segment mandarin oranges, removing as much white pith as possible.
In a small saucepan, gently warm honey over low heat. Add chopped walnuts and stir to coat.
To serve, place a meringue nest on each plate. Fill the center with mandarin segments.
Generously drizzle the warm honey-walnut mixture over the mandarins and meringue.
notes: Ensure egg whites are at room temperature for best meringue volume.
Let meringues cool completely in the oven for maximum crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage and Broccoli Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. Golden-brown crumbled Italian sausage pieces are naturally mixed with vibrant green broccoli florets and al dente orecchiette pasta. The pasta is lightly coated in a savory sauce, with some residual broth visible, creating a comforting, cohesive look. The arrangement is casual and organic, reflecting a home-cooked meal. A generous sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese and a scattering of fresh, chopped parsley add color and freshness on top. The scene is lit with warm, inviting light, highlighting the food's natural textures. An everyday ceramic plate and a simple fork rest casually next to the bowl, emphasizing a homely, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The portion is a single, modest serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add orecchiette pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.

While pasta cooks, remove Italian sausage from casings. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove sausage from skillet; set aside. Drain excess fat, leaving about 15ml in the pan.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Add broccoli to the boiling pasta water during the last 3-4 minutes of pasta cooking. It should be tender-crisp.

While broccoli cooks, add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet with sausage drippings. Mince garlic. Add minced garlic and red chili flakes to the skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not burn garlic.
Drain pasta and broccoli, reserving 125ml of pasta cooking water. Add drained pasta and broccoli to the skillet with garlic. Add cooked sausage back to the skillet.
Pour in chicken broth or reserved pasta water. Stir well to combine all ingredients. Simmer for 1-2 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Grate Parmesan cheese. Stir in most of the grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Finely chop fresh parsley.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining Parmesan and fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure sausage is cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Mushroom & Jalapeño Cheese Bites
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve golden-brown, bite-sized cheese toastie squares are arranged casually on a well-used wooden cutting board. Some pieces slightly overlap, creating a natural, approachable look. The toasted bread has a crisp, buttery exterior. Glimpses of creamy, melted American cheese and the savory, earthy mushroom, onion, and vibrant green jalapeño filling peek from the edges. Colors are warm: toasted golden-brown bread, creamy yellow-white cheese, and deep earthy browns of mushrooms with pops of bright green. The board rests on a simple kitchen table, showcasing natural wood grain. A casually placed, folded cloth napkin sits nearby. Warm, inviting lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The entire board is visible, presented as a comforting shareable appetizer.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a comforting appetizer or snack.
Pair with a simple dipping sauce like extra mustard or a mild tomato dip.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add diced mushrooms. Cook until all moisture has evaporated and mushrooms are lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Season mushroom and onion mixture with salt and pepper. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
In a bowl, combine cooled mushroom mixture, grated cheddar cheese, chopped pickled jalapeños, and Dijon mustard. Mix well.
Lay out 4 slices of bread. Place one slice of American cheese on each.
Evenly distribute the mushroom and cheese filling over the American cheese.
Top with another slice of American cheese, then cover with the remaining 4 slices of bread to form sandwiches.
Trim crusts from each sandwich. Cut each sandwich into 2 or 3 bite-sized squares or triangles, aiming for 8-12 pieces total.
Brush the tops and bottoms of the bread bites generously with melted butter.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Place the buttered bread bites in the pan.
Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and the cheese is thoroughly melted and gooey.
Serve immediately while warm.
notes: Ensure mushrooms are well-cooked to remove excess moisture for best texture.
Adjust jalapeño quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Kamut Polenta and Coffee-Chocolate Jus
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate set on a simple wooden table. A single, generously portioned braised beef short rib, dark and glistening with a rich coffee-chocolate jus, sits prominently on a bed of creamy, golden-tan kamut polenta. The short rib is whole, showing its tender, fall-off-the-bone texture. The polenta has a smooth, creamy consistency, with subtle lotus seed specks. The jus, a deep brown with a subtle sheen, pools around the short rib. Garnish with a few fresh thyme leaves. Beside the plate, a warm, golden-brown kamut biscuit, showing its rustic top, is placed. The setting is a modern bistro style with natural, even lighting, highlighting the rich colors and textures. A simple cotton napkin is folded beside the plate.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Season short ribs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs from pot.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes. Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in cocoa powder. Deglaze pot with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Return short ribs to pot. Pour in beef stock and coffee. Add thyme and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot tightly. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until meat is fork-tender.

While ribs braise, prepare biscuits. In a bowl, whisk 250g kamut flour, baking powder, and a pinch of salt. Cut in 100g cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add cold milk, mixing until just combined.
Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface. Gently pat to 2 cm thickness. Cut into 8 biscuits using a round cutter. Place on a baking sheet.
Bake biscuits in the same oven for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.

For kamut polenta: In a medium saucepan, bring 700 ml salted water to a simmer. Slowly whisk in 200g kamut flour. Cook, stirring frequently, until thickened and creamy, about 15-20 minutes. Stir in 50g butter and 50g dried lotus seeds. Season with salt.

Remove short ribs from oven. Skim excess fat from braising liquid. Strain liquid into a clean saucepan. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until slightly thickened into a jus. Season with salt and pepper.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of kamut polenta onto each plate. Top with a braised short rib. Drizzle with coffee-chocolate jus. Serve with warm kamut biscuits on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Mushroom Medley and Bell Pepper Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Mushroom Medley and Bell Pepper Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh or thick chicken chunks are positioned prominently. Beside it, a neat mound of fluffy brown rice, interspersed with vibrant red and yellow diced bell pepper cubes, adds color. Earthy, sautéed cremini mushroom slices are scattered around the chicken and rice, providing depth and texture. The dish is garnished simply with fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The plating is organized and balanced, with moderate negative space. Textures include crisp sear on chicken, tender interior, fluffy rice, and tender-crisp vegetables. The setting is a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and refined presentation. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a casual dining aesthetic.
instructions: Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions. Use 400ml water or chicken broth for cooking. Set aside. Keep warm.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Rest on a cutting board.
While chicken rests, dice red bell pepper into small cubes. Slice mushrooms thinly. Mince yellow onion and garlic.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to the same skillet. Add minced onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned and tender.
Add minced garlic and diced bell pepper to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until fragrant and slightly tender-crisp. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir cooked brown rice into the skillet with the vegetables and broth. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley. Slice rested chicken thighs into thick chunks, or keep whole. Do not fan out.
Plate a portion of the bell pepper rice. Place a chicken thigh or chicken chunks beside the rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Resting the chicken after searing helps keep it juicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Mole Poblano
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Pollo en Mole Poblano is presented on a clean, round, white porcelain dinner plate. A large, dark-skinned chicken thigh, deeply caramelized from searing, rests prominently on a pool of rich, glossy mole sauce. The mole, a deep, complex reddish-brown, exhibits a smooth, thick consistency, clinging to the chicken. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped fresh cilantro leaves provides a vibrant color contrast against the dark sauce, along with a sprinkle of pale, toasted sesame seeds for texture. The chicken piece is whole, showcasing its succulent, tender appearance. The plate sits on a simple, warm-toned wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp, folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. A small, white ceramic bowl of fluffy white rice and a stack of warm, soft corn tortillas are positioned nearby, along with a traditional Mexican talavera-style water glass. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the sauce's sheen and the chicken's inviting texture, creating an authentic and approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the mole sauce.
Accompany with a side of traditional Mexican rice.
Offer a small bowl of pickled red onions or jalapeños for a tangy counterpoint.
Serve with a refreshing Agua Fresca or Horchata.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt.
Sear chicken skin-side down in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Cook until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear other side briefly. Remove chicken, set aside.

Carefully remove stems and seeds from dried chiles. Toast chiles in the dry pot for 30 seconds per side until fragrant. Do not burn. Place chiles in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let rehydrate for 20 minutes.
In the same pot, add a little oil. Sauté chopped tomatoes, onion, and garlic until softened and lightly browned.

Drain rehydrated chiles. Add chiles, sautéed vegetables, almonds, raisins, half of the sesame seeds, tortilla piece, cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, and cumin seeds to a blender. Add 200 ml chicken broth.
Blend until very smooth. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Press solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.

Heat 15 ml lard or oil in the pot over medium heat. Add strained mole paste. Cook, stirring constantly, for 10-15 minutes. The paste will thicken and darken. This step is crucial for flavor development.
Gradually whisk in remaining chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add chopped dark chocolate and sugar. Stir until chocolate is fully melted and incorporated. Season with salt to taste.

Return seared chicken thighs to the mole sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Serve chicken with mole sauce. Garnish with fresh cilantro and remaining toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The mole paste requires patient cooking to develop its deep flavor and color.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Cacciatore with Rigatoni is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple light wooden table. The rigatoni pasta, cooked al dente, forms a neat base, coated lightly in the rich, rustic tomato sauce. A tender, whole seared chicken thigh, its skin a deep golden-brown, is placed centrally atop the pasta. The vibrant red sauce, teeming with browned sliced mushrooms, diced softened onions, and strips of red bell pepper, generously covers the chicken and pasta. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes are scattered throughout the sauce, adding pops of color. Fresh, torn basil leaves are sprinkled over the dish, providing a contrasting green accent. Grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese lightly dusts the top. The textures are varied: tender chicken, soft vegetables, and firm pasta. The scene is well-lit with natural, even light, and a simple cotton napkin is folded beside the bowl. A traditional fork and spoon are placed to the side. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, allowing the food to be the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper strips to the same pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and their liquid has evaporated.
Stir in minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze. Cook until wine is nearly evaporated.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and halved cherry tomatoes to the pan. Bring sauce to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Nestle them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pan. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in fresh basil. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve. Plate rigatoni. Top with a chicken thigh and generous spoonfuls of the cacciatore sauce. Garnish with additional fresh basil and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The red wine can be omitted or substituted with extra chicken broth if preferred.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato Sugo and Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato Sugo and Tagliatelle is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, artfully mounded nest of golden tagliatelle, glistening with a rich, rustic red tomato sugo, forms the base. Visible chunks of crushed tomatoes and flecks of vibrant green fresh basil and parsley are interspersed throughout the sauce. Three to four thick, irregularly shaped medallions of golden-brown pan-seared chicken are placed gracefully on top of the pasta, not fanned, showcasing their crispy edges. A light scattering of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese crowns the dish. The setting features a simple, warm-toned wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Traditional Italian flatware is placed to the right. In the soft-focus background, a small, rustic ceramic bowl holds extra grated Parmesan and a clear cruet of olive oil, completing an authentic Italian casual dining scene with natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Canned whole peeled tomatoes (San Marzano recommended)
Chicken broth or dry white wine

instructions: Pound chicken breasts to an even 2 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and black pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the skillet. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and optional red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth or white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.

Add canned whole tomatoes. Crush tomatoes with a spoon. Season with salt and black pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
While sauce simmers, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add tagliatelle pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Slice cooked chicken breasts into thick medallions. Add sliced chicken to the tomato sugo. Stir to coat. Simmer 2 minutes to warm through.
Drain pasta, reserving 60ml pasta water. Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sugo and chicken. Toss to combine. If needed, add a splash of reserved pasta water to achieve desired consistency.
Stir in fresh basil and chopped parsley. Serve immediately, topped with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Tofu with Ginger Pea Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Crispy Tofu with Ginger Pea Sauce is meticulously plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Fluffy jasmine rice forms a neat mound at the center. Golden-brown, pan-seared 2cm tofu cubes, with a visibly crispy exterior, are artfully arranged atop and around the rice. A vibrant, light green ginger-pea sauce, smooth yet dotted with whole green peas, is generously spooned over the tofu and rice, creating appealing pools on the plate. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced bright green spring onions, adding a fresh visual and aromatic contrast. The composition is balanced, showcasing varied textures and natural colors: crisp tofu, tender peas, fluffy rice, and a glossy sauce. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. Chopsticks are neatly placed beside the plate, with a subtle white rice bowl in the background. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's freshness and detail.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with hot jasmine rice
Use chopsticks for eating
instructions: Press tofu for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Cut pressed tofu into 2cm cubes.
In a bowl, toss tofu cubes with 15g cornstarch, a pinch of salt, and white pepper.
Heat 60ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes in a single layer. Pan-sear until golden and crispy on all sides. This takes 8-10 minutes. Remove tofu from pan and set aside.
In the same pan, add grated ginger and minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 100g of the green peas to the pan. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, and 120ml water. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
In a small bowl, whisk 15g cornstarch with 30ml cold water to create a slurry.
Pour cornstarch slurry into the simmering sauce, whisking continuously until the sauce thickens.
Remove sauce from heat. Carefully transfer half of the sauce mixture with the cooked peas to a blender. Blend until smooth.
Combine the blended sauce with the remaining unblended sauce from the pan. Stir in the remaining 100g whole green peas.
Gently fold the crispy tofu cubes into the sauce.
Serve immediately over cooked jasmine rice. Garnish with thinly sliced spring onions.
notes: Ensure tofu is pressed well to achieve maximum crispiness.
Adjust ginger and garlic quantities to personal taste preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of rustic oven-baked chicken and potatoes. Two bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, roasted to a deep golden-brown with slightly crisped skin, are nestled amidst large, irregular chunks of tender, golden-edged potatoes and soft, caramelized onion wedges. The dish boasts warm, earthy tones from the roasted vegetables and savory chicken, accented by vibrant green flecks of freshly chopped dill and parsley. Components naturally overlap, filling an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic plate, leaving comfortable negative space. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table under warm kitchen lighting. A simple, off-white linen napkin is casually placed, alongside a rustic metal fork. A small side bowl of tangy pickled cucumbers and a slice of dark rye bread complete the authentic Eastern European home meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled cucumbers (ogurtsy).
Offer slices of dark rye bread.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 1 kg, peeled and cut into thick rustic chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt, pepper, paprika, and dried dill.
In a large bowl, combine potato chunks and onion wedges. Drizzle with olive oil. Add minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange the seasoned potatoes and onions in a single layer in a large oven-safe baking dish.
Place chicken thighs on top of the vegetables.
Pour chicken broth around the chicken and vegetables.
Cover the baking dish tightly with aluminum foil.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil. Continue baking for another 25-35 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy, and chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C. Potatoes should be tender.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish generously with fresh dill and parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of golden-brown roasted chicken thighs, nestled amongst thick wedges of perfectly roasted potatoes and caramelized onion chunks, fills a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The chicken skin is crisp, the meat tender and juicy, showing a deep golden hue. Potatoes are soft and fluffy inside with a crisp, golden exterior. Large, tender roasted garlic cloves are scattered throughout. A scattering of fresh chopped parsley adds a vibrant green contrast. The plate rests on a well-worn, rustic wooden dining table. A simple fork and knife are placed casually beside the plate, with a cream linen napkin nearby. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, homely atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a comfortable family kitchen.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Wash and scrub potatoes. Cut potatoes into thick wedges. Cut onion into large wedges. Smash garlic cloves with the side of a knife.
In a large bowl, combine chicken thighs, potato wedges, onion wedges, and smashed garlic.
Drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle with dried rosemary, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper. Toss well to coat all ingredients evenly.
Spread ingredients in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and potatoes are tender and golden. Flip potatoes and chicken halfway through cooking for even browning.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Serve hot directly from the pan or transferred to a serving platter.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Chicken and Potato Bake is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, cooked whole, anchors the center. Around it, golden-roasted potato wedges are arranged organically, interspersed with vibrant, slightly burst red cherry tomato halves and soft, caramelized red onion wedges. Scattered among the vegetables are glossy, dark Kalamata olives. A sprig of fresh oregano rests atop the chicken, and a bright yellow lemon wedge is placed to the side. The dish exhibits a natural, flowing arrangement with balanced negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table, complemented by a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the rich textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to absorb the pan juices.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2 cm thick wedges.
Halve cherry tomatoes.
Cut red onion into 2 cm thick wedges.
Smash garlic cloves lightly.
Combine chicken, potato wedges, cherry tomatoes, red onion wedges, garlic, Kalamata olives, oregano, and rosemary in a large roasting pan.
Drizzle with olive oil. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Arrange ingredients in a single layer, ensuring chicken skin is facing up.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip chicken and potatoes. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the dish before serving. Garnish with fresh oregano sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Aji de Gallina
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Aji de Gallina is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, resting on a rustic wooden table. Thick rounds of boiled potato form a neat base. Piled atop is a generous portion of creamy, vibrant yellow-orange chicken stew. Shredded chicken is visibly integrated into the rich, velvety sauce, which shows subtle red from tomato and white from melted queso fresco. The sauce is thick, clinging to chicken and potatoes, yet fluid. Garnishes are meticulously placed: two half-moon slices of hard-boiled egg, two halved black olives, and a sprinkle of bright green chopped parsley provide contrasting colors and textures. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. A simple cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting warmth and vibrant hues, creating an approachable, refined restaurant presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fluffy white rice to absorb the creamy sauce.
Traditionally, aji de gallina is accompanied by hard-boiled eggs and black olives.
Consider a simple side salad with a light vinaigrette to cut through the richness.
instructions: Boil chicken breasts in salted water until cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Shred chicken finely using two forks. Reserve 400 ml of chicken broth.

While chicken boils, boil potatoes in a separate pot of salted water until fork-tender. Drain. Peel and slice three-quarters of the potatoes into 1 cm thick rounds. Set aside. Mash the remaining quarter of the potatoes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium heat. Add finely diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add aji amarillo paste. Stir and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in reserved chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add shredded chicken and mashed potato. Stir well to combine.

Reduce heat to low. Stir in crumbled queso fresco and evaporated milk. Cook, stirring occasionally, until cheese melts and sauce thickens to a creamy consistency, about 5-7 minutes. Do not boil vigorously. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Arrange sliced potatoes on individual serving plates. Ladle generous portions of the creamy chicken mixture over the potatoes.
Garnish each plate with hard-boiled egg slices, black olive halves, and chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The spice level can be adjusted by varying the amount of aji amarillo paste.
The sauce should be creamy and rich, not watery. Adjust broth or mashed potato if needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Shrimp Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, white, shallow pasta bowl, showcasing a generous, artfully swirled mound of linguine coated in a creamy, off-white sauce. Plump, perfectly cooked, golden-pink shrimp are nestled throughout and atop the pasta, some peeking out, others partially covered by the sauce. The sauce clings beautifully to the pasta strands and shrimp, with visible flecks of minced garlic and finely diced onion. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the top, adding a pop of green and freshness. A light dusting of freshly ground black pepper provides a subtle contrast. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. Beside the bowl, standard silver flatware (fork and spoon) rests on a folded natural cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background. The shrimp are presented whole, not sliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano at the table.

ingredients.name: Fresh mozzarella, grated or finely diced

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml of pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add shrimp to the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, just until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from the skillet and set aside.
Pour broth into the skillet, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in milk and bring to a gentle simmer. Gradually add grated mozzarella, stirring constantly until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth and creamy.

Add cooked pasta and the cooked shrimp back into the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If the sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 50ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Stir in chopped parsley. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork and Potato Stir-Fry with Creamy Soy Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Pork and Potato Stir-Fry is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The dish features substantial 2-3 cm chunks of seared pork, mixed with tender 2 cm potato cubes, vibrant green beans cut into 3-4 cm pieces, and bright yellow corn kernels. Thinly sliced onions are visible throughout. All ingredients are coated in a glossy, creamy, light brown soy-mayonnaise sauce. The arrangement is natural and mounded, filling the center of the plate, with components touching and slightly overlapping. Colors are warm and inviting: golden-brown pork, pale yellow potatoes, deep green beans, and bright yellow corn, all against the creamy sauce. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a comfortable home kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene from above, highlighting the texture and appeal of the home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
instructions: Boil potatoes. Cook until fork-tender, about 10-15 minutes. Drain. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat.
Add pork cubes. Sear pork until browned on all sides. Cook for 5-7 minutes. Remove pork from pan. Set aside.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return pork to the pan. Add green beans and corn kernels. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mayonnaise, water or dashi broth, and sugar (if using).
Pour sauce over ingredients in the pan. Stir to coat.
Add cooked potatoes to the pan. Gently stir to combine.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens and coats all ingredients.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Ginger-Glazed Chicken with Tomato Consommé and Pasta Pearls
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly portioned dish presented on a pristine, large white bone china plate with generous negative space. The focal point is a golden-brown, seared chicken breast, sliced into two elegant medallions or presented as a single, thick chunk, glistening subtly with a caramelized ginger glaze. Adjacent to the chicken, a small, artful cluster of delicate, off-white pasta pearls is precisely arranged. Surrounding these elements, a crystal-clear, amber-hued tomato consommé forms a shallow, inviting pool, its surface catching the light. A few drops of vibrant green oregano oil are meticulously dotted onto the consommé, creating a beautiful color contrast. The entire composition is asymmetrical and organic, emphasizing natural shapes. A minimal garnish of finely snipped micro chives or tiny basil leaves rests gently on the chicken or pearls. The plate sits on a smooth, grey-veined marble surface, illuminated by dramatic, focused lighting that creates soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sculptural quality. A crisp, white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle, is placed beside the plate, completing the ultra-minimalist, sophisticated setting.

ingredients.name: Micro basil or chives, finely snipped

instructions: Prepare Tomato Consommé:
Combine chopped tomatoes, onion, smashed garlic, and oregano sprigs in a large pot.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cook 20 minutes. Vegetables should soften.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Do not press solids.
Let liquid drip slowly for 1-2 hours for clear consommé.
Season consommé with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Make Pasta Pearls:
On a clean surface, make a well with flour. Add egg yolk and a pinch of salt to the center.
Gradually incorporate flour into yolk. Add tiny drops of water if needed to form a stiff dough.
Knead dough 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Roll dough very thin. Cut into tiny squares or use a small round cutter to form 'pearls' (2-3mm diameter).
Dust pearls lightly with flour to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Prepare Ginger Glaze for Chicken:
Combine grated ginger, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and brown sugar in a small saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened. Set aside.
Cook Chicken:
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Seal chicken breasts in vacuum-seal bags.
Cook in a sous vide bath at 68°C for 1.5 hours.
Remove chicken from bags. Pat very dry.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Brush generously with ginger glaze. Continue searing, brushing frequently, until glaze caramelizes and chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature. Rest chicken 5 minutes.
Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick medallions or serve whole as a chunk.
Make Oregano Oil:
Combine oil and oregano leaves in a small saucepan.
Heat gently over low heat 5 minutes. Do not fry.
Remove from heat. Let cool. Strain through a fine sieve.
Cook Pasta Pearls and Assemble:
Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil.
Add pasta pearls. Cook 1-2 minutes until al dente. Drain immediately.
Gently reheat consommé.
Place a few pasta pearls artfully in the center of a shallow bowl.
Carefully place one portion of sliced chicken (medallions or chunk) next to the pearls.
Pour warm consommé around the chicken and pearls. Do not submerge chicken.
Drizzle oregano oil around the consommé.
Garnish with micro basil or chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Candied Pork Belly with Coconut Rice and Umami Carrot
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an elegant, matte white bone china sharing platter, allowing for abundant negative space. The composition features a few precisely cut 1.5cm cubes of golden-brown candied pork belly, their exteriors glistening with caramelized sugar and their edges crisp. Adjacent, a perfectly formed quenelle of creamy, off-white coconut rice pudding rests. A small, dark, glossy pool of intensely caramelized onion and black garlic puree provides a deep umami counterpoint. A vibrant orange line of spiced carrot fluid gel arcs gracefully across the plate, offering a touch of bright color and subtle sweetness. A delicate, translucent rice crisp shard stands vertically, adding architectural height and a crisp texture. The elements are arranged with sophisticated minimalism, each component distinct yet harmoniously balanced. A light dusting of toasted black sesame seeds provides a subtle visual and textural accent. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the clean lines and refined textures.
instructions: Cut pork belly into 3x3 cm cubes. Sear all sides in a hot pan until golden.
Place seared pork in a pot. Add water to cover, star anise, soy sauce, mirin, and sliced ginger. Simmer gently for 2 hours until very tender.
Remove pork from liquid. Press between two weighted trays in the refrigerator overnight.
Cut chilled, pressed pork into 1.5x1.5 cm cubes. Toss with a light sugar glaze (sugar, water, pinch of salt). Roast or pan-fry until caramelized and crispy on all sides.
Rinse glutinous rice. Cook with coconut milk, 50g sugar, and vanilla bean paste until tender and creamy. Blend until smooth. Pass through a fine sieve. Chill.

Slice onion thinly. Caramelize slowly in a pan with a pinch of salt until deep brown and sweet (approx. 45-60 minutes). Add black garlic and a splash of water, simmer briefly. Blend until perfectly smooth. Pass through a fine sieve.

Peel and chop carrots. Steam until very tender. Blend with 50g sugar, cinnamon, and cardamom. Pass through a fine sieve. Add agar-agar and bring to a simmer to activate. Chill. Once set, blend again until a smooth, pourable fluid gel forms.

Whisk rice flour with 50ml water and a pinch of salt to form a thin batter. Spread very thinly on a silicone mat. Bake at 150°C until crisp and golden, about 10-15 minutes. Break into irregular, delicate shards.

On a minimalist serving platter, arrange a few perfect cubes of candied pork belly. Place a small quenelle of the chilled coconut rice next to it. Dot the plate with the dark onion-garlic puree. Draw a delicate line or small pool of the carrot fluid gel. Stand a delicate rice crisp shard upright.
Lightly dust with toasted black sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Penne with Caramelized Onion and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous individual portion of Baked Penne with Caramelized Onion and Mozzarella is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table surface. The pasta is golden-brown on top, showcasing patches of melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese and hints of crispy, caramelized onion peeking through. Below the crust, the penne pasta is coated in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered on top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish is served directly from a ceramic baking dish, with a portion transferred to the plate. A simple, clean silver fork and knife are placed to the right of the plate, and a folded cotton napkin rests to the left. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and warm colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting with a casual atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions, cooking to al dente. Drain pasta. Set aside.
Peel and thinly slice onions. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.

Add sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25-30 minutes until deeply caramelized and golden brown. Add a pinch of sugar during the last 10 minutes to aid caramelization. Remove onions from skillet. Set aside.
Peel and mince garlic. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same skillet over medium heat.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and black pepper. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Chop mozzarella into small cubes or shred. Reserve 50g for topping.
Combine cooked pasta, tomato sauce, caramelized onions, most of the mozzarella, and half of the fresh basil in a large bowl. Mix gently.
Transfer pasta mixture to the prepared baking dish. Spread evenly.
Sprinkle reserved mozzarella and grated Parmesan cheese over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and the top is golden brown. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil before serving.
notes: Cook pasta al dente as it will continue to cook in the oven.
Allow the dish to rest for a few minutes after baking to set the cheese and sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Cerdo y Tomate
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Arroz con Cerdo y Tomate is presented centrally on a clean, white, shallow round dinner plate. The rich reddish-orange rice, infused with tomato and paprika, forms a slightly mounded base. Irregularly shaped, browned pork chunks are nestled throughout the rice, showcasing their seared exterior. A few smaller, vibrant red tomato pieces are visible within the dish. The surface is slightly moist, topped with a generous scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley for color and texture. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table, reflecting a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin and traditional European-style flatware are placed beside the plate. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant ambiance with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up juices.
Offer a simple green salad as an accompaniment.
Pair with a dry Spanish white or light red wine.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 2-3 cm chunks. Season pork with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, shallow pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and bay leaf. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes until tomatoes break down and sauce thickens.
Return seared pork to the pan. Add rice and stir to coat grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Do not stir excessively.
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Remove bay leaf. Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust liquid quantity based on rice type; Bomba rice absorbs more liquid than Arborio.
For best results, use high-quality, ripe tomatoes or good canned diced tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Aerated Dark Chocolate, Raspberry, Tonka Bean Crisp
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented on a pristine, large white bone china plate, allowing abundant negative space to highlight the delicate composition. A single, elegant quenelle of dark aerated chocolate mousse, light and airy, rests off-center. Beside it, vibrant ruby-red dots and flowing streaks of raspberry fluid gel provide a striking color contrast and artistic movement. A small, artfully scattered cluster of pale green pistachio crumble adds subtle texture and color. Vertically inserted into the mousse or nearby are one or two irregular, wafer-thin golden-brown tonka bean crisps, alongside a slender, glossy shard of dark chocolate glass, adding architectural height and reflective quality. The arrangement is organic and minimalist, emphasizing the purity of ingredients and precision of technique. The plate sits on a polished dark wood table, with a precisely folded white linen napkin and minimalist silver flatware.

ingredients.name: Dark Chocolate (70% cocoa solids), finely chopped
Gelatin Leaf (2g), bloomed in cold water

instructions: Melt 150g dark chocolate gently over a bain-marie. Set aside.
Whisk egg yolks, 30g sugar, and a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Heat cream and milk in a saucepan until simmering.
Temper hot cream mixture into egg yolks. Return mixture to saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened (82°C). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Pour hot custard over melted chocolate. Stir until smooth.
Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill completely for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Transfer chilled chocolate mixture to a stand mixer. Whip on medium-high until light and aerated. Do not over-whip.
Transfer to a piping bag. Chill until ready to plate.
Combine raspberries, 20g sugar, and lemon juice in a saucepan. Simmer 5 minutes.
Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.
Return juice to clean saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar.
Bring to a boil. Simmer 1 minute, whisking.
Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set (approx. 30 minutes).
Transfer set gel to a blender. Blend until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Transfer to a squeeze bottle or piping bag. Chill.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Cream 50g butter, powdered sugar, and grated tonka bean until light.
Add 50g flour. Mix until just combined.
Roll dough very thinly between two parchment sheets.
Bake 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp.
Cool completely. Break into irregular shards. Store airtight.
Pulse pistachios, 20g sugar, 20g flour, and a pinch of salt in a food processor until coarse crumbs form.
Add cold 20g butter. Pulse until pea-sized crumbs form. Do not overmix.
Spread on a baking sheet.
Bake at 160°C for 10-12 minutes, until golden and fragrant.
Cool completely. Store airtight.
Temper 50g dark chocolate (melt to 45-50°C, cool to 27°C, reheat to 31-32°C).
Spread a very thin layer onto an acetate sheet or parchment paper.
Allow to set partially. Cut into long, thin shards before fully set.
Allow to fully crystallize. Carefully peel off. Store in a cool, dry place.
Pipe an elegant quenelle or swirl of aerated chocolate mousse onto one side of a chilled plate.
Dot raspberry fluid gel artfully around the mousse, creating flowing streaks.
Scatter a small amount of pistachio crumble beside the mousse.
Insert one or two irregular, wafer-thin tonka bean crisps vertically into the mousse or beside it.
Insert a slender, glossy shard of chocolate glass vertically into the mousse or beside it.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna Niçoise Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain plate set on a light oak bistro table. The focal point is a thick, whole rectangular block of seared tuna, showing a thin grey seared edge and a vibrant deep pink center. Beside the tuna, two halves of a soft-boiled egg reveal jammy, translucent orange yolks. The salad consists of vibrant red cherry tomato halves, thick cucumber medallions, and delicate purple red onion rounds. The vegetables are lightly coated in a pale, creamy lemon-mayonnaise dressing. Fresh green parsley is scattered naturally across the plate. The lighting is bright and natural, coming from the side to highlight the textures of the seared fish and glossy egg yolks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices
Pair with a chilled dry Rosé from Provence
Provide a small bowl of Niçoise olives on the side
instructions: Boil water in a small pot. Add eggs and cook for 6 minutes and 30 seconds. Transfer eggs to ice water immediately. Peel and set aside.
Cut tuna loin into four thick 150g rectangular blocks.
Season tuna with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Sear tuna for 45 seconds per side until a crust forms but the center remains rare.
Slice cucumber into 2cm thick medallions. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice the red onion into rounds.
Whisk mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth.
Arrange cucumber medallions, tomatoes, and red onion on four plates.
Place one whole seared tuna block on each plate. Do not slice.
Halve the soft-boiled eggs and place next to the tuna.
Drizzle the mayonnaise dressing over the vegetables. Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure the tuna is sushi-grade for the best flavor and safety.
Dry the tuna loin thoroughly with paper towels before searing to achieve a better crust.
