Knead dough on a clean surface for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll out pasta dough very thinly, about 1 mm thick. Use a pasta machine or rolling pin.
Cut dough into wide ribbons, approximately 2-3 cm wide, to create pappardelle.
Once beef is tender, remove bay leaf and herb sprigs from ragu. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add fresh pappardelle to boiling water. Cook for 2-4 minutes until al dente. Fresh pasta cooks quickly.
Drain pasta, reserving some pasta water.
Add cooked pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Serve immediately. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: This recipe champions sustainability by utilizing fermented tomatoes, which extend shelf life and add complex umami. Beef cheek is a less common, flavorful cut that benefits from slow cooking, minimizing waste.

To prepare fermented tomatoes: Slice 500g ripe tomatoes. Weigh them and add 2% of their weight in non-iodized salt. Massage gently. Pack tightly into a clean jar. Ensure tomatoes are submerged in their own liquid (or add a little 2% brine if needed). Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Store in the refrigerator once fermented.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Mediterranean Chicken and Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks are nestled among rustic potato wedges, vibrant red and yellow bell pepper strips, and bright orange carrot rounds. The ingredients are coated in a rich, savory tomato-based broth, infused with smoked paprika and herbs. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The stew has a comforting, rustic yet refined appearance, showcasing distinct shapes and colors. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, with a silver fork and spoon, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting warmth and inviting textures. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the broth.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Cut potatoes into 3 cm wedges. Cut carrots into 1 cm thick rounds. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm strips.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks in batches. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, smoked paprika, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot. Add potatoes and carrots.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add bell peppers. Continue simmering, uncovered, for another 10-15 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender. Stir occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley for garnish.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Paprika Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: The Spanish Braised Chicken with Paprika Vegetables is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A single, golden-brown braised chicken thigh, with its skin crisped from initial searing, is placed prominently in the center. Surrounding the chicken are artfully arranged, rustic chunks of tender potato wedges, vibrant orange carrot rounds, and rich red and yellow bell pepper strips. Halved cherry tomatoes are interspersed, adding bright pops of color. All ingredients are coated in a glossy, deep reddish-orange paprika-infused braising sauce, which pools slightly at the base of the plate, reflecting the natural overhead light. The textures are varied: the slight crispness of the chicken skin, the succulence of the chicken meat, and the softness of the slow-cooked vegetables. A generous sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley provides a contrasting garnish, adding freshness and visual appeal. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard European-style flatware. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, showcasing a hearty, comforting dish with refined restaurant-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread
Simple green salad
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and bell pepper strips. Cook for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add diced tomatoes (undrained), chicken broth, potato wedges, and carrot chunks to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up, ensuring they are partially submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F) and vegetables are tender.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato Essence and Root Vegetable Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, boasting a crisp, golden-brown skin, rests atop a smooth, pale orange root vegetable puree. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, unsliced. A vibrant, deep red fermented tomato essence pools elegantly around the base of the chicken, creating a rich contrast. The plate is a handcrafted ceramic in an earthy cream tone, leaving ample negative space for a clean, minimalist composition. A few small, fresh green herb leaves (such as thyme or parsley) or microgreens are placed delicately on the chicken or puree for a natural, subtle garnish. The scene is lit by soft, natural light, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the ingredients. The background is clean and uncluttered, featuring a light reclaimed wood or stone surface, with an undyed linen napkin subtly present, emphasizing the dish's sustainable and pure aesthetic. The entire plate is visible.

ingredients.name: Seasonal root vegetables (e.g., parsnip, celeriac, carrot), peeled and roughly chopped
Chicken stock (preferably homemade from chicken bones)
Vegetable stock (preferably homemade from vegetable scraps)
For garnish: Small fresh herb leaves (e.g., thyme, parsley) or microgreens

instructions: Prepare Root Vegetable Puree: In a pot, combine chopped root vegetables with vegetable stock. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain vegetables, reserving stock. Blend hot vegetables with a splash of reserved stock until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Fermented Tomato Essence: In a saucepan, heat 10ml olive oil over medium heat. Add half the diced onion and 1 minced garlic clove. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add drained lacto-fermented tomatoes, 1 thyme sprig, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Remove thyme. Blend mixture until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Reduce strained liquid over medium-low heat until slightly thickened and intensely flavored, about 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Sear Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 20ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.

Finish Chicken: Flip chicken. Add remaining diced onion, 2 minced garlic cloves, and rosemary sprig to the pan. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Roast for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Let rest 5 minutes.

Plate: Spoon a generous dollop of warm root vegetable puree onto the center of each plate. Place one pan-seared chicken thigh on top of the puree. Carefully spoon the reduced fermented tomato essence around the chicken. Garnish with a few small fresh herb leaves or microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Peperoni Ripieni di Manzo e Riso
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Italian Stuffed Bell Peppers is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two vibrant bell pepper halves, one rich red and one bright yellow, are generously filled with a savory mixture of browned ground beef, fluffy basmati rice, finely diced carrots, and onions, all simmered in a rich tomato sauce. The top of each pepper is crowned with a golden, melted crust of Parmesan cheese, showing slight browning. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped basil leaves garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. A small pool of rustic tomato sauce from the baking process lightly coats the bottom of the plate, complementing the peppers. The dish is centrally placed, allowing for moderate negative space around it. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate, hinting at a casual yet refined dining experience. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Set aside.
Cook basmati rice according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Set aside.
Finely dice onion and carrot. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and carrot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef to the skillet. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in cooked rice, half of the Parmesan cheese, and fresh herbs.
Spoon beef and rice mixture into bell pepper halves. Fill generously.
Pour beef broth into a baking dish. Arrange stuffed peppers in the dish.
Cover baking dish with foil. Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove foil. Sprinkle remaining Parmesan cheese over peppers. Bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until peppers are tender and cheese is golden brown.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Satay Skewers with Peanut Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown seared chicken satay skewers, featuring chicken cut into small cubes, are artfully arranged on a clean white porcelain plate. The grilling imparts a tender interior and a perfectly caramelized exterior. A rich, creamy peanut sauce is elegantly drizzled over some skewers, with a small pool beside for dipping. Garnished with fresh cilantro leaves, a scattering of finely chopped roasted peanuts, and vibrant lime wedges, adding fresh color and texture. The composition highlights natural textures and appealing colors. Moderate negative space surrounds the main elements, creating a professional yet approachable presentation. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, bathed in natural, even lighting, emphasizing the vibrant hues and inviting textures of the satay, ready for a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Acar Timun (cucumber and red onion relish) for a refreshing contrast.
Offer additional lime wedges for guests to squeeze over the skewers.
Serve as a shared appetizer, allowing guests to take skewers from a central platter.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass stalk, outer layers removed, bruised, finely chopped

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2 cm cubes.
Combine 60 ml coconut milk, curry powder, turmeric, ginger, garlic, lemongrass, fish sauce, soy sauce, lime juice, and brown sugar in a bowl. Mix well.
Add chicken cubes to the marinade. Toss to coat evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Soak bamboo skewers in water for 20 minutes to prevent burning.
Thread marinated chicken cubes onto skewers, about 4-5 pieces per skewer.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large pan or grill pan over medium-high heat. Alternatively, preheat a grill.
Cook chicken skewers for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C.
For the peanut sauce: Heat remaining 15 ml vegetable oil in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add chopped shallot and cook until softened, about 2 minutes.
Stir in roasted peanuts, remaining 60 ml coconut milk, tamarind paste, and red chili (if using). Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and a pinch more brown sugar or lime juice if needed.
Serve chicken satay skewers immediately with peanut sauce, garnished with fresh cilantro and lime wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
For a spicier peanut sauce, add more fresh chili or a pinch of cayenne pepper.
Marinating chicken longer enhances flavor and tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet au Vin Rouge
recipes.visual_description: A single, plump, bone-in chicken thigh is centered on a round white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken skin is deeply browned and slightly crispy from searing, contrasting with the tender, succulent meat beneath. A rich, glossy, dark red-brown wine sauce generously pools around the chicken, studded with tender, whole pearl onions and vibrant orange carrot rounds. Glossy, golden-brown quartered cremini mushrooms are nestled within the sauce and around the chicken. A small sprig of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley is delicately placed on top of the chicken for a pop of color and freshness. The plate is clean, with moderate negative space, showcasing the dish as the focal point. The setting is a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin positioned to the side. Traditional silver flatware is arranged beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant-style presentation. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy mashed potatoes or crusty baguette to soak up the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Carrots, peeled and cut into 2 cm rounds
Dry red wine (e.g., Pinot Noir or Burgundy)

instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Add bacon lardons. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Add chicken pieces to the hot pot, skin-side down. Sear until deeply golden brown on all sides. This may require working in batches. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Drain most of the fat, leaving about 15 ml in the pot. Add pearl onions and carrot rounds. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Cook for 1 minute, stirring to coat.
Gradually pour in red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Return chicken pieces and cooked bacon to the pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken braises, melt butter in a separate pan over medium heat. Add quartered cremini mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender.
Remove chicken and vegetables from the pot. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Skim any excess fat from the sauce.
Reduce sauce over medium-high heat until slightly thickened, if desired. Stir in sautéed mushrooms.
Return chicken and vegetables to the sauce. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality dry red wine that you would enjoy drinking.
This dish can be prepared a day in advance and reheated; flavors often improve overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken & Fermented Tomato Ragu
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Slow-Cooked Chicken & Fermented Tomato Ragu is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The rich, rustic ragu fills the center, featuring tender, irregular chunks of slow-cooked chicken, vibrant, roughly chopped fermented tomatoes, and whole, plump chickpeas. The sauce is thick and earthy red, with a natural, slightly chunky consistency. Fresh, bright green parsley leaves provide a simple garnish. The plating is natural and unforced, with ample negative space. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of lush green foliage, suggesting sustainability.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, skinless, cut into 3cm chunks
Onion peels and root ends (for broth)

instructions: To ferment tomatoes: Place roughly chopped tomatoes in a clean jar. Add 1.5% salt by weight of tomatoes (e.g., 12g salt for 800g tomatoes). Press down to submerge tomatoes in their own liquid. If needed, add a little water to cover. Cover jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Refrigerate once desired tanginess is achieved.
Prepare onion broth: Combine onion peels and root ends with 500ml water in a small saucepan. Simmer gently for 20 minutes. Strain, discard solids. Set broth aside.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in fermented tomatoes, including their liquid. Add dried oregano and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add onion broth. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. If not, add a little water.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Stir in drained chickpeas. Cook for 5 minutes to heat through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Remove bay leaf before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: For enhanced zero-waste, use chicken bones or trimmings to enrich the onion broth.
Fermentation time for tomatoes can vary based on temperature and desired tanginess; taste daily.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Rice and Halloumi Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mediterranean rice and halloumi salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The base is a generous mound of fluffy, cooled white rice, lightly tossed with a colorful medley of diced red tomatoes, bright green cucumber chunks, dark purple Kalamata olives, and golden-yellow corn kernels. Freshly chopped green parsley and mint are visibly mixed throughout. Nestled atop the rice salad are several golden-brown, seared halloumi cheese slices, their surfaces showing appealing grill marks. A small amount of mixed salad greens is lightly interspersed. Dominant colors are the creamy white of the rice, the rich reds of tomatoes, the deep greens of cucumber and herbs, the dark purples of olives, and the golden-brown of the halloumi. Contrasting textures include tender rice, crisp cucumber, juicy tomatoes, firm olives, slightly charred corn, and chewy halloumi. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and traditional Mediterranean flatware are beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the freshness.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or crusty rustic bread for scooping.
Offer a side of tzatziki or hummus.
Serve chilled for a refreshing summer meal.
instructions: Rinse rice. Cook in 600ml salted water according to package directions. Fluff with a fork. Let cool completely.
Dice cucumber and tomatoes. Halve olives. Finely dice red onion. Chop parsley and mint.
If using fresh corn, grill or pan-fry kernels until slightly charred. If using frozen, sauté until tender. Let cool.
Cut halloumi into 1.5 cm thick slices. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook halloumi slices 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and slightly crisp. Set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooled rice, cucumber, tomatoes, olives, corn, red onion, parsley, and mint. Pour dressing over the mixture. Toss gently to combine.
Divide salad among four plates. Arrange grilled halloumi slices on top of each salad portion. Serve immediately with crusty bread or pita bread on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Bean and Corn Enchiladas with Roasted Tomato Roja Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents two whole, golden-brown corn enchiladas, generously bathed in a rich, rustic roasted tomato roja sauce. The sauce, a deep reddish-brown, exhibits flecks of roasted tomato and onion. Each enchilada is plump with a savory black bean and corn filling, visible at the ends. The filling consists of tender black beans, vibrant yellow corn kernels, and finely diced sautéed white onion. A delicate sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh cilantro adorns the top, alongside a small dollop of creamy white Mexican crema. The enchiladas rest on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, leaving moderate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin and traditional flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and authentic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Mexican rice.
Offer additional lime wedges for squeezing.
Provide extra Mexican crema or sour cream on the side.

ingredients.name: Monterey Jack or Oaxaca cheese, shredded

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve tomatoes. Quarter one onion. Peel garlic cloves. Place tomatoes, onion, and garlic on a baking tray. Drizzle with 15 ml oil. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly charred.

Transfer roasted vegetables to a blender. Add 10 g chili powder, cumin, oregano, and vegetable broth. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Pour sauce into a saucepan and simmer gently for 10 minutes. Keep warm.
Dice remaining onion. Heat remaining 15 ml oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Drain and rinse black beans. Add beans and corn kernels to the skillet with the onion. Add remaining 5 g chili powder. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper.
Warm corn tortillas. You can microwave them briefly or dip quickly in warm oil. This makes them pliable.
Spoon a portion of the bean and corn filling onto each tortilla. Roll tightly. Place seam-side down in a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Pour the warm roja sauce evenly over the rolled enchiladas. Sprinkle shredded cheese generously over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and sauce is heated through.
Remove from oven. Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro. Serve immediately with a dollop of Mexican crema and lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Tomato Braise
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared chicken thigh, its skin a rich golden-brown and visibly crisp, rests centrally on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm, natural beige tone. The chicken is nestled amongst a vibrant, rustic braise of tender, deep red fermented tomato chunks and glistening, amber caramelized onion slices. The tomatoes display varying shades of red, from bright to muted, indicating their fermentation. A light, savory braising liquid, slightly thickened, pools around the chicken and vegetables, reflecting subtle natural light. A few fresh thyme sprigs, vibrant green, are thoughtfully placed for a pop of color and natural texture. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced. The plate features ample white space, emphasizing the dish's natural beauty and minimalist aesthetic. The setting is an eco-conscious light bamboo table. An undyed linen napkin and simple, matte ceramic utensils complete the clean, organic presentation under soft natural lighting.
instructions: PREP FERMENTED TOMATOES (5-7 days prior): Wash 500g ripe tomatoes. Quarter them. Pack tightly into a clean 1-liter jar. Dissolve 20g sea salt in 1 liter filtered water to create a 2% brine. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if available. Seal jar loosely. Allow to ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days, or until tangy and slightly effervescent. Burp daily. Refrigerate once desired tanginess is achieved.

PREPARE CHICKEN & STOCK: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper. Reserve any chicken bones or trimmings for stock. In a large pot, combine reserved chicken bones/trimmings, onion skins, tomato cores, and 1 liter water. Simmer gently for 1 hour to create a zero-waste chicken stock. Strain and set aside 250ml.

CARAMELIZE ONIONS: Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-30 minutes until deeply golden brown and sweet. Remove caramelized onions from pot and set aside.

SEAR CHICKEN: Increase heat to medium-high. Add remaining 15ml olive oil. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot pot. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pot.

BUILD BRAISE: Add minced garlic and diced fresh tomatoes to the pot. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant. Drain the lacto-fermented tomatoes, reserving their brine. Add the fermented tomatoes, reserved chicken stock, thyme, and rosemary to the pot. Bring to a simmer.

BRAISE CHICKEN: Return seared chicken thighs and caramelized onions to the pot. Ensure chicken is partially submerged. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

FINISH SAUCE: Remove chicken and herbs from the pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Reduce the braising liquid until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed. A splash of the reserved tomato brine can be added for extra tang.
SERVE: Place a chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon generous amounts of the reduced sauce, caramelized onions, and fermented tomatoes over and around the chicken.
notes: The lacto-fermented tomatoes add a complex, tangy depth to the braise, enhancing flavor naturally. Adjust fermentation time to desired tanginess.
This recipe utilizes chicken bones, onion skins, and tomato cores for a zero-waste chicken stock, maximizing flavor and minimizing food waste.
The reserved tomato brine can be used in dressings or other culinary applications to further reduce waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken and Turkey Medallions with Tomato-Basil Essence
recipes.visual_description: A single serving is meticulously presented on a large, pristine white bone china plate, allowing for abundant negative space. The plate rests on a smooth, cool white Carrara marble surface. Two thick, perfectly seared chicken medallions and two thick turkey medallions, displaying a deep golden-brown crust from precise searing, are artfully arranged slightly to one side. Their interiors are moist and tender. Beside the poultry, a small, delicate coil of pale yellow fine egg noodles forms a refined textural contrast. A small, vibrant crimson pool of the concentrated tomato-basil essence is strategically placed to complement the proteins, its smooth, rich surface reflecting light. The entire composition is accented by a few tiny, bright green micro basil leaves scattered delicately over the poultry or a single, perfectly formed basil leaf placed thoughtfully. The lighting is dramatic and professional, creating soft shadows that enhance the dish's three-dimensionality. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a sharp triangle, is placed elegantly beside the plate. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish remains the sole focus of the image, showcasing sophisticated simplicity and masterful execution.

ingredients.name: Micro basil or small basil leaves

instructions: Quarter tomatoes. Mince 1 garlic clove. Heat 10ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add minced garlic, cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add tomatoes, 50ml chicken stock, and a pinch of salt. Simmer 15 minutes, crushing tomatoes. Stir in 10g chopped basil. Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Return liquid to clean saucepan. Reduce over medium-low heat until slightly thickened and intensely flavored, about 10 minutes. Stir in Worcestershire sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add fine egg noodles. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain immediately. Toss lightly with 5ml olive oil to prevent sticking. Form into small, delicate nests or coils. Keep warm.

Pat chicken breasts and turkey tenderloin dry with paper towels. Cut each chicken breast horizontally into two thick medallions. Cut turkey tenderloin into 8-10 thick medallions (approx. 2.5cm thick). Season all poultry medallions generously with salt and black pepper.

Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Once butter is melted and sizzling, add poultry medallions in a single layer, without crowding the pan. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until deep golden-brown crust forms. Sear turkey 3-4 minutes per side until deep golden-brown. Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and chili flakes to pan. Baste poultry with pan juices and melted butter for 1 minute. Transfer poultry to a wire rack set over a baking sheet. Finish in a preheated oven at 180°C for 5-7 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest poultry 5 minutes before plating.

Place a small, delicate noodle nest slightly off-center on each large white plate. Arrange 2-3 poultry medallions artfully beside the noodle nest. Spoon a small pool of the warm tomato-basil essence next to the poultry. Garnish with micro basil leaves or a single small basil leaf. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken and turkey reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The tomato essence should be intensely flavored; reduce until it coats the back of a spoon lightly.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Turkey Ragu with Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous portion of tagliatelle pasta thoroughly coated in a rich, savory ragu. The ragu features tender, shredded chicken chunks and finely crumbled ground turkey, both simmered until deeply flavorful. The sauce is a vibrant, rustic red from the crushed tomatoes, flecked with darker bits of caramelized meat and bright green slivers of fresh basil. Visible strands of al dente tagliatelle are intertwined throughout the ragu, creating a natural, flowing mound. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green basil leaves adorns the top, providing a fresh aromatic contrast. The texture is moist and inviting, with the pasta glistening from the sauce. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The table setting includes a simple wooden surface, a white cotton napkin, and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add ground turkey to the pot. Break it up with a spoon. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add minced garlic and chili flakes to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and chicken broth.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 45 minutes.
Remove chicken from pot. Shred chicken using two forks.
Return shredded chicken to the ragu. Stir well. Continue to simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, cook tagliatelle according to package instructions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to combine thoroughly.
Stir in most of the fresh basil leaves.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Adjust chili flakes to your preferred spice level.
For deeper flavor, brown chicken and turkey well before adding liquids.
Using boneless, skinless chicken thighs ensures tender meat that shreds easily.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Pork with Fermented Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-cooked pork with fermented tomato sauce is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone, centered on a light, reclaimed wood table. Large, rustic chunks of tender, braised pork, rich brown in color, are nestled within a vibrant, deep red fermented tomato sauce. The sauce has a slightly rustic, chunky texture, with visible pieces of softened tomato and diced vegetables like carrots and celery. Dark green, wilted seasonal greens are integrated into the dish, adding a contrasting color and soft texture. A light scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top. The plating is minimalistic and natural, emphasizing the inherent beauty of the ingredients with ample white space on the plate. The background is clean and unfussy, with subtle hints of natural elements or potted plants, creating an eco-conscious atmosphere. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its earthy colors and comforting textures. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is loosely draped beside the plate. No utensils are present on the plate, maintaining a pure focus on the food.

ingredients.name: Seasonal greens (e.g., kale, spinach), roughly chopped

instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 4-5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks in batches until well browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove pork and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in lacto-fermented tomatoes and their liquid. Stir to combine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return pork chunks to the pot. Add vegetable stock and bay leaves. Ensure pork is mostly submerged. Add more stock if needed.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2-2.5 hours, or until pork is very tender. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Stir in seasonal greens during the last 10 minutes of cooking until wilted.
Remove bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Fried Soy-Garlic Chicken with Caramelized Onions and Beet-Grapefruit Salad
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-fried chicken cutlet, cooked to a crisp exterior, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is a whole, tender piece, not sliced. A neat pile of glistening, deeply caramelized thin-sliced onions sits atop one end of the chicken. Beside the chicken, a vibrant mound of fresh beet-grapefruit salad is artfully arranged. The salad features diced, rich purple beets and bright, juicy pink grapefruit segments, lightly coated in a creamy, off-white dressing and sprinkled with crumbled white feta cheese. The colors on the plate are balanced and natural: the warm golden chicken, translucent amber onions, vivid red-purple beets, and cheerful pink grapefruit. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Pound chicken breasts to 1.5 cm thickness. Season chicken with salt, pepper, minced garlic, soy sauce, and sugar.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft. Remove from pan.
Place flour on a shallow plate. Dredge each chicken breast in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat 30ml olive oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Pan-fry for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Cook in batches if necessary.
While chicken cooks, prepare salad dressing. In a small bowl, whisk mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper.
In a medium bowl, combine diced beets and grapefruit segments. Gently fold in the dressing. Add crumbled feta cheese.
Plate each chicken cutlet. Top with a spoonful of caramelized onions. Place a generous portion of beet-grapefruit salad alongside.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Northern Thai Pork Belly Curry with Pickled Green Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion of Northern Thai Pork Belly Curry is presented in a deep, handcrafted ceramic bowl with a natural, earthy glaze. Large, tender chunks of braised pork belly are nestled within a rich, reddish-brown curry sauce. Halved pickled green tomatoes add vibrant color and a contrasting texture. A small, separate mound of pristine white jasmine rice is plated alongside or on a smaller accompanying dish. The curry's surface is lightly speckled with ground peanuts and a few fresh green coriander sprigs are thoughtfully placed as a natural garnish. The setting features a light, textured bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting. The background is clean and minimalist, with a subtle hint of green foliage from a nearby plant, enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic. The composition emphasizes natural textures and colors, with ample white space around the main dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice, a staple accompaniment for Thai curries.
Offer fresh vegetables like cucumber slices or blanched green beans on the side for textural contrast.
Traditionally eaten with a spoon and fork, or chopsticks and a spoon if preferred for the rice and curry.

ingredients.name: Pork belly or shoulder, cut into 4-5cm chunks

instructions: Prepare Hung Lay Paste: In a mortar and pestle or food processor, combine rehydrated chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric powder, curry powder, white peppercorns, salt, and kapi (if using). Pound or process until a fine paste forms.
Brown Pork: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add pork chunks. Sear pork until browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Cook Paste: Reduce heat to medium. Add Hung Lay paste to the pot. Stir-fry paste for 3-5 minutes until fragrant.
Combine and Simmer: Return browned pork to the pot. Add pickled green tomatoes, roasted peanuts, tamarind paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, and water or stock. Stir to combine.
Braise Curry: Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 1.5-2 hours, or until pork is very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Adjust Seasoning: Taste and adjust seasoning with more fish sauce, palm sugar, or tamarind as needed. The curry should be a balance of savory, sweet, sour, and mildly spicy.
Serve: Ladle curry into individual serving bowls. Garnish with fresh coriander. Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
notes: For pickled green tomatoes: Combine 250g halved green tomatoes with a cooled brine of 125ml white vinegar, 125ml water, 10g salt, and 5g sugar. Refrigerate for at least 24 hours before use.
This recipe emphasizes sustainable practices by utilizing green tomatoes, which are often overlooked, and focusing on a slow-braised, flavorful main course that can be a centerpiece.
traditional_techniques: Pounding curry paste in a mortar and pestle

recipes.recipe_name: Clear Chicken & Turkey Consommé with Tomato Confit, Garlic Noodle, and Basil Essence
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china bowl holds a single portion of Clear Chicken & Turkey Consommé. The consommé is perfectly translucent, a light golden amber hue. At the center, a small, artfully arranged nest of delicate, thin garlic tagliolini noodles rests. Around the noodles, two to three vibrant red cherry tomato halves, gently confit and slightly shriveled, are precisely placed. A few drops of emerald green basil essence are artfully dotted on the consommé's surface, creating subtle color contrast. A single sprig of vivid green micro basil garnishes the dish, adding a delicate final touch. The presentation emphasizes abundant negative space, showcasing the clarity of the consommé and the precise execution of each component. The bowl sits on a polished white Carrara marble surface, accompanied by a single, folded white linen napkin and minimalist silver flatware, under dramatic, focused lighting.
instructions: Combine chicken and turkey bones, quartered onion, roughly chopped carrot, and roughly chopped celery in a large pot. Add 3 litres cold water. Bring slowly to a simmer over medium heat. Skim impurities from surface. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 4 hours. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill stock completely. Remove any solidified fat layer.

In a bowl, combine ground chicken breast, egg whites, tomato paste, bay leaf, and black peppercorns. Whisk well until combined. Add chilled stock to the chicken mixture in a clean pot. Place pot over medium-low heat. Stir constantly with a wooden spoon, scraping bottom, until a 'raft' of solids forms and floats to the surface. Stop stirring. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes. Do not boil vigorously. Carefully ladle clear consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth into a clean pot. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm.

Preheat oven to 120°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a small oven-safe dish. Add thinly sliced garlic, olive oil, thyme sprigs, pinch of salt, and black pepper. Roast for 45-60 minutes until tomatoes are tender and slightly shriveled.

Combine "00" flour, whole egg, egg yolks, garlic powder, and pinch of salt. Knead dough until smooth and elastic. Cover and rest dough for 30 minutes. Roll dough very thin using a pasta machine or rolling pin. Cut into fine tagliolini (very thin noodles). Cook noodles in a pot of salted boiling water for 1-2 minutes until al dente. Drain immediately. Toss lightly with a few drops of olive oil to prevent sticking.

Blanch fresh basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to cool. Squeeze basil leaves dry. Blend blanched basil with grapeseed oil until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for a clear basil essence.

Gently warm the confit tomatoes and garlic noodles. Place a small, artfully arranged portion of garlic noodles in the center of a warm soup bowl. Arrange 2-3 confit cherry tomato halves precisely around the noodles. Carefully ladle hot, clear consommé into the bowl, ensuring clarity. Drizzle a few drops of basil essence around the elements. Garnish with 2-3 small micro basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken, Potato, and Broccoli Bake
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rectangular portion of creamy chicken, potato, and broccoli bake is centered on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The top crust is a rich, bubbly golden-brown from the melted Cheddar cheese, with some darker caramelized edges. Beneath the cheese, tender, thinly sliced potatoes are visible, their pale yellow contrasting with vibrant green broccoli florets and succulent, lightly browned chicken chunks. Small pieces of softened, translucent onion are interspersed throughout the creamy, savory sauce that binds the ingredients. The dish presents a comforting, hearty texture with a slight crispness on top and a soft, yielding interior. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and warm colors in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad
Serve with crusty bread for dipping in sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Cut chicken breasts into 2.5 cm cubes. Peel and thinly slice potatoes 3mm thick. Cut broccoli into small florets. Dice yellow onion. Shred cheddar cheese.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear chicken until lightly browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Chicken does not need to be cooked through. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in garlic powder and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in heavy cream and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer. Season with salt and black pepper. Remove from heat.
Arrange half of the thinly sliced potatoes in an even layer in the prepared baking dish.
Layer half of the seared chicken cubes over the potatoes.
Scatter half of the broccoli florets and half of the sautéed onions over the chicken.
Pour half of the cream sauce evenly over the layers.
Sprinkle half of the shredded cheese over the sauce.
Repeat layers with remaining potatoes, chicken, broccoli, onions, cream sauce, and cheese.
Cover baking dish tightly with aluminum foil.
Bake for 40 minutes.
Remove foil. Continue baking for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender, chicken is cooked to 75°C (167°F), and cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Let stand 5-10 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for food safety.
For best results, use a mandoline to slice potatoes evenly thin.

recipes.recipe_name: Pickled Carrot & Mushroom Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a matte, earthy beige finish, resting on a light, reclaimed wood surface. Pickled carrot rounds, thinly sliced mushrooms, and delicate red onion half-moons form a vibrant, organic base. Scattered throughout are bright red cherry tomato halves and small, evenly diced pieces of tender chicken. A generous sprinkling of fresh, vibrant green dill adds a contrasting pop of color and texture. The dressing lightly coats all ingredients, creating a subtle sheen. The composition is natural and unforced, with ample negative space. A rustic, dark rye bread slice and an undyed linen napkin in a natural tone complete the eco-conscious table setting. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the fresh textures. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of green foliage.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with slices of dark rye bread.
Offer a small side of smetana (sour cream) for an authentic Russian touch.
instructions: Prepare the pickling brine: Combine water, white vinegar, sugar, salt, peppercorns, bay leaves, and smashed garlic in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
Prepare vegetables: Peel carrots. Slice carrots into thin rounds. Slice mushrooms into thin pieces. Slice red onion into thin half-moons.

Pickle vegetables: Place sliced carrots, mushrooms, and red onion into a clean, heat-proof jar or container. Pour the warm pickling brine over the vegetables. Ensure vegetables are fully submerged. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight. Reserve 30 ml of pickling brine for the dressing.
Prepare chicken: Ensure cooked chicken breast reaches 75°C internal temperature if cooking fresh. Dice the cooked chicken breast into small cubes (approximately 1 cm).
Prepare tomatoes and dill: Halve or quarter cherry tomatoes. Roughly chop fresh dill.
Make the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, Dijon mustard, reserved pickling brine, and black pepper until emulsified.
Assemble the salad: Drain the pickled vegetables. In a large mixing bowl, combine pickled carrots, mushrooms, red onion, cherry tomatoes, and diced chicken. Add chopped dill.
Dress and serve: Pour the dressing over the salad. Gently toss to combine. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes fermentation and preservation, extending the shelf life of vegetables. Consider composting any vegetable trimmings or using them to make a vegetable broth, aligning with zero-waste principles.

recipes.recipe_name: Russian Pickled & Fermented Garden Starter
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is elegantly presented on a handcrafted, light beige ceramic plate, showcasing a minimalistic and natural composition. At the base, a subtle, organic smear of creamy white bean puree provides an earthy foundation. Centered on the puree, a small, artfully arranged mound of mixed pickled vegetables creates a vibrant focal point. This includes glossy, dark brown pickled mushroom halves, bright orange julienned pickled carrots, and delicate, vibrant purple-pink thin slices of pickled red onion. Nestled amongst these are deep red, slightly softened wedges of pre-fermented cherry tomatoes, alongside golden-brown, irregularly cut chunks of pan-seared chicken. Small, golden-crisp roasted potato cubes are scattered throughout the medley, adding texture. The dish is garnished simply with fresh, verdant dill sprigs and tiny parsley leaves, providing a pop of green. The entire arrangement is topped with airy, golden-brown crispy rice bits, offering a delightful crunch. The plate, with its generous negative space, rests on a natural, light-colored reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is gently folded beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The background remains clean and unobtrusive, featuring subtle hints of natural elements like a plant, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare quick pickle brine. Combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Remove from heat.
Slice red onion thinly. Julienne carrot. Halve button mushrooms. Place each vegetable into separate small jars.
Pour hot brine over the red onion, carrot, and mushrooms. Ensure vegetables are submerged. Let cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Drain before use.
Cut potato into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, until golden and tender. Set aside.

Cut chicken breast into 2 cm irregular chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Heat a pan with olive oil over medium-high heat. Pan-sear chicken chunks for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Set aside.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Press leftover cooked rice into a thin, even layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until crispy and golden. Break into small, irregular pieces.

Prepare white bean puree. Combine cooked white beans, 1 minced garlic clove, 15ml olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper in a food processor. Blend until smooth and creamy. Add a tablespoon of water if needed for desired consistency.
In a mixing bowl, combine drained pickled mushrooms, pickled carrots, and pickled red onion. Add pre-fermented cherry tomatoes, roasted potato cubes, and pan-seared chicken chunks.
Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves, chopped dill, and chopped parsley to the vegetable mixture. Drizzle with 35ml olive oil. Toss gently to combine.

To plate, spread a small, irregular smear of white bean puree on each plate. Arrange a small mound of the pickled vegetable and chicken mixture on top of the bean puree. Sprinkle generously with crispy rice pieces. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Corn Quesadillas with Tomato-Olive Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown flour quesadilla, cut into three neat triangular wedges, is centrally arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The griddled tortilla exterior shows subtle char marks. The rich, melted cheddar cheese oozes slightly at the edges, revealing a savory interior of sautéed, thinly sliced cremini mushrooms and vibrant yellow corn kernels. The diced red onion and minced garlic are subtly integrated into the filling, adding depth. To the side, a small, round bowl holds a fresh, colorful salsa composed of finely diced red Roma tomatoes, dark sliced black olives, and bright green chopped cilantro. A lime wedge rests on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table, a light grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and warm colors, with a subtle restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fresh tomato-olive salsa.
Offer sour cream or Mexican crema for a cooling counterpoint.
A side of pickled jalapeños can add a spicy kick.
instructions: Prepare the salsa. In a medium bowl, combine finely diced Roma tomatoes, sliced black olives, half of the chopped fresh cilantro, half of the minced garlic, lime juice, and a pinch of salt. Mix well. Set aside.

Prepare the filling. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add finely diced red onion and sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add thinly sliced cremini mushrooms and remaining minced garlic. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and most liquid has evaporated.
Stir in fresh corn kernels, ground cumin, and chili powder. Cook for another 3 minutes. Season the filling with salt and black pepper to taste. Remove from heat.

Assemble quesadillas. Lay one flour tortilla flat. Sprinkle a quarter of the grated cheddar cheese evenly over one half of the tortilla. Spoon a quarter of the mushroom and corn filling over the cheese. Top with another quarter of the grated cheddar. Fold the other half of the tortilla over the filling to create a half-moon shape. Repeat for all four quesadillas.

Cook quesadillas. Heat a large, dry non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat. Place one or two assembled quesadillas in the hot skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, or until the tortilla is golden brown and crispy, and the cheese is completely melted. Press gently with a spatula.
Remove cooked quesadillas from the skillet. Cut each quesadilla into three triangular wedges.
Plate immediately with a side of the fresh tomato-olive salsa. Garnish with remaining fresh cilantro.
notes: For best results, use fresh corn kernels. If using frozen, thaw and drain well.
Ensure the skillet is not too hot to prevent burning the tortilla before the cheese melts.
Experiment with different cheese blends for varied flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Cheek with Koji-Garlic Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef cheek is presented as a substantial, glistening whole piece on a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate. The beef, deep mahogany from searing and caramelized Koji-Garlic Glaze, rests prominently. Around it, a generous and colorful medley of roasted seasonal root vegetables, cut into rustic, thick chunks, is artfully arranged. The vegetables display natural, varied hues of orange, cream, and subtle purple, with slight charring. A minimal drizzle of rich, reduced braising liquid pools around the base of the beef. The dish is garnished simply with a scattering of fresh, vibrant green herbs like parsley or chives, adding a pop of natural color. The plate is set on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the ingredients. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of natural elements or plants, maintaining focus on the food and its sustainable presentation.

ingredients.name: Seasonal root vegetables (e.g., carrots, parsnips, celeriac)
Fresh herbs for garnish (e.g., parsley, chives)

instructions: Trim beef cheeks. Reserve trimmings for stock. Pat beef dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef cheeks until deep brown on all sides. Remove beef from pan.
Add chopped leek white parts and sliced garlic cloves to the pan. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Deglaze the pan with mirin. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar, and beef stock. Bring the liquid to a simmer.
Return beef cheeks to the pan. Ensure liquid partially covers the beef. Cover the pot. Braise in a preheated oven at 150°C for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is very tender.
For the Koji-Garlic Glaze: Roast the whole garlic head until soft. Squeeze out the roasted garlic cloves. Blend the roasted garlic cloves with koji and a splash of the braising liquid until smooth.
Cut root vegetables into rustic, thick chunks. Steam or roast them until tender-crisp.
Once beef is tender, remove it from the braising liquid. Reduce the braising liquid by half over high heat. Strain the reduced liquid.
Brush beef cheeks generously with the Koji-Garlic Glaze. Broil briefly until the glaze is caramelized.
Plate the braised beef cheeks with the roasted root vegetables. Drizzle with the reduced braising liquid. Garnish with fresh herbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Vegetable Rice
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single serving of Spanish Chicken and Vegetable Rice is presented in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl. The base is a generous portion of golden-hued, saffron-infused medium-grain rice, cooked to a tender, slightly al dente consistency, with individual grains visible. Nestled within and atop the rice are succulent, golden-brown seared chicken thigh chunks. Diced red tomatoes, bright orange carrot pieces, and earthy brown quartered mushrooms are interspersed throughout the rice, adding bursts of color and texture. Cannellini beans are gently folded in, providing creamy contrast. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge placed on the rim of the bowl. The overall composition is abundant and inviting, showcasing a medley of colors against the golden rice. The setting features a simple wooden table, a light gray linen napkin, and a fork, with soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up juices
Offer a side of alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Work in batches if necessary. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook for 3-4 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Stir in diced tomatoes, smoked paprika, and saffron threads. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to combine.
Add rice to the skillet. Stir constantly for 1-2 minutes to lightly toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return seared chicken to the skillet, nestling it into the rice. Ensure chicken is submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the skillet tightly. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed.
Stir in rinsed cannellini beans. Cover and let rest off heat for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not stir the rice too much after adding the broth to allow for proper absorption and avoid stickiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Birra Sostenibile con Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rigatoni pasta, richly coated in a deep reddish-brown tomato and beer-braised sauce. Large, irregular chunks of tender, braised chicken are nestled among the pasta, showcasing their natural, rustic texture. A vibrant sprinkle of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese rests atop the dish. A small, artful cluster of bright green fresh basil leaves provides a pop of color. A small mound of thinly sliced, translucent pink pickled red onions is placed delicately to the side of the pasta, offering a contrasting color and texture. The pasta is naturally arranged, not mounded, allowing negative space on the plate. The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate with a slightly uneven, organic rim. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A natural beige, undyed linen napkin is folded simply beside the plate. A traditional, simple silver fork and spoon are placed to the right. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft, diffused natural light illuminating the scene from the side, highlighting the textures of the food. A subtle hint of green foliage from a potted plant is visible in the very soft-focus background, adding an organic touch.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pane casareccio) to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan at the table.
A simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar can accompany the dish.
instructions: Prepare pickled onions: Thinly slice one onion. Combine vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Pour over sliced onions. Let cool completely and set aside.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until deeply golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2-3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Return chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in sauce. Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
While chicken simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 200 ml pasta cooking water.
Remove chicken from sauce. Shred or cut into large, irregular chunks. Return chicken to sauce. Stir well.
Add cooked rigatoni to the sauce. Stir to coat. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water until desired consistency.
Serve immediately. Top each portion with grated Parmesan and a spoonful of pickled onions. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: The pickled onions provide a bright, acidic counterpoint to the rich braised chicken and utilize a zero-waste preservation technique.
Using bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs would add more depth of flavor to the sauce.
Reserve pasta water to adjust sauce consistency and help it cling to the pasta.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Apple, Mustard & Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A substantial, golden-brown braised beef chunk sits centrally on a round white porcelain plate. Its exterior shows a rich, dark crust, while the interior is visibly tender and moist. Alongside, a cluster of golden-roasted potato chunks, their skins slightly crisped, dusted with fresh rosemary. Scattered around the beef and potatoes are caramelized apple wedges and soft, translucent onion slices, adding warm color and slight sweetness. A glossy, deep amber braising liquid, reduced to a rich sauce, pools elegantly around the base of the beef, reflecting light. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. The plate rests on a simple, textured light wood table. A folded, charcoal-grey cotton napkin is positioned to the left. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting textures. The background is a gently blurred, warm-toned bistro setting, hinting at a cozy restaurant atmosphere without distraction.

ingredients.name: Firm Apples (e.g., Honeycrisp, Granny Smith)
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, cored and cut into 8 wedges each

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge beef in flour.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the pot. Add chopped onions and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute. Deglaze the pot with red wine (if using), scraping up any browned bits. Cook until wine is mostly reduced.
Stir in beef broth, Dijon mustard, grainy mustard, and 1 sprig each of rosemary and thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef chunks to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged. Cover the pot and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
While beef braises, prepare potatoes. Toss potato chunks with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, pepper, and remaining 2 sprigs of rosemary. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes in the oven during the last 45-60 minutes of beef braising, or until golden and tender. Flip halfway through.
About 20 minutes before serving, heat a separate pan over medium heat. Add apple wedges and cook until slightly softened and lightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes.

Carefully remove beef from the pot. Discard herb sprigs. Skim any excess fat from the braising liquid. Reduce sauce on stovetop over medium-high heat until slightly thickened, about 5-10 minutes. Adjust seasoning.

To plate, place one braised beef chunk centrally on each plate. Arrange roasted potato chunks and caramelized apple wedges around the beef. Spoon a generous amount of the rich braising sauce over and around the beef. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Roasted Vegetable Pasta Salad with Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The Tomato and Roasted Vegetable Pasta Salad is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its vibrant medley of colors. Tender 2 cm chicken chunks are nestled among al dente fusilli pasta. Diced 1 cm red and yellow bell peppers, sliced browned mushrooms, and softened diced onions add earthy tones and varied textures. Bright red chopped tomatoes and flecks of fresh green basil provide bursts of color and freshness. The entire salad is lightly coated in a glistening olive oil vinaigrette, ensuring all components are subtly integrated. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden kitchen table, accompanied by a simple, sturdy fork and a casually folded cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, emphasizing a comfortable, family-style meal.
instructions: Cook fusilli pasta according to package directions. Drain. Rinse with cold water to stop cooking. Set aside.
Cut chicken breast into 2 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Cook until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice onion and bell pepper into 1 cm pieces. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Add another 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion, diced bell pepper, and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Remove skillet from heat.
Chop ripe tomatoes into 1.5 cm pieces. Chop fresh basil.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooked pasta, cooked chicken, sautéed vegetables, and chopped tomatoes.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 30 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Pour dressing over the salad mixture. Add chopped fresh basil.
Toss gently to combine all ingredients. Serve immediately or chill before serving.
notes: This salad can be served warm, at room temperature, or chilled.
It makes an excellent meal prep option for lunches.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Sirloin with Apple-Mustard Pan Sauce and Roasted Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared sirloin steak, golden-brown with a savory crust, is placed slightly off-center on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The steak, presented as a thick, whole piece, glistens subtly. Beside it, a generous mound of roasted new potatoes, quartered and golden-edged, show crisp exteriors and soft interiors, flecked with chopped rosemary and roasted garlic. A rich, glossy apple-mustard pan sauce is artfully spooned over the steak, pooling slightly at its base, showcasing tender, lightly caramelized onion slices and softened apple wedges. A fresh rosemary sprig rests beside the steak as a verdant garnish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, under even, natural light, creating a refined yet approachable casual dining scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Quarter or halve new potatoes. Toss with 30ml olive oil, chopped rosemary, smashed garlic, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown.
Season sirloin steaks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear steaks for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness.
Remove steaks from skillet and rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add thinly sliced onion and cook over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Core apples and cut into 1 cm thick wedges. Add apple wedges to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly tender.
Whisk in Dijon mustard and beef broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes, reducing slightly to form a light sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning of the sauce.
Plate each sirloin steak alongside a generous portion of roasted potatoes. Spoon apple-mustard sauce over and around the steak. Garnish with a fresh rosemary sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Parmesan & Dark Beer Madeleines with Beef Tartare, Roasted Tomato Confit, and Chili Rice Crisp
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a large, matte black designer plate with a wide, abundant negative space, set upon a polished white Carrara marble surface. Dramatic, focused lighting casts elegant shadows, highlighting the textures. Two to three golden-brown, shell-shaped Parmesan and dark beer madeleines are artfully placed, their ridged surfaces catching the light. Beside each madeleine, a precise quenelle of vibrant, deep red beef tartare is meticulously positioned. The tartare is finely diced, showing distinct pieces of red bell pepper and chili, reflecting a subtle gloss. Scattered around the tartare are a few jewel-like roasted cherry tomato halves, their skins slightly wrinkled and caramelized, revealing the juicy interior. A delicate, irregular chili rice crisp, translucent and airy, stands upright or leans gracefully against the tartare, adding architectural height and a contrasting texture. The composition is restrained, showcasing flawless execution of each component, with intentional spacing and a sophisticated color palette of warm browns, deep reds, and bright whites. No garnishes beyond the core elements.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a madeleine tray.

For Madeleines: Grate 50g Parmesan. Finely mince one shallot and one garlic clove. In a bowl, whisk eggs. Add melted butter, dark beer, grated Parmesan, minced shallot, and garlic. Mix well. Sift in flour and baking powder. Fold gently until just combined. Do not overmix. Fill madeleine molds two-thirds full. Bake 12-15 minutes, until golden and puffed. Cool on a wire rack.

For Beef Tartare: Finely dice beef tenderloin into 3 mm cubes. Finely mince remaining shallot, one garlic clove, and red bell pepper. Finely mince red chili (remove seeds for less heat). In a bowl, combine beef, minced shallot, garlic, bell pepper, chili, capers, Dijon mustard, 20 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix gently to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning.

For Roasted Tomato Confit: Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a small baking dish. Add remaining garlic clove (lightly crushed), fresh thyme sprigs, 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in oven at 150°C for 25-30 minutes, until softened and slightly caramelized.

For Chili Rice Crisps: Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan to 180°C. Cut rice paper into irregular, organic shapes (approx. 5 cm). Fry rice paper pieces one at a time for 2-3 seconds until puffed and crisp. Remove and drain on paper towels. Lightly sprinkle with chili powder and salt.

To Assemble: Arrange 2-3 madeleines per person on a minimalist sharing platter or individual designer plates. Place a quenelle or small mound of beef tartare beside each madeleine. Artfully arrange a few roasted tomato confit halves around the tartare. Lean a chili rice crisp against each tartare portion. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Chicken and Mushroom Rigatoni is artfully presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a rustic, deep red tomato sauce, flecked with finely diced garlic and oregano. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks are nestled amongst the pasta, showcasing their seared exterior. Sautéed red bell pepper strips and earthy brown mushroom slices are visibly integrated, adding vibrant color and varied texture. A scattering of fresh green basil leaves and a dusting of grated Parmesan cheese provide a fresh garnish. The dish is arranged organically, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting textures, reflecting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese
Serve with a side of crusty bread
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken generously with salt and black pepper.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Dice onion. Slice bell pepper into thin strips. Mince garlic.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion, bell pepper strips, and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables soften and mushrooms are browned.
Add minced garlic, dried oregano, and dried basil. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring the sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml of pasta water.

Return cooked chicken chunks to the sauce. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Add cooked rigatoni to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water until desired consistency is reached.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh basil leaves and additional grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: Al dente tagliatelle pasta, coated in a rich, creamy, reddish-orange tomato sauce. Sautéed sliced cremini mushrooms, cooked to a golden-brown, are mixed throughout the pasta. Halved cherry tomatoes add bursts of bright red. A generous dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the top, melting slightly into the warm pasta. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the dish for a vibrant contrast. The pasta is served in a simple, deep, off-white ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used rustic wooden dining table. A standard metal fork rests casually beside the bowl. Natural, warm light highlights the comforting textures of the dish. Portions are modest and home-style.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml of pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. This is the base of your soffritto.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Sauté until mushrooms are golden brown and have released their liquid, about 8-10 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, to deepen flavors.
Stir in heavy cream and 50g of grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
